Work requirements for some Medicaid beneficiaries begin across the U.S. in January, the result of President Donald Trump's big 2025 tax cut and policy law, and a handful of Republican-led states are imposing tougher rules than the law requires.

At issue is how someone can prove they are too medically frail to work. While federal regulations say the state can take the recipient's word for it for the first year, at least six states are requiring documentation immediately. There is a continuing push in other states to follow suit eventually.

Advocates say that could create problems, especially for new applicants to the joint state-federal health insurance program for lower-income people.

“Someone may not be able to work, but they can’t see a doctor because they can’t afford it. So they’re now applying for Medicaid,” said Jennifer Tolbert, director of state health policy and data at the research organization KFF. “But Medicaid is saying you need documentation from a provider.”

As some Republican-led states take a tougher-than-required approach to implementing the federally mandated changes, Democrats in 25 states are suing and asserting that the rules are too harsh.

Some say documentary evidence is necessary to avoid fraud

The Medicaid changes are projected to save the federal government $887 billion over the next decade and result in 7.5 million fewer people with health insurance, according to the Congressional Budget Office’s 2025 estimate.

The conservative Foundation for Government Accountability has been pushing states not to make it too easy for people to avoid work requirements, saying able-bodied adults are pushing enrollment and costs higher.

Jonathan Ingram, vice president of research and policy at the group, has been encouraging states not to take a beneficiary’s word for it, a process known as self-attestation.

“Self-attestation is fraud-by-design,” he said via email. “It is a policy developed by bureaucrats to maximize enrollment at the expense of program integrity.”

Self-attestation comes under penalty of perjury, so people who lie can be subject to criminal charges — though such charges are rare.

Arkansas, Idaho, Indiana, New Hampshire, North Carolina and Ohio all have laws or policies that bar self-attestation to qualify for the work requirement exception starting next year.

Republican Missouri state Rep. Darin Chappell said he worked with the Foundation for Government Accountability to craft a proposed amendment that would have enshrined Medicaid work requirements in the state constitution. It would have required “documentary evidence” of work or reasons for exemptions, specifically prohibiting self-attestation.

The amendment passed the Missouri House but died without a vote in the Senate. Chappell plans to try again next year.

“If someone has a debilitating physical ailment — or mental ailment for that matter — something that prohibits them from working, that’s totally legitimate,” he said. “But we’re not taking anybody’s word for it. I don’t mean to shock you none, but people do tend to lie about such things.”

Most nondisabled beneficiaries under 65 already work

The new mandate applies to up to 20 million lower-income adults without children at home who are enrolled in Medicaid through an optional expansion in 40 states and the District of Columbia. The requirement does not apply in the 10 states, mostly in the South, that did not expand Medicaid.

Beneficiaries will have to work or volunteer at least 80 hours each month or be in school at least half-time to qualify, with exceptions for situations including medical frailty.

The law had said medically frail people include those who have substance use disorders, disabilities or serious medical conditions. But the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services published a rule in June that went further and was stricter than states and providers expected, saying someone’s condition must “significantly impair” their ability to work, volunteer or attend school as required for an exemption.

Currently states generally decide once a year whether Medicaid recipients still qualify for benefits. The new law will require it to happen twice for most enrollees.

States will be allowed to accept self-attestation just once each time a person enrolls starting in 2028. After that, documentation would be required at least every 12 months to verify that they still have the condition and that it still prevents them from being able to work.

The government expects states to rely increasingly on third-party data — on things such as workers’ compensation claims or prescription information — to help make determinations. For conditions that do not show up in the databases, states can require a doctor's certification, a disability award letter or other proof.

While states have been ramping up the use of this information, the work requirements are still a big change, and many will first have to spend millions of dollars improving their computer systems.

States are already struggling in some cases to make changes to the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance food program, or SNAP, that are required under Trump's law, including an expanded work requirement.

In Arizona, for example, enrollment plummeted by 55% from April 2025 to April 2026 — the biggest drop in the country — with more than 400,000 fewer people getting benefits now. Last month, the state said that was largely due to difficulties in putting in place new federal requirements that resulted in higher call volumes and additional verification.

Patient advocates worry aid will be denied to qualified people

Ingram said some of the concerns about ending self-attestation are overblown and people can get diagnoses to support their inability to work at many places, including charitable clinics and federally qualified health centers. He also noted that Medicaid allows retroactive coverage for doctor visits that happen before enrollment.

Patient advocates say it's not that simple.

“The added paperwork, the hoops you have to jump through lead to coverage loss,” said Nate Crippes, a lawyer at the Disability Law Center in Utah, where a law allows self-attestation to qualify for the work requirement exception on a provisional basis.

An added challenge is that most people in the Medicaid expansion group in his state have a mental health or substance use disorder diagnosis — or both.

“We’re choosing to make people with health conditions jump through a bunch of hurdles,” said Camille Richoux, health policy director at Arkansas Advocates for Children and Families.

It can be tricky if states decide to rely partly on patient diagnosis codes to determine whether recipients are able to work.

Lucy Dagneau, senior director of the state and local campaigns team at the American Cancer Society Cancer Action Network, said the codes do not indicate the severity of a condition. For example, some patients with a specific cancer can continue working, she said, but others who are in more advanced stages cannot.

“Our fear is by that banning self-attestation, unfortunately, the state lawmakers who pass those laws are going to have a hand in more people losing coverage in their state than would have,” she said.

____

Associated Press writers David A. Lieb in Jefferson City, Missouri, and Laura Turbay in Little Rock, Arkansas, contributed.

News.title: Carreras’ try-of-season contender helps Bath eclipse Harlequins
News.content:
And they kept playing, it was not until Richards scored in the 72nd minute that the game was decided. Still for Bath, a five-try victory away from home, felt like a decent return.

If they were to stand any chance of finding a way back into the game, Quins had to score first after the restart. They were rewarded for their attacking intent after running from a scrum deep in their half, with Murley cutting a brilliant line before Pedro Delgado drove over for his side’s third try.

Quins had the opportunity to further cut the deficit when first Sam Riley carried down the left wing and Cameron Anderson drove into the Bath 22. But as Quins looked to pick and go, Beno Obano and Guy Pepper combined to hold the ball up over the line.

It felt like a significant moment and when Riley was shown a yellow card for a high tackle on Obano moments later, the odds against a Quins comeback lengthened again. Yet there was something sticky about their resilience.

“I am really happy with the grit and the fight that they showed, particularly in the second half,” said Gilmore. “We had some massive defensive sets on our goal-line which we withstood. I reckon they were the moments last year that Bath would probably run in three tries really quickly and kick the score out, which is good.”

Bath emptied their bench, including the introduction of England flanker Pepper, but they could not pull away as expected in the final quarter, despite some impressive contributions by Tom de Glanville.

It was left to their line-out maul to score their first points of the second half, with Richards touching down to seal Harlequins’ fate. Still, there were enough promising glimpses to give Harlequins supporters hope that more encouraging days lie ahead.

News.title: Manchester City found guilty of 114 charges
News.content:
Manchester City have been found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought by the Premier League over breaches of its financial rules. It is a decision that, if upheld, would equate to one of the biggest scandals in football history.

City face a range of sanctions from a fine to points deductions and even expulsion from the Premier League. Or a combination of all, under rule W51 of its handbook. No punishment has yet been announced.

If the verdict is upheld, with City expected to appeal, it will also raise question marks over the 20 trophies the club have won under Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, whose Abu Dhabi group took over in 2008.

The charges can be broken down into five categories and relate to a period from 2009-23 in which City won six League Cups, three FA Cups, seven league titles and the Champions League. There is the provision for removing past titles, but that would appear remote.

Of the 115 charges:

Fifty-four were for failing to provide accurate financial information from 2009-10 to 2017-18

Fourteen were for failing to provide accurate details for player and manager payments from the same period

Five were for failing to comply with Uefa’s rules from 2013-14 to 2017-18

Seven were for breaching Premier League profitability and sustainability rules from 2015-16 to 2017-18

Thirty-five were for failing to co-operate with the investigation from 2018-23.

City have been the dominant force in English football for most of that time, but that status is under threat with a verdict that will send shockwaves around Europe and could have huge ramifications for the club.

That is unless they can win an appeal, with sources cautioning it still may take up to another two to three years for the case to be resolved, following on from an already five-year investigation.

Case is far from being resolved

The Premier League’s rules provide for an independent appeal board with broad powers, including the ability to uphold, vary or overturn the independent commission’s decision.

It would therefore appear that despite the verdict, the case is far from being resolved and punishment decided. The details of the commission’s findings, when published, will be crucial to determining what happens next.

But if it is upheld, the verdict also opens up the possibility of City facing legal action from other clubs who feel they missed out on trophies and even merit money from league placings.

It is understood Premier League clubs are already discussing legal action and possible compensation claims as a result of the guilty verdict.

News.title: This quiet Dyson fan proved itself during a heatwave
News.content:
What is the Dyson Purifier Cool PC1?

The Dyson Purifier Cool PC1 is one of the brand’s more straightforward fans. There’s no humidifying or heating here, just a focus on cooling and air purification.

True to Dyson’s design ethos, the Purifier Cool PC1 is bladeless, which makes it safe around kids and pets, and easy to clean. The tower fan uses the company’s renowned technology to project a smooth stream of air, with 10 speed settings and a 350-degree oscillation range that circulates air evenly throughout the room. It’s relatively compact and lightweight, too.

The remote control magnetically attaches to the top of the fan but you can also control the device using the MyDyson companion app.

While it doesn’t offer all the extras of Dyson’s more expensive air purifiers, it’s a solid option if you want reliable cooling without any fuss, which is why it’s our Best Buy Dyson fan.

JUMP TO:

I’ve been testing the Dyson Purifier Cool PC1 in my home office, a small-to-medium-sized room that felt more like a sauna than a workplace during the recent heatwaves. While I wasn’t precisely measuring its air purification qualities (you can find that review on our best Dyson fan round-up), the windows open onto a main road so I was able to test out its ability to handle a steady stream of traffic fumes, dust and general pollution drifting in.

I used the fan over several weeks to see how it performs on a day-to-day basis, assessing all of the usual metrics: how well it cools the room, how quiet it is during use, how intuitive the controls are and whether the design fits into a regular living or working space. And finally, as Dyson is known for its premium pricing, is the Purifier Cool PC1 worth the outlay?

News.title: Britain sends team to South Sudan as country braces for Ebola
News.content:
British Ebola specialists have been deployed to South Sudan because of fears the haemorrhagic fever will spread from neighbouring Congo.

A rare form of Ebola, known as the Bundibugyo species, is spreading rapidly in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), where more than 7,800 people have caught the virus since May, 3,700 of whom have died.

To prepare for the threat of imported cases, Britain has positioned three experts in and around the South Sudanese capital, Juba. They will assist and train local authorities on infection control, set up awareness campaigns for local communities, and test people crossing the border for the virus.

The team is employed by the UK Health Security Agency’s (UKHSA) Public Health Rapid Support Team (PHRST), which is regularly sent to the epicentre of disease outbreaks overseas – for instant the cruise ship at the centre of a deadly hantavirus in the South Atlantic earlier this year.

The current Ebola outbreak is the fastest-growing ever recorded and is on course to become the largest in history, overtaking the 2014-16 West Africa Ebola outbreak, in which around 30,000 people contracted the haemorrhagic fever and roughly a third died.

Experts fear it is only a matter of time before the virus spreads to South Sudan, which shares a 500-mile border with the DRC. Thousands of people cross the frontier each day to work, attend school and trade goods, mostly fish, in lucrative markets between the two countries.

If the virus gained a foothold in South Sudan, which became the newest country on earth after severing ties with Khartoum in 2011, experts fear the consequences would be catastrophic and worsen an already dire humanitarian situation.

“It’s so variable as to where the outbreak is spreading at the moment, there are cases from some of the border towns [with South Sudan],” Ed Newman, director of the PHRST, told The Telegraph.

“There’s a feeling [Ebola could spread] any day. Maybe you could say we’ve been lucky so far,” Mr Newman said, on the sidelines of a UKHSA conference in Manchester.

News.title: Russell capitalises on Antonelli error to take Azerbaijan GP pole
News.content:
Russell – who begins the weekend 81 points behind the Italian – simply has to capitalise. And he really should do. Even if Antonelli hadn’t crashed out, he has looked on a different level this weekend, dominating practice and qualifying. Russell topped Q1, Q3 and Q3, securing the 12th pole of his career with a lap which was nine tenths quicker than his best lap in Q2 and eight tenths quicker than Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc, the next fastest driver. He could hardly believe it himself.

“That was a pretty decent lap,” he told his team over the radio on his cooldown lap. “How much was [the gap]?”

“Just over eight tenths to Leclerc.” came the response. “Woah!”

This has not been the easiest season for Russell, who began the year the overwhelming favourite for the title, having dominated his younger team-mate over the course of last season. So he could be forgiven for feeling proud of having done such a good job.

“It’s been a while so it definitely feels good,” he admitted. “This was probably the biggest pole margin of my whole career, including my F2 and F3 days.

“The lap felt really sweet, car’s been feeling really great this weekend. On a track like this where you can hug it, it feels amazing.”

News.title: Buttler injury derails England chase and sends Sri Lanka series to decider
News.content:
Enter Buttler to play a wonderful counter-attack, whacking Wellalage for four and six and dumping leg-spinner Sachindu Colombage over the rope twice as he raced to 41 off 22 balls.

Buttler was at a crossroads after the T20 World Cup in February. Despite England making the semi-finals, he averaged just 10 in the tournament to complete a third poor World Cup in a row. A break with his family, and a very good Indian Premier League, where he made a crucial technical correction, changed his fortunes.

Matthew Hayden, the batting coach at the Gujarat Titans, asked him whether he was watching the ball closely enough. Buttler discovered that, now 36, he is a right-eye dominant batsman, so with Hayden’s help he opened up his stance to give himself a better view of the ball. A summer rich in runs has followed with an average of 51 for England and a strut back in his body language. The injury has surely ended Buttler’s summer and there are worries that he could be out of the Pakistan ODI triangular tournament next month as well, just to add to the night’s woes.

This was not a vintage England performance. Atkinson made a crucial error on the boundary, dropping a straightforward chance off Kusal Mendis on 17. It kickstarted Mendis, who went on the charge smashing 51 in 24 balls. He put on 137 in 120 balls with Kuminda Mendis. Josh Tongue had an off day going at seven an over and Jofra Archer was given similar treatment, although he bowled better than figures suggest, as anything wayward with pace on the ball was hit away.

Overton was more effective with his cutters and slower balls, while Ahmed did at least bag a couple of wickets, credit for keeping his head after some early rough treatment. Kusal Mendis was given out leg before on 99 but overturned the decision and stroked a four next ball for a deserved hundred.

News.title: Oil jumps after Saudi thwarts missile attack
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. A global rout in bond markets deepened overnight as traders expect the US to keep raising interest rates.

Japan’s 10-year bond yield surged to 3.08pc on Thursday, its highest level since 1996, as markets responded to stronger than expected US economic data and higher oil prices.

It followed sharp rises in the US on Wednesday, when the yield on 10-year Treasuries – a benchmark of global borrowing costs – surged as high as 5.12pc, up from 4.96pc. It was the biggest jump since the “liberation day” tariff turmoil in April last year.

Bonds were sent into turmoil as traders bet that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates three times by April next year in an effort to bring down inflation. Money markets suggest there is a 70pc chance of the Fed following this month’s first rate rise in three years with a second in October.

This followed closely watched industry data on Wednesday, known as PMIs, showed US private sector activity jumped unexpectedly to a five-year high in September.

Meanwhile, oil prices spiked 3.9pc on Wednesday to move back above $100 a barrel, risking an inflationary spiral in the world economy.

Jim Reid, an analyst at Deutsche Bank, said: “The main driver was a strong batch of PMIs, along with a rebound in oil prices, which both led to mounting speculation about faster rate hikes.” Here is what you need to know.

5 things to start your day

1) US borrowing costs hit highest since 2007 on fears economy overheating | Yield on 10-year Treasuries soars amid inflation concerns as oil prices rise

2) Diesel prices surge as Trump mulls 90-day US export ban | Pump prices could exceed £3 per litre in Britain if Washington imposes ‘catastrophic’ block on exports

3) England’s first new reservoir in 30 years delayed despite drought warnings | Havant Thicket, in Hampshire, will now be completed in 2034, five years after initially planned

4) Timpson customers ask for extra belt holes after weight-loss jabs | Boss of key cutting chain credits Ozempic and Mounjaro after surge in requests

5) Chinese carmaker’s new EV battery will charge in under five minutes | Geely says its latest system is fastest in industry as brands approach ‘physical limit’

What happened overnight

Debt markets were in turmoil after Japanese bond yields hit 30-year highs.

As Tokyo markets reopened after a three-day holiday, the benchmark 10-year Japanese government bond yield jumped to its highest level since 1996.

This came after a steep sell-off in the US market overnight. Oil prices remained around $103 a barrel and the dollar held gains after Tehran’s leader vowed to never surrender following a warning by Donald Trump that he could “annihilate” Iran.

Japan’s benchmark stock market, the Nikkei 225 rose 1pc to 65,645.10, as some chipmakers got a boost from the recent interest in AI. Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 fell 0.7pc to 8,702.00.

Hong Kong’s Hang Seng lost 0.3pc to 24,762.39, while the Shanghai Composite dipped 0.9pc to 4,545.09. Trading was closed in South Korea for the Chuseok autumn harvest holiday.

News.title: Zelensky lashes out at EU
News.content:
Volodymyr Zelensky lashed out at the European Union over its moves to weaken sanctions on Russian oligarchs.

In his address to the UN General Assembly, the Ukrainian leader warned that beyond making life “more comfortable” for Russians, “it also gives the war more time for Putin to send poor people into the kill zone. So Russia’s revenues must remain a target.”

His criticism came after France and Luxembourg successfully pushed for sanctions exemptions for Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman, Russian oligarchs, on Tuesday.

Kyiv branded the decision “shameful and unjustifiable”. The men are known to share close ties to Vladimir Putin and have net worths of $14bn and $16bn, respectively.

In his fourth address to the UN as a wartime leader, Mr Zelensky said it was paramount that the international community increased pressure on the Kremlin to stop “the madness” of the war spreading.

Under pressure from Donald Trump to halt attacks on Russian energy targets, Mr Zelensky defended his country’s aerial offensive for successfully depriving Putin of revenue for his war.

“When someone gives Russia more money through trade, they give this war more time. And that is exactly why we insist on limiting trade with the aggressor, and why we are burning Russia’s revenues ourselves,” he said.

‘End the war before winter’

Washington has recently attempted to revive the long-stalled negotiations between Ukraine and Russia. On Tuesday, Mr Zelensky implored Mr Trump to help Kyiv end the war “before winter”.

Mr Trump appeared optimistic, suggesting an agreement would happen “more quickly than people understand”.

Sergei Lavrov, the Russian foreign minister, told the UN Security Council on Wednesday that Russia was prepared to negotiate for a lasting peace but would not “pause the war”.

Mr Zelensky sought to remind world leaders that the conflict was not constrained within Ukraine’s borders at a time when the global community was distracted by a myriad of conflicts and crises.

Citing the support of Iran and North Korea for Russia, he warned that Putin’s war kept “spreading further”.

“Putin is always looking for someone who can help him kill more, kill more people for every kilometre of land, take more territory and take another country instead of simply stopping and running his own country,” Mr Zelensky said at the UN.

He noted that fighters from at least 47 countries were helping to prosecute Moscow’s war against Ukraine and urged leaders to prevent their citizens from being dragged into the conflict.

After Mr Zelensky’s address, reports emerged that Kirill Dmitriev, Putin’s envoy, was on his way to the US where he would meet Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, the Trump administration representatives.

Sources told Reuters that the meeting would take place in New ‌York on the sidelines of the UN summit.

Marco Rubio, the US secretary of state, also confirmed Mr Trump had invited his Russian counterpart to attend the G20 summit of world leaders in Miami in December.

Sports.title: ‘I know what I saw’ – ‘Sad’ Noel Gallagher reveals shock at Man City verdict and admits it will ‘taint’ title wins
Sports.content:
Next

NOEL GALLAGHER has revealed his shock at Manchester City being found guilty of 114 out of the 115 charges levelled at them by the Premier League.

But the Oasis superstar and City megafan does NOT believe that these verdicts taint moments like Sergio Aguero‘s dramatic title-winning goal in 2012.



On Friday it emerged that City are set to be found guilty of almost every charge levelled at them following an investigation dating back several years.

The sanctions have not yet been decided, although severe consequences could include points deductions, fines and even EXPULSION from the league – although City are set to appeal.



Following City’s shattering news, Gallagher appeared on the Let Me Talk podcast to share his feelings on the matter.

Giving his initial reaction, Gallagher, 59, said: “(I was) A little surprised when I heard it on the radio, surprised only as the club has assured us all along that they vehemently denied any of these charges.

“So it was a bit of a shock to find out that we’ve been found guilty of all but one.

“But really, overall quite sad, really. sad for the fans and the players.”

Gallagher was then asked if the verdict makes him feel differently about his club’s achievements, including their dramatic title win in 2012, which was snatched from Manchester United‘s grasp courtesy of a last-gasp winner by Sergio Aguero.

Gallagher added: “Our focus as fans is always on the pitch, and we know what we saw, we know what we saw – they won it on the pitch.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

“Whatever goes on in the boardrooms, it’s nothing to do with the supporters or the players.

“The players won that game and won that title on the pitch.

“Whether some of those players should have been there or not, that’s nothing to do with the fans.

“We were there, we know what we saw. Does it taint it? I suppose in the eyes of everyone else in England it would.



“But I know what I saw, and I know what I felt.”

The charges levelled at City are for alleged rule breaches between 2009 and 2018.

During this period, they won three Premier League titles, the FA Cup twice, the League Cup four times and the Community Shield.

They won the title in 2011/12, 2013/14 and 2017/18. Manchester United were runners up in the first and last of those title wins, while Liverpool came second in 2013/14.

Those clubs could potentially be handed the title for those years, meaning Steven Gerrard would win a title and Sir Alex Ferguson could add one more to his packed cabinet and then-United boss Jose Mourinho would add to the titles he won at Chelsea.



It’s understood that a points deduction from when the decision is made is more likely.

A City spokesperson told The Athletic on Friday: “The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality.

“As such Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the club’s statement of February 2023.

“The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis the Premier League board and executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair minded regulator, free from partisan influence.”

Sports.title: Cole Palmer’s girlfriend nearly spills out of dress and stuns in bikini on holiday after his controversial England exit
Sports.content:
Next

OLIVIA HOLDER has posted several snaps of herself on holiday in the Caribbean.

Cole Palmer‘s stunning girlfriend, 24, jetted off to the Dominican Republic after her man withdrew from England duty.



While away, Olivia has been enjoying some sunshine by the sea.

In her latest Instagram post, the model shared plenty of pictures of herself relaxing in her bikini.



Olivia wrote: “pucci prints on”.

The social media star boasts more than 30,000 Instagram followers.

And her post swiftly received more than 1,000 likes, in addition to several gushing comments.

One fan wrote: “You really are the bestttt”.



While a second called her: “Pucci princess”.

A third swooned: “Okay insane”.

And another added: “She perfecttt”.



Chelsea star Palmer, 24, was initially recalled to Thomas Tuchel‘s England squad after being snubbed for the World Cup.

The Stamford Bridge hero subsequently withdrew, however, to the frustration of his national team boss.

Ahead of tonight’s Wembley clash with Spain, Tuchel said: “It is another missed opportunity. He misses too many opportunities and I don’t blame him for it. It is just a fact. He misses way too many camps with injuries.

“I only want to rely on what I personally witness and what I see within my team. For that you have to be in camp.

“If you are not in camp, there is a next level to impress that you cannot achieve. You can only leave when you are actually with me on the pitch and with us on the pitch So, yes it is a missed opportunity.



“My understanding is that he faces discomfort and pain and he cannot compete on the highest level.

“He just informed us, or Chelsea did. That is my understanding. We are not managing load. When I was in club football I used the term of an international break. When you hear it on the other side it is a totally different picture.”

Sports.title: England Wag takes cheeky swipe at Thomas Tuchel as she shares ‘a lot of mirror selfies’ from holiday
Sports.content:
Next

AN ENGLAND Wag took a cheeky swipe at Thomas Tuchel with her mirror selfies on holiday.

Britney De Villiers jetted off to Dubai with her man Morgan Gibbs-White for the extended international break.



However, their holiday was disrupted almost immediately after landing in the Middle East.

That is because Gibbs-White got a late call-up to the England squad for the Nations League fixtures.





And that meant he had to leave Britney and the kids on holiday as he headed back home to link up with the Three Lions at St George’s Park.

As a result, the glamorous South African model and influencer could not resist a funny dig at the situation Tuchel has dropped her in.

She wrote on Instagram to her 274,000 followers: “A lot of mirror selfies because my photographer had to leave,” followed by a laughing emoji.

Britney posted eight photos from the holiday – including five mirror selfies.



In them, she rocked a black-and-white checked bikini with a matching bandana and overshirt, posed in a close-up one wearing a sleeveless beige top and showed herself in the lift with one of the kids.

The other photos showed the stunning sunset in Dubai, her footballer partner by the pool holding their child and looking at a bird of prey and another of Britney and the kids in the sea.

One of the selfies, though, did feature Gibbs-White as she wore a blue swimsuit – clearly taken before he had to whizz off.



When he did, he recorded a hilarious TikTok video with Britney in which they mimed the words to High School Musical 2 hit Gotta Go My Own Way.

Britney captioned it: “When he gets a last-minute England call-up 2 hours into the family holiday.”

She then added: “He was clearly in a really good mood otherwise he’d never make this video with me.”



Fans were divided on social media – with some loving it but others joking he should be sent back on holiday for it.

Gibbs-White, 26, is hoping to add to his six senior England caps in the Nations League fixtures.

And if he continues to shine, he could find himself a club and country team-mate of Harry Kane, with Bayern Munich said to be interested.

Sports.title: 'Littler can become greatest ever but won't surpass legendary Taylor'
Sports.content:
Stephen Bunting believes Luke Littler can end his career as the greatest darts player of all time, even if he doesn’t win as many titles as the legendary Phil Taylor.

Littler had been on course for a clean sweep of the 2026 ranking events before a shock exit at the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam.

The world No 1 had won the first six premier events of the season after following his World Championship triumph at Alexandra Palace in January with the World Masters, UK Open, Premier League, World Cup of Darts and World Matchplay.

Darts in 2026 Event Winner Dates World Championship Luke Littler Dec 11-Jan 3 World Masters Luke Littler Jan 29-Feb 1 UK Open Luke Littler March 6-8 Premier League* Luke Littler Feb to May World Cup* Luke Littler and Luke Humphries June 11-14 World Matchplay Luke Littler July 18-16 World Series of Darts Finals* Ross Smith September 17-20 World Grand Prix Sept 28-Oct 4 European Championship October 22-25 Grand Slam of Darts November 14-22 Players Championship Finals November 27-29 *Non-ranking event

Littler was hoping to add the World Series of Darts Finals, World Grand Prix, European Championship, Grand Slam of Darts and Players Championship Finals trophies to complete a historic monopoly over the year - but lost to Jonny Clayton in the quarter-finals.

Despite defeat, many experts are already predicting the 19-year-old becoming the greatest player the sport has ever seen - including Bunting.

"I do," the 41-year-old told Sky Sports News when asked if he thinks Littler can end his career as the greatest darts player ever. "I think he's got a lot more to give the sport."

Image: Phil Taylor is regarded as the best darts player of all time

However, Bunting believes darts legend Taylor, who retired in 2018, will still have the edge over Littler when it comes to the number of titles won.

"I think he'll win a lot more world titles, but I don't think he'll win as many as Phil," he said. "The standard of play is a lot better than in Phil's day. Phil did dominate.

"But [Littler] is someone who has changed our sport. He's brought the [age] demographic of the sport down. If you ask people who a darts player is, they all say Luke Littler, that's how powerful his name is."

Bunting did admit, however, that he would rather leave the debate over who is the best to Taylor and Littler themselves.

"I think certainly Luke's ceiling is phenomenal," he continued. "Based on his ceiling he is the best player in the world. Phil 'The Power' Taylor won 16 World Championships - you can't take that away from Phil.

"If Phil tells me he's the best darts player in the world, he's the best darts player in the world. I'll leave it for them to discuss. I'd be happy to win one or two world titles, but Luke is smashing it already.

"He's playing fantastic, won another European Tour, so he's pretty unstoppable. But there's a couple of players behind him who can also have high ceilings as well, so on the day, who knows what can happen."

Speaking on Love The Darts podcast, Bunting addressed Littler being booed and whistled at during the World Series of Darts Finals where he was asked whether it has gone too far.

"A loud whistle really does throw you off and I've had it in my career. It's not nice and it's off-putting when you're throwing for a double," said Bunting. "It's the minority."

Goodbye Peter Griffin, hello Titanium

Image: Stephen Bunting thinks Taylor will end up with more titles than Littler

Bunting will be competing at the World Grand Prix where he will be looking to go one step further after making the semi-finals twice previously.

"Definitely," Bunting said when asked if he can win the title in Leicester. "Hopefully I can go in with some really good form, these next few tournaments push me there with some confidence.

"The Grand Prix is a double-off format, I really enjoy hitting my doubles. It's going to be a great tournament. It's brilliant Sky Sports covers it and hopefully I can put on a good show for the fans and get the title."

As well as watching Bunting in full flow, fans at Leicester's Mattioli Arena will be excited when he walks out to his song 'Titanium'.

"My son's favourite song," Bunting said when asked about his song change. "It was an easy one to pick. I wanted to get away from the Peter Griffin and the 'Bird is the Word' song. Everyone's been really positive towards it.

"It's one of the greatest walk-on songs in my opinion. It's really a special moment when I'm doing the actions and they're singing it back to me. It makes me feel so happy.

"Obviously, we're up there to do a job and play darts, but the walk-on and the crowd takes the pressure away and it relaxes me when I've done the walk-on.

"When the crowd are singing 'let's go Bunting-mental', they really are my 12th man. To be able to use the crowd as a power, it's really important, they're a huge part of my game and it's nice to be able to give something back to them."

Bunting spoke to Sky Sports News ahead of the launch of his new book 'Bulletproof', with the autobiography's title a nod to the lyrics in 'Titanium' and his nickname - but also about his battle to refuse to give up his darts.

"Sometimes it can be really difficult," Bunting admitted when asked about the hate he can receive on social media. "I'm lucky I've got a great team around me, a brilliant family and some unbelievable fans and they've really helped me through a little bit of a dark time.

"It came off the back of the 'people's champion' debacle, which was taken well out of context. I've put that all behind me now. It's about rebuilding again. The confidence is high, even though the results are not going my way at the minute, I'm sure that's about to change.

"It was important to show everyone, this was a life story, so, everything needs to be in there," he said. "The gambling debts were a big part of my life.

"When times were low, I'd lock myself away, and I'd be on my phone gambling. It was a horrible place to be in. I was in a rut and thankfully, sports psychologist, hypnotist and everything about that really helped me and helped me look at it in a positive way, even though somethings may not be positive, still taking a positive spin on it.

"Gambling was a way out at the time but I was able to put that to bed and if one little bit out of this book can help anyone in this situation, the book's a winner."

Sports.title: Fury claims all-British heavyweight blockbuster with AJ in jeopardy
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury has sensationally claimed that his long awaited fight against Anthony Joshua is in serious jeopardy.

On Thursday, confirmation finally arrived that Fury and Joshua's all-British heavyweight showdown will take place at Cardiff's Principality Stadium on Friday December 11 following months of protracted negotiations to stage the biggest fight in British boxing history.

Saudi boxing powerbroker Turki Alalshikh announced the details had been ironed out for the two foremost heavyweights of their generation to collide but Fury has made the astonishing claim that the fight could be called off.

"Breaking news, Anthony Joshua and Eddie Hearn are trying to pull out the fight," said Fury.

"They're saying they're not going to fight now. It's mainly to do with Eddie Hearn's ego. He's making up a million different things and threatening 'we're not gonna fight'," said Fury.

"Now the Gypsy King is coming back to the United Kingdon to thrash you in front of all my fans in Wales, and now you are making a million excuses.

"Now you've got Turki Alalshikh finding alternative, real men who will fight at the drop of a hat. I hope you are happy."

Image: Tyson Fury claims heavyweight super fight with Anthony Joshua could be called off

Sky Sports News have contacted Matchroom Sport for comment.

Joshua and Fury, both former heavyweight world champions, have had a long-running rivalry, punctuated by callouts and trash talk but marred by the difficulty of finalising a deal.

Recent events in the ring had also threatened to derail it. Joshua's tune-up bout in July almost ended in disaster when little-known Kristian Prenga knocked him down twice in the first round. Joshua rallied to dispatch Prenga in the second round.

Fury's road to the fight has also been unusual. He announced his retirement after losing a rematch to Oleksandr Usyk and, after a year out of the sport, began training in Thailand. In April he came back at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London when he soundly outpointed Arslanbek Makhmudov.

He decided he wanted his own additional warm-up in July and boxed Mariusz Wach in Thailand in a non-TV bout, eventually stopping the veteran after seven rounds.

Sports.title: Eye Of Dubai looks to retain Ripon crown
Sports.content:
Ripon, Southwell and Belmont Park headline Saturday's action - live on Sky Sports Racing.

3.28 Ripon - Eye Of Dubai bids for a third win in the race

Eye Of Dubai seeks a third consecutive success in the feature Ripon Cathedral City Of The Dales Handicap.

John and Sean Quinn's five-year-old returned to winning ways when claiming the Ayr Bronze Cup last weekend and this course specialist must be feared from this 5lb higher mark.

Stalemate Dark Thirty is a noteworthy runner after his excellent third at the Curragh and the handicapper has given him a chance with a 2lb drop in the weights. Jake Dickson takes a further 5lb off, giving this gelded son of Starspangledbanner a real opportunity here.

Trefor is a course and distance winner who is closely matched with Indian Run on their Windsor 1-3 in August and both rate each-way contenders, despite the inconsistent recent efforts of the former.

David O'Meara saddles Yes I'm Mali who scored over this track and trip on his penultimate start and should go well with Conor Whiteley claiming a handy 5lb.

7.00 Southwell - Well-bred pair Pyramid and Kashooda headline

Pyramid and Kashooda contest a potentially informative Free Bets On attheraces.com Maiden Stakes at Southwell.

Juddmonte colt Pyramid caught the eye when runner-up at Wolverhampton on his debut in July, denied a run until the race was over, he stuck on nicely and should improve for that outing. The winner has since finished second in Listed company while the third scored next time so the form looks rock solid.

Kashooda is the main danger for Andrew Balding and Callum Hutchinson. She has placed on both starts to date including when second to a nice type at Kempton and ought to have more to offer.

Others to note include Roxy Power and Pepperazzi, who debuts in the Valmont silks for Oliver Cole.

10.19 Belmont Park - Pride Of Arras and El Cordobes lock horns

A cracking renewal of this Grade 1 Joe Hirsch Stakes sees European raiders El Cordobes and Pride Of Arras headline a field of seven.

Charlie Appleby's El Cordobes finished third behind stablemate Rebel's Romance in this race last year before producing a career best to claim the same spot in the Breeders' Cup Turf. Not seen since down the field in the H.H The Amir Trophy in February, he has claims if fit enough after this break.

Image: El Cordobes heads Stateside for the Joe Hirsch Stakes

Ralph Beckett's Pride Of Arras took the notable scalp of Gethin when landing the Group 3 September Stakes at Kempton and a similar display would give him an obvious chance as he heads up to Grade 1 company again.

Far Bridge took a Grade 3 on his last outing but was behind El Cordobes in this race last season, while the Ed Walker-trained Fort George has claims on the pick of his form.

Best of the rest

The day begins with Grade 1 action from Australia, where Guest House and St Gotthard contest the Golden Rose Stakes at Rosehill (7.05am).

Back on home soil, Zarakova tops six runners in Ripon's 2.16pm Lloyd Landrover Ripon Nursery Handicap. In opposition is Palace Legacy, who steps into handicap company for the first time.

Auteuil's G3 Prix de Maisons-Laffitte at 2.50pm sees Leopard Du Berlais attempt to get back on track. The four-year-old won his first three starts by a combined 18 lengths but has failed to fire since. A market check could prove important.

Caragio was unlucky not to win the Leger Legends contest at Doncaster earlier this month, when trainer and owner Adam Kirby kicked for home slightly early aboard this son of Caravaggio. Down 1lb for that effort, he will be well-fancied in Southwell's 8pm At The Races App Expert Tips Handicap.

Stateside, Sunlit Uplands, Esna, Cathedral and Kathynmarissa all line up for the G2 Flower Bowl at Belmont before Santa Anita plays host to the Goodwood Stakes at 12.30am.

Sports.title: Fisher vs Pirotton - big fight predictions
Sports.content:
Experts have their say ahead of the Johnny Fisher vs Michael Pirotton, Craig Richards vs Radivoje Kalajdzic and Lee Cutler vs Louis Greene fights, live on Sky Sports from 7pm.

Johnny Fisher vs Michael Pirotton

Chris Billam-Smith (Former world champion): I did some sparring with Johnny, he's fit and strong as always. You can see that changes have been made under Tony [Sims, his new trainer]. From what I have seen of Pirotton, he's quite negative, he keeps it long. I expect Johnny to come through that.

Johnny Nelson (Former world champion): Pirotton, we don't know enough about him. We've made that mistake before when you run away with the hype machine.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Michael Pirotton says he is ready for whatever Johnny Fisher brings ahead of their heavyweight clash at the Copper Box.

Pirotton's never been put down, he's sparred with a lot of big-name fighters. I hope Johnny wins but I am concerned about this fight. Pirotton, his background pedigree is nothing to be sniffed at.

If Pirotton boxes in the defence then Johnny Fisher will hunt him down. He's better off going to fight fire with fire.

Da'Mazion Vanhouter (heavyweight prospect): It's going to be a good fight, I can see Fisher pulling it off. I don't know if it'll be a knockout or a decision but I'm saying it'll be a good fight. I think it'll definitely be tough.

Cheavon Clarke (Former British champion): I'm voting for Johnny. I've heard that Pirotton's very good. I'm sure Johnny's been training, I'm sure he'll come prepared. He'll be fit and ready to roll. So I'm rolling with the Brit.

Paul Ready (boxing manager): I think it will be interesting. I favour Johnny to maybe stop him in the second half of the fight. But I think there will definitely be some moments where Johnny will be tested. I think the start will be key for both. But I fancy Johnny Fisher by stoppage, in maybe eight or nine.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Michael Pirotton discusses why he feels more ready than ever to take on Johnny Fisher and discusses what he'll need to do to take the win.

Craig "Spider" Richards vs Radivoje "Hot Rod" Kalajdzic

Billam-Smith: I've done loads of rounds with Craig over the years. Good fighter, got a good jab, good timing but he's deceiving with it.

Radivoje obviously carries power and can box a bit. It'll be an interesting one. I'd pick Craig to win that, probably on points.

Nelson: Spider you saw him in there with Bivol. He's got bottle and he's got self-belief. He'll probably think to himself, this is my last hurrah.

Every fight for him is a world title fight because he still has that appetite and that ambition. I see Spider winning. He's a very clever fighter, very underrated boxer.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Having announced he'll face Radivoje Kalajdzic on Zuffa Boxing 11's undercard, Craig Richards believes he'll now be able to be able to get the big fights after linking up with the new promotional company.

Vanhouter: You can expect to see Hot Rod's best performance. He's going to shock UK fans after this fight.

Clarke: I think Spider's a very good fighter. I've done rounds with him as well. His fight against Buatsi, what a fight that was. Spider's a very good fighter and I'm expecting him to come out on top. Stoppage - I'm calling it.

Ready: I think Craig will definitely have to overcome some adversity in that fight but I think Craig maybe wins a split.

Lee Cutler vs Louis Greene

Billam-Smith: It's not an easy fight for Lee, by no stretch. You know what you're getting. Green is going to come forward. Lee's adaptable, he can box in different ways, he can box on the front foot, he can box on the back foot. It's down to the game plan. Stick to that and he can win.

Nelson: Louis is a scary man but I like Lee Cutler for this fight. There's a lot more going on with Lee Cutler. Don't be fooled and don't dismiss his experience in the ups and downs of our game. I'm going with Lee Cutler. It'll be a great fight. Trust me it will be an action-packed fight.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Johnny Fisher looks ahead to his fight against Michael Pirotton and praises his support network that has carried him this far.

Vanhouter: I like Lee Cutler's style, I think he'll pull it off. I like his style so I'm hoping that Lee wins.

Clarke: That's possibly fight of the night because them two are coming and I don't feel that they're going to leave anything. I think it's going to be sit in the middle of the ring and slug it out. It's going to be who's the tough man on the night. I think that's a 50-50 fight, definitely. But I live in Kent, so I'm rolling with Louis.

Ready: I'm going to go for the upset here. I think it'll be Louis Greene, points. I think it'll be a good attritional fight.

20m ago 05.56 EDT Tomorrow’s match could potentially be season-defining for Arsenal – despite it being so early in the campaign. The Gunners have scored just two goals in their opening three games and currently sit on five points following two draws and a win. League leaders Manchester City extended the gap to four points last weekend, and Arsenal cannot risk dropping too far behind them. Arsenal head coach Renée Slegers said: “I think it’s been clear that we wanted more points, so the two draws we’re not happy with, and I don’t think we need to over-dramatise the performances, but of course we want to and need to score and win games, and we’re of course very aware of it, and that’s where we are now and we’re looking ahead to Sunday.” View image in fullscreen Renee Slegers says Arsenal are ‘not happy’ with their two draws this season. 1h ago 05.10 EDT Bernstein argues 'money is not sufficient' for potential City punishment Former Manchester City chairman David Bernstein believes “money is not sufficient” in terms of a potential punishment for the club being found guilty on virtually all counts of breaching Premier League financial rules. News broke on Friday that City had been found guilty on all but one of the 115 charges laid by the Premier League in February 2023, charges the club have always strenuously denied. The charges date back to the 2009-10 season, since which time City have won multiple major trophies. City are expected to appeal, and Bernstein, who was City chairman between 1998 and 2003, would want to see that process dealt with quickly. He told Times Radio: “I felt absolutely awful, I felt in shock yesterday, actually. I think you’ve asked me on the programme because of my time as chair of City and the FA, but basically I’m a fan of Manchester City and have been a fan for 70 years. “It’s really awful that this great period of success, which followed many years of being less successful, when I was chair I think I helped get the club out of a very difficult period and started the road to better things. “But to see all this tarnished in this way is very sad, I feel particularly bad for the wonderful supporters of the club who’ve stayed with the club through thick and thin. It’s a pretty bad day I think for the fans in blue of Manchester.” Asked what the correct punishment would be, Bernstein said: “First of all, the timing of this I think is crucial. This whole process has taken too long already. “So the appeal process now has to be done quickly because…you’ve got the club playing with this cloud over its head and it’s just not viable. “The appeal process cannot go on for year after year, I think that would be a disaster. Not just for this particular case but for English football generally. The timing is crucial. “I can’t give a view on the punishment. If they are found, after the appeal, guilty of 115 charges, my beloved club is going to face a very severe penalty. “All I would say is that money is not sufficient, it would have to be something, unfortunately, more drastic than that.” Press Association Share

1h ago 05.06 EDT Thomas Tuchel has thrown Cole Palmer’s England future into major doubt by questioning whether the Chelsea attacker wants to be part of his squad. England’s head coach did not hold back on Palmer’s latest withdrawal from international duty, warning that the 24-year-old has missed too many opportunities to play for his country. Palmer has only 14 caps and his decision not to join up with the squad this week, because of a minor muscular injury, caused disappointment given he was left out of Tuchel’s World Cup squad after struggling with form and fitness last season. Tuchel said: “He misses too many camps. That’s the overall headline. We have a lot of invitations and he couldn’t make this one. It is what it is. I am not ready to focus on players who are not here. The players that are here have my full attention. “It is a missed opportunity. He [Palmer] misses too many opportunities. I don’t blame him for it. It is just a fact. He misses way too many camps with injuries, and I only want to rely on what I witness within my team, and for that you have to be in camp.” View image in fullscreen Cole Palmer withdrew from the England squad last week. Photograph: Ryan Pierse/Getty Images Share

2h ago 04.40 EDT England host Spain at Wembley this evening. Thomas Tuchel was asked yesterday if he thought that Spain’s possession-based style of play gives them an advantage. In response, the England head coach said: “I think it is an advantage in general. Not only against us, but against everyone. This is how they play. I think they rely on that. This is how they train and they were brought up. This is clearly part of them. “But at the moment, I think the more you analyse Spain and their last matches they played in, you have to admire the way in which they defend. They added this to their game. It is collective work and they are masters of delaying and pushing you towards wide areas where they can initiate the press. “They have world class goalkeepers, as you know - three of them - but they are hardly tested. It is so difficult for every single team in the world to create chances against them. We have a plan and we have ambition, and we want to prove the opposite. We want to be the exception to the rule, but at the moment they are a very complete team.” View image in fullscreen Thomas Tuchel looks on during a training session at Tottenham Hotspur Training Centre. Here was a grand, stoic old club, taken over in 2008 by Abu Dhabi royalty and mega-funded to imperious success, then crowned serial champions by a league simultaneously pursuing charges of monstrous financial cheating…” How drawn-out saga of Manchester City’s alleged cheating came to this Read more Share

2h ago 03.52 EDT Rodri says nobody can take away Manchester City players’ success and still believes in his former club’s innocence despite reports they have been found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules. “We have faced something similar back in 2020, we had a similar judicial process,” the Barcelona midfielder said. “Different accusation but similar process. “There as well in the first instance we were found guilty, but we believed in the club and the innocence that the club maintained and in the end we ended up acquitted. So, I believe in the justice system, and I believe in the innocence of the club.” Asked if such talk hurts having achieved so much with City, Rodri said: “For us, the players, it is a different thing than for you guys. I can understand all kind of opinions, and it is something that now is big. “But we always tried to think in a positive way, when you live that club daily and the people who have worked hard all these years to have all the success we had. “Not only Pep [Guardiola] and the players but all the structure, from the owners to the guys who worked daily. What we did, they cannot take it out of us. It is something that is not paid by money, it is paid with effort, with partnership and with being shoulder to shoulder every day. “We had a lot of success over the years and here in Wembley, so I can tell you everything was deserved and I’m glad I could live one of the best eras of English football.” View image in fullscreen Spain's Rodri during a press conference at Wembley Stadium. Sports.title: Manchester City verdict: what happens next, will club appeal and could they be relegated?
Sports.content:
What happens next?

Manchester City have been found guilty of the vast majority of the 134 disciplinary charges brought against them by the Premier League.

In keeping with the history of this explosive case which has been conducted exclusively in private and with every party sworn to secrecy, there is a lot we don’t know. We do not even have an official confirmation that the three-person judicial panel has reached a verdict on the case. All of football is acting as if they have, however, and that reports of a big win for the Premier League are correct.

If these assumptions are correct, and neither party have formally denied them at least, then the immediate thing to watch out for is news of an appeal. Under Premier League rules, City would have 14 days from the announcement of the verdict to submit an appeal and the process that follows should be completed in less than 12 weeks from then. Once the appeal has been heard – which should happen in one block of no more than five days – and a verdict reached, the appeal panel are also expected to publish written reasons behind their decisions. We should also see the written reasons from the original judicial panel too, but the unique scale of this case has meant that normal procedures have not always been followed, and the date of publication for these reasons remains unknown.

If City do appeal, what happens?

The club would be submitting an appeal based solely on the decision and not any resulting punishment, which is yet to be determined. In hoping to make the case that the judicial panel were wrong in their observations, City would be allowed to submit new evidence, providing it had not been previously available to them, and make new oral presentations. Once the hearing is concluded, a verdict would be expected in 30 days.

If an appeal fails, what then?

According to Premier League rule W.97, “the decision of an Appeal Board shall be final”, but even this is subject to one final route, that of arbitration. This would again mean appearing in front of another panel of eminent legal figures, but the criteria for any hearing would be a lot stricter and successful arbitration only possible in the main if the judicial panel or appeal board was found to have abused the legal process. City have recently been through the arbitration process with the Premier League over its rules related to associated party transactions and, after an initial verdict challenged two applications of the rules but otherwise found them to be sound, City and the Premier League reached a settlement which stopped the case from going to court.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

When and how would City be punished?

If City managed to overturn the verdict, there would of course be no sanction. If City’s appeals failed, there are a number of measures available to the panel. They start at fines and end at complete expulsion from the league, with a variety of sporting sanctions including point deductions falling in-between. Given the magnitude of the verdict, City can expect to receive a punishment at the sharper end of the scale should their appeal not prove successful.

Could relegation be the end of it?

It seems unlikely. Premier League clubs and those who have been relegated from the division are understood to have been assessing any potential financial losses they may have incurred during the period City were winning and, appeal pending, breaking the rules. A wave of lawsuits is likely to follow, with Manchester United, for example, having finished second behind City in 2017-18 and potentially denied a record-breaking 21st league title in the process. It is possible that clubs who were relegated could argue that they were sent down because of points denied them by a City side subsequently found to have cheated. Premier League clubs reportedly lost their appetite for legal action after an estimated £50m cost to the competition last season, but if the verdict against City revealed this week is ultimately upheld, a new wave of lawsuits will surely follow.

Sports.title: ‘Island girl’ Malard aims to ‘become a legend’ in Réunion with Bompastor
Sports.content:
It is rare to see Melvine Malard without a grin and she has a mountain of reasons to keep it that way. A wedding in June, a big-money move to Chelsea, a Ballon d’Or nomination and a first taste of a fiery London derby against Arsenal at Stamford Bridge on Sunday. The French forward is loving life and the personality behind the smile that instantly connects her to teammates is infectious.

“Goals,” says Malard, with a laugh, when asked what keeps her happy. “Seriously though, it’s seeing the kids, the families, my family, in the stands. It is crazy. I love my life, I love my job, I’m happy with my wife and everything is good. I smile because of those things, because I’m happy.”

You cannot help but feel the childlike wonder emanating from the 26-year-old at football being her job and this being her life. The little girl who started playing football later than most, at six or seven, after she had tried out “literally every other sport”, retains the deep appreciation for the joy it has brought her from the first moment.

The love of the game was instant, “partly because it’s a team sport and I loved that you get to enjoy it with everyone in your team and then I also found I felt both strong and free when I play football. I have to play with a lot of energy and a lot of smiles. It’s also important for me that the fans get to know me and get to enjoy the football with me.”

0:46 Chelsea’s Melvine Malard: ‘Football is the last sport I tried’ – video

Malard grew up on Réunion, a small island east of Madagascar that has a population of less than one million, was formerly a French colony and is now an overseas department of France.

“It’s a little island with a lot of people smiling, good life and good food,” she says. Girls did not really play football, but Malard paved the way: “I’m very proud of that; it’s a good feeling.”

At 14 she caught the eye of Sonia Bompastor at an under-15s match at France’s national football centre in Clairefontaine. The now-Chelsea manager was in charge of Lyon’s academy.

Bompastor persuaded Malard’s mother to allow the 14-year-old to move more than 5,600 miles and Malard hasn’t looked back, though home is far from forgotten. “Everywhere I go and wherever I think about where I’m from, I want to show where I’m from and I want to give back and just make everyone proud of me.”

Signing for Chelsea from Manchester United this summer was a full circle moment, reuniting her with the manager who plucked her from her island life and gave her the chance to pursue her dream at one of the biggest clubs in Europe.

“I will never forget Manchester United,” Malard says. “They helped me make a change in my life when I really needed change.”

She has a lot of love for many people at the club. However, she wanted to be somewhere that matched her ambitions. She loves life, but life is short.

View image in fullscreen Malard celebrated with a Réunion flag after helping Manchester United win the FA Cup in 2024. Photograph: Adam Davy/PA

Asked whether it was frustrating that things did not really kick on after Manchester United’s FA Cup win, with a lack of club support for the women’s side widely reported, Malard says: “Of course, it’s for that reason that I’m here. I don’t want to lose any time in my career. Football moves quickly and sometimes you need to make the choice that is best for your career. I think coming here was a good choice. At Chelsea, there are clear ambitions: to win the game, win the trophies and raise the level higher. That is where I need to be.”

Bompastor’s pursuit was a real vote of confidence in her as a player and person, because few know her better. “She knows my qualities, my energy, my personality and she knows what I need to learn and where I need to progress,” Malard says.

Bompastor wields influence. “It’s not just about Sonia as a manager,” Malard says. “Sonia is also a legendary player, [her assistant and partner] Camille Abily also. They played football, they know football and when they speak with me I can’t say anything because they know more than me. That can help you progress a lot, they set the level you know you need to be at to become a legend.”

Legacy matters to Malard. She wants to become a legend at Chelsea and the Champions League is the way she believes she can do it: “I want to write my name on a new page, but not any page, a page you remember. For me, the way to do that with Chelsea is to win something the club has never won..”

She came off the bench in the 5-2 home win over Real Sociedad in qualifying, making the difference with the score at 2-2 by scoring the first of her two goals 12 minutes later.

View image in fullscreen Malard scored on both her WSL and Champions League debuts for Chelsea. Photograph: Linda Nylind/The Guardian

“It felt good, very good,” she says. “I think it’s because of my personality too. I’m not a player that is difficult to play when things aren’t going to plan. I’m the player that puts energy into every area on and off the pitch. The girls know that about me already, they know where I want to go.”

A frustrating couple of weeks out with injury followed, but she returned, and scored, in Chelsea’s 2-0 win over Birmingham and featured in the 1-0 win over Austria Vienna on Wednesday.

Sitting by the Shed End sign in the royal blue Stamford Bridge seats, Malard is excited at the prospect of facing Arsenal here. “All players want to play this game,” she says, the smile still there but with an edge this time. “You train hard for these games against big teams in big stadiums with lots of fans waiting for you to play and score. I can’t wait.”

She wants to score, she wants to win, but she is winning regardless and every game, every moment, every accolade takes her back to the beginning.

“When I look at the little girl from that island today playing for Chelsea and nominated for the Ballon d’Or, it’s a lot for me to take in, and a lot for my family,” she says. “It gives me the motivation to continue this way and, I’m very proud of myself.”

Sports.title: Liverpool rehire Julian Ward as sporting director to replace Richard Hughes
Sports.content:
Liverpool have appointed Julian Ward as their sporting director for a second time following the departure of Richard Hughes to Al-Hilal.

Ward, who was Liverpool’s sporting director for one season in 2022-23, has returned to the role after spending the past two years as technical director for Fenway Sports Group, the club’s owners.

The swift process of finding a successor to Hughes, who left for the Saudi Pro League after two and a half years at Anfield when the summer transfer window ended, was led by the FSG president, Mike Gordon.

Ward has worked in various capacities for Liverpool over the past 14 years, including European scouting manager, assistant sporting director and sporting director.

His appointment offers continuity at a time of upheaval in the Liverpool hierarchy with Hughes and Michael Edwards, the former chief executive of football at FSG, exiting this year and the owners in the process of selling a 38% stake in the club to 1892 Holdings for £2bn. The consortium, fronted by Amit Bhatia and including the Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, has an option for a full takeover should FSG decide to sell up.

View image in fullscreen Jürgen Klopp signs a contract extension in April 2022 with FSG’s Michael Gordon (left) and Julian Ward, then Liverpool’s assistant sporting director. Photograph: Andrew Powell/Liverpool FC/Getty Images

The 45-year-old Ward replaced Edwards as sporting director in 2022 but told FSG he wished to step away for personal reasons only months into the role. Luis Díaz, Cody Gakpo, Alexis Mac Allister and Darwin Núñez were signed during Ward’s first spell although the then manager Jürgen Klopp had a greater say on transfers after Edwards left.

Ward remained highly regarded by FSG, however, and Gordon, who had resumed the day-to-day running of Liverpool after Hughes’s departure, considers his extensive knowledge of the club and of squad planning as invaluable. As FSG’s technical director, Ward had oversight of the global talent strategy that has seen Liverpool sign several highly rated young prospects this year.

Liverpool’s new sporting director will lead the club’s football operation alongside the assistant sporting director David Woodfine, chief scout Barry Hunter, FSG’s director of football development Pedro Marques and Andoni Iraola’s senior leadership team.

Sports.title: Lamine Yamal: ‘Football is mechanised but players like me have that special spark’
Sports.content:
Like the kid he is, Lamine Yamal just wanted to keep playing. This wasn’t Plaça Joan XXIII, wasn’t El Parque de Rocafonda either; it wasn’t the Mataró neighbourhood where it all began, but it might have been. “We’re in a World Cup final and I wanted to carry on,” he says, and there’s the smile again, the braces. Really? “Yes”. No nerves? “No. I never thought: ‘Just blow the whistle’. I was enjoying it.” No fear, just fun: 19 July, New Jersey and he knew: this 19-year-old who had happily been asleep on the bus to the biggest match of his life.

And now he sits in a first-floor office in Las Rozas, surrounded by tactics boards and stats sheets. There’s a Spain keyring hanging from the door and a second star on his shirt. In the corridor, crates loaded for London. Son of Mounir and Sheila, named after the family friends who helped them, “touched by God’s wand” in the words of the coach whose office is next door, there’s something about Lamine Yamal. He turned 17 the day before the final of Euro 2024, a schoolboy sitting exams, and 19 the day before the semi-final of the World Cup. Asked what he wanted, he said a trip to New York, so there he was, about to be a champion again.

The way Lamine Yamal tells it, Spain knew they were world champions before they had scored, in the moment Enzo Fernández was sent off. It was the third minute of second-half stoppage time, still 0-0, but now, he says: “We knew it was impossible they would score, and with the ball against 10, very difficult for us not to.” The surprise was that they hadn’t already, but on 106 minutes the ball came to his feet. He had been thinking about this moment for some time.

The battle with the one, two, three players facing you is “very psychological”, Lamine Yamal says. “A full-back will have a coach who says: ‘OK, Lamine: what he does is …’ I think of him as a robot, trying to stop me. Robots can be almost perfect but a human will have something a robot doesn’t. Football is mechanised but there are players like me, Pedri, many others, who have that special spark. There’s a typical Neymar move when he stops, fakes, goes the other way: I watched so many videos of him. I try to play with opponents, ensure they can’t mechanise me, don’t know where I’m going.”

“I remember three plays in minutes 60, 70, 80 or thereabouts, when I took on the full-back. Every time, [Alexis] Mac Allister came over. If I had really wanted to go at the full-back, I would have gone at him fast; instead this time I went slower, carrying the ball, so that Mac Allister had time to get to me, Pedro [Porro] could arrive behind me and I could play it back.” A little space made, from Porro’s cross Nico Williams headed back and Ferran Torres, who had struggled throughout the tournament, scored the goal.

“We knew Ferran needed it,” Lamine Yamal says, then laughs: “Well, everyone needs a goal in a World Cup final. If Unai Simón had scored, great. When it goes in, it’s spectacular, you feel you’re champions. You can’t explain the emotion. All I wanted was to keep playing. I never thought: ‘They might equalise’. There was a small push, a chance [Pau] Cubarsí cleared, but I was enjoying it.”

Lamine Yamal talks to the Guardian’s Sid Lowe about his iconic photos with Lionel Messi

The mini trophy is at Lamine Yamal’s mum’s house; he gave the Lego trophy to his dad but his little brother, Keyne, broke it. At the final whistle, he embraced Lionel Messi. “I said thank you for everything you gave football. I don’t do things to look nice for the photo; that came from inside,” Lamine Yamal says, but the symbolism was powerful, like a rite of passage, a passing of the torch. Lamine, 19, hugging Messi, 39, who had bathed him when he was a baby, as if it was a baptism, the creation. As if he had made this happen.

Almost absurd in its perfection, utterly implausible, the bathtub origin story poses so many questions, but here’s one that baffles: why on earth did your dad not produce that picture for 17 years? “Because I told him not to,” Lamine Yamal says. “He put it on Facebook once and I told him to take it down. Comparisons were too easy, that was all people would talk about. I wanted to be Lamine; I didn’t want to be Messi. I just wanted to get where I could get. I asked him to wait. When I’m Lamine, do what you want.”

Oh, he’s Lamine all right, and where he has got to no one has. A global social phenomenon, his image was everywhere at the World Cup, whole stadiums waiting on him, the comparisons he tried to avoid inevitable. And, amazingly, in his favour. No one had ever won a Euros and a World Cup younger, at 19 years and six days. Messi was 35 when he won the World Cup; Diego Maradona was 25; Cristiano Ronaldo never has. Who knows what he could achieve? Spain’s candidate for the Ballon d’Or (even if Kylian Mbappé has support in Madrid), he would be the youngest winner, ever.

View image in fullscreen Lamine Yamal with the World Cup after Spain beat Argentina 1-0 after extra time. Photograph: Alex Livesey/Danehouse/Getty Images

Nor is it just about the titles. It is about the play and the personality, something different, an appeal, apparent even in this office. And something deeper, too. Luis de la Fuente likened Lamine Yamal to Salvador Dalí and Michelangelo, a genius. He knows that himself and doesn’t mind saying so. Doesn’t mind saying that, yes, he should be named the world’s best footballer. Because, well, he is. Even at 19, which may in fact be what goes against him.

“Being completely honest, it’s not just this year I’ve been at a Ballon d’Or [winning] level, but longer. Everyone knows that; they know I am differential,” he says. “I think people think: ‘Lamine is 19, he’ll win it at some point, so let’s say someone else …’ I just have to win, win, win, and there will be a time when there’s no debate. There will be people who love me, people who say: ‘What a pain in the arse he is’, and that’s fine.”

“After the final, my family were so happy,” Lamine Yamal continues, laughing once again. “The problem with that is they don’t know what it is to lose. I go to the Euros, I win it. I go to the World Cup, I win it. It seems easy. There was a moment I thought: ‘When I don’t win they’re going to think I’m terrible.’ I told them: ‘Calm down, there will be plenty more World Cups.’ I have to play more and win more.

“At the Euros I didn’t even know who I was, where I was, the significance of it all. I could sit an exam and the next day play France because I wasn’t really conscious of the difference. I won it and said: ‘Well, that’s good, but a World Cup is better, no?’ Now I know what a Euros means. I know what a World Cup is, although I think you truly realise when you go to the next one and lose. There’s a lot still to do. Why not be the best national team in history? The best Barcelona? And if there’s anyone in the world who doesn’t ‘rest’ on success, who doesn’t have normal standards, it’s me.” No pressure, kid.

Lamine Yamal has lived that from the start. He was 13 the first time he felt some sort of fame. One day we will stop talking about his age but stop for a minute and it is still absurd: he went to the Euros at 16, a literal child, and the World Cup at 18 and won both. He has three league titles. The money, the fame, the exposure. It’s remarkable really that, to put it bluntly, he’s not a dickhead. “Well,” he laughs, “it depends how you’re brought up. I will never say: ‘Who are you? I won the World Cup.’ Only stupid people would do that. I know that football is 0.000001% of life.”

And there it is again; the maturity. Here’s a teenager supporting a family, who in his own words was handed “too much responsibility” too soon, who talks eloquently about the demands, exposure and about embracing them. At times he can seem to actually enjoy the attention and the pressure, wilfully adding to it, all a game. He can be accused of talking too much, and can reply: “Well, as long as I am winning … sport is serious but I want a show, some fun.” Remember Adrien Rabiot? He does. “That day you all saw how much I like it,” he says, grinning. At the World Cup his headband read: “Ego Yamal”. There’s a cheek, a mischief; he’s “playing” with us, he admits, with the silliness of it all.

View image in fullscreen Lamine Yamal with his brother Keyne after Spain had beaten England in the Euro 2024 final in Berlin. The winger had just turned 17. Photograph: Stefan Matzke/sampics/Getty Images

At times, but not all times. He says “a bad game from Lamine equals 400 bad games for anyone else”, that “I’ll produce a nine out of 10 and people will say seven out of 10”. At the World Cup, he visited Nashville: there’s a smile as he recalls the “cowboys, the atmosphere” … and the anonymity. A photo appeared of him at Walmart, a silly thing that mattered. “If we stopped in a gas station, I could get out and grab something,” he says. What he posts, what he says, he controls – which doesn’t mean always getting it right, or being happy. One post last season was entitled “my inner abyss”.
