World.title: Oil rig arrives in Mombasa ahead of Kenya's first commercial drilling
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Oil rig arrives in Mombasa ahead of Kenya’s first commercial drilling. [Courtes]

Kenya has moved closer to commercial oil production after a 1,500 horsepower drilling rig arrived at the Port of Mombasa ahead of its deployment to the South Lokichar Basin in Turkana County.

The GW70 rig, leased by Gulf Energy E&P BV from Great Wall Drilling Company, docked at Kilindini Port on Friday aboard MV Transit Sedanka after sailing from Duqm Port in Oman.

It is expected to be transported to Turkana, where drilling is scheduled to begin on November 1.

“All workstreams at Gulf Energy E&P BV SEZ are running to a tight project management schedule, and the project remains on course for First Oil production in December 2026,” Gulf Energy Chief Executive Officer Paul Limoh said.

The arrival marks a step in the commercial development of the South Lokichar Basin, more than a decade after oil was first discovered in Turkana in 2012.

The first phase of the project is expected to produce about 20,000 barrels of crude oil per day, with output projected to rise to 50,000 barrels per day in the second phase.

The Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA) says Kenya is targeting first oil in December 2026, while the first crude exports through the Port of Mombasa are expected in the first quarter of 2027.

The GW70 will undergo commissioning and acceptance checks before drilling begins. Gulf Energy has contracted Baker Hughes for integrated well services and SLB to provide an early production facility for the first phase.

World.title: Two more suspects arrested over lawyer Kyalo Mbobu murder
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The two suspects are currently in custody undergoing processing as detectives pursue additional leads.

Detectives have arrested two more suspects in connection with the fatal shooting of lawyer Kyalo Mbobu, as an intelligence-led operation targeting people linked to the September 9, 2025 murder intensifies.

The two boda boda riders Nicholas Lemiso Naula and Noah Kipkirui Langat were arrested in Nairobi’s Central Business District, following sustained efforts by detectives to trace individuals suspected to have been involved in the killing.

According to the Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI), Lemiso is a boda boda rider who allegedly ferried the main suspect, Police Constable Julius Cheruiyot, to and from the scene of the murder, while Langat was arrested over alleged surveillance on Mbobu before his killing.

"With three suspects now in custody, detectives are intensifying the hunt for other persons suspected to have played a role in the meticulously planned killing," DCI stated.

His arrest comes shortly after detectives arrested Cheruiyot in connection with the killing.

“The dragnet over the fatal shooting of lawyer Kyalo Mbobu has widened, with detectives arresting a second suspect as an intelligence-led operation targeting persons linked to the murder intensifies,” DCI said.

The two suspects are currently in custody undergoing processing as detectives pursue additional leads and seek to identify and arrest other people who may have been involved. The DCI said the operation remains active as investigators work to establish the circumstances surrounding Mbobu’s murder.

“The DCI is leaving no stone unturned in its efforts to unravel the full circumstances surrounding Lawyer Mbobu’s murder and bring all those responsible to justice,” the agency said.

World.title: KRA seizes 53,000 under-declared smartphones at Eldoret Airport
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The consignment was intercepted by KRA enforcement teams following an intelligence report.

Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA) has seized a consignment containing 53,000 under-declared smartphones at Eldoret International Airport, averting a potential tax loss of Sh21.5 million.

KRA enforcement teams intercepted the consignment after an intelligence report indicated it contained undeclared mobile phones and other high-end electronic goods.

The cargo, which had been declared under five Customs entries, was part of consolidated shipments that also included shoes, clothing, automotive spare parts, household goods, electronic accessories and other assorted items.

KRA said an initial declaration listed only 3,000 smartphones. However, verification established 55,607 ordinary smartphones, alongside 309 undeclared high-end smartphones.

The high-end devices included Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra, Samsung Galaxy Z Fold and Apple iPhone 17 Pro Max models.

“The consignment therefore reflects both under-declaration and non-declaration of dutiable goods,” KRA said in a statement issued on Wednesday.

The tax authority said the verification exercise was conducted to establish whether all mobile phones contained in the consignment had been properly declared.

KRA said the alleged tax evasion contravenes Section 203 of the East African Community Customs Management Act (EACCMA), 2004.

The law provides that a person who makes a false or incorrect Customs entry, or knowingly participates in the fraudulent evasion of duty, commits an offence.

“A person who, in any matter relating to Customs, makes any entry which is false or incorrect in any particular, or in any way is knowingly concerned in any fraudulent evasion of the payment of any duty, commits an offence,” KRA said, citing the law.

According to the authority, a person convicted under the provision is liable to imprisonment for a term not exceeding three years or a fine of up to US$10,000.

KRA said it was intensifying efforts to uncover tax evasion schemes to improve revenue compliance and ensure adherence to tax laws and procedures.

“KRA is actively engaged in unearthing tax evasion schemes to boost tax revenue compliance as well as adherence to tax laws and procedures, hence ensuring fair trade is maintained within the market,” the authority said.

The authority also appealed to members of the public, taxpayers and businesses with information on individuals, companies or networks involved in the generation, sale, purchase or use of fictitious VAT invoices to report them.

KRA said information provided would be treated confidentially and the identity of informants kept anonymous.

World.title: 'We know what happened': Uhuru claims Raila won 2022 polls
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Former President Uhuru Kenyatta. [File, Standard]

Former President Uhuru Kenyatta says he remains convinced that Raila Odinga won the 2022 presidential election.

Speaking during a Jubilee Party meeting in Nairobi on Tuesday, September 22, Uhuru questioned how the Azimio coalition could have lost the presidency despite performing strongly in other elective races.

“We did everything to help Baba become President of the Republic of Kenya. He got the votes, and to this day I know that he is the one who won those votes. We know how things happened, and we do not want it to happen that way again,” Uhuru said.

The late Odinga contested the August 9, 2022 election under the Azimio la Umoja-One Kenya Coalition Party, with Martha Karua as his running mate. Ruto ran under the United Democratic Alliance (UDA) as the presidential candidate of the Kenya Kwanza Alliance.

Ruto was declared president-elect after garnering 7,176,141 votes, 50.49 per cent, against Odinga's 6,942,930 votes, 48.85 per cent. Ruto's margin was 233,211 votes.

The Supreme Court later unanimously upheld his election after dismissing petitions challenging the results.

But Uhuru pointed to the coalition's performance in the parliamentary and county races to question how Azimio could have lost the presidency.

“How can you say we were defeated when we had most of the MPs, governors and senators? How were we defeated in the presidency?” he asked.

In the National Assembly, figures published after the election initially put Azimio ahead of Kenya Kwanza, with 165 seats against 160, while 12 seats were held by independent MPs.

Azimio also won 23 of the 47 governorships, while Kenya Kwanza secured 22. The remaining two were won by Taita Taveta Governor Andrew Mwadime and former Meru Governor Kawira Mwangaza, who ran as independent candidates.

In the Senate, Kenya Kwanza had an advantage, winning 24 of the 47 directly elected seats against Azimio's 23.

The parliamentary balance later shifted in favour of Kenya Kwanza after several MPs changed their political allegiance.

In October 2022, National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang'ula declared Kenya Kwanza the majority coalition with 179 MPs against Azimio's 157, after several MPs from parties including UDM, MDG, Maendeleo Chap Chap and PAA moved towards the Kenya Kwanza side.

Uhuru also rejected claims that he was responsible for Odinga's loss, saying he was not a candidate in the election.

“I am surprised when people say that we did not help Baba and that they defeated me. I was not on the ballot, and they are lying. I was only Raila's handyman,” he said.

He warned against what he described as divisive and dirty politics, saying Kenya should not repeat the events surrounding the 2022 election.

“Dirty politics and politics aimed at dividing Kenyans will take us nowhere. Let us not divide each other. What does it help us? Sell your manifesto,” Uhuru said.

He said he accepted the Supreme Court's decision after the 2022 presidential petitions and handed over power to Ruto without disputing the outcome, accusing Ruto of dragging his name in his failed leadership.

“When we finished and the court ruled, we did not dispute it. We went and handed over the presidency to them. And now, after four years, they are still talking about Uhuru. But when things are not working, people tend to look for excuses,” he said.

This is the clearest public assertion by the former president since the 2022 elections that Odinga won the presidential vote.

World.title: Ruto offers Kenya as test case on African risk
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto with Dangote Industries President and CEO Aliko Dangote and Africa Finance Corporation (AFC) CEO Samaila Zubairu on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York, USA. [PCS]

President William Ruto has offered Kenya as a test case for how African risk is assessed, saying the country will open its default and recovery data to rating agencies and accept changes to the methodology if the evidence supports them.

Ruto said financial rules are steering African pension savings towards government securities rather than infrastructure, even where regulations allow greater investment in projects.

He made the proposal Monday, September 21, at the Africa We Build High-Level Roundtable on regulation, risk and reward in New York. The Africa Finance Corporation (AFC) convened the event on the margins of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly.

Kenyan pension funds hold 46 per cent of their Sh3.2 trillion ($24.7 billion) in government securities but only 0.02 per cent in infrastructure debt, Ruto said. The rules allow pension funds to invest up to 10 per cent in infrastructure.

“Africa's problem is no longer the amount of capital available to it. Africa's problem is the set of rules that decide where that capital is allowed to go,” Ruto noted.

Ruto returned to an argument he made at the inaugural Africa We Build Summit in Nairobi in April, where he said African countries should use domestic capital to finance their own infrastructure.

At the New York roundtable, he revisited his earlier phrase, “he who pays the piper calls the tune”, using a teacher in Eldoret who has contributed to a pension fund for 20 years to illustrate his point.

“In Nairobi I said that he who pays the piper calls the tune. I meant it as a warning about depending on other people's money. This morning I mean it as an opportunity. The teacher in Eldoret is paying the piper. She has earned the right to call the tune,” Ruto explained.

He said the teacher's savings are more likely to sit in a US Treasury bill than in a nearby geothermal plant.

“Her fund manager is not being unpatriotic. He is being rational. The rules he works under tell him the Treasury bill is prudent and the power plant is adventurous. Capital follows incentives, and we wrote the incentives,” Ruto observed.

The Africa Finance Corporation's President and Chief Executive Samaila Zubairu framed the wider problem in similar terms at the Nairobi summit, saying Africa is “not capital-poor; it is capital-trapped.”

Ruto now wants African risk assessed using evidence from African markets rather than assumptions that he argues can make projects and countries appear more expensive to finance.

He said Kenya will make its pension and insurance regulators available to work with rating agencies, insurers and standard setters.

“If the evidence vindicates the current methodology, we will accept the finding and say so publicly. If it does not, we will expect the methodology to change,” Ruto added.

He proposed that the roundtable establish a working group based in Nairobi to continue the work and report to the next Africa We Build Summit in 12 months with findings backed by numbers.

President William Ruto on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York, USA. [PCS]

Ruto made four requests to rating agencies, insurers, regulators and other institutions involved in financing: price African risk against African experience, make insurance on productive assets affordable, end penalties on long-term assets in prudential and liquidity rules and build bankable project pipelines.

He said African non-bank domestic capital pools have passed $2 trillion, while external concessional and commercial flows to Africa totalled $1.7 trillion between 2014 and 2024.

Official development assistance has also fallen every year since 2020, Ruto said, arguing that Africa can no longer rely on external financing to meet its infrastructure needs.

Kenya has begun putting some of the proposed financing mechanisms in place.

Ruto said the National Infrastructure Fund, signed into law in March, aims to mobilise up to $40 billion for roads, ports, power and water without new public debt.

In May, Kenya listed its first infrastructure fund on the Nairobi Securities Exchange and raised Sh3.4 billion with United Kingdom support. Kenya also increased its equity in the Africa Finance Corporation by Sh3.25 billion ($25 million), Ruto said.

The president said Kenya was willing to expose its own financing system to scrutiny as part of the test.

“If the evidence supports the current methodology, we will accept it. If it does not, we will expect the methodology to change,” Ruto told the roundtable.

The broader goal, he said, is to make it as easy for African institutional investors to finance productive assets as it is to buy government debt.

“The day a Kenyan pension trustee can buy a Kenyan power station as easily as she buys a Treasury bill, this argument will be over,” Ruto said.

World.title: Ndindi Nyoro, Kinangop MP clash over alleged threatening message
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kiharu MP Ndindi Nyoro arrives at St Paul ACK church in Engineer Town for the service on September 20, 2026. [James Munyeki, Standard]

There was drama at St Paul ACK church in Engineer Town during service on Sunday after Kiharu MP Ndindi Nyoro clashed with Kinangop MP Zachary Kwenya Thuku over an alleged threatening message.

Thuku, who is allied to the Kenya Kwanza government led by President William Ruto, is said to have warned Nyoro against attending the service.

"Yesterday, I received a message from the MP for Kinangop, Kwenya Thuku, warning me not to attend the church service. If I am lying, let him come here and read the message he sent me," Nyoro said.

He challenged the Kinangop MP to read the message aloud to the congregation.

"If anything happens to me today, Kenyans will judge whoever will be responsible," said Nyoro.

The Kiharu MP challenged Thuku to face him at a public rally at Engineer Trading Centre.

When he rose to speak, the Kinangop MP said he would not address the matter in church.

Instead, he said this was a political issue that the leaders would resolve.

"Let us solve this matter amicably. We are all brothers in this political journey," he said amid cheers from the congregation.

Recently, Nyoro added his voice to the growing political realignment in Mt Kenya, openly acknowledging the political tightrope he now walks as he distances himself from his former allies in the ruling party.

In a candid interview, he admitted that his previous close ties with President William Ruto and the Kenya Kwanza administration have left him vulnerable to suspicion from both sides of the political divide but insisted his decision to abandon the ruling party, United Democratic Alliance (UDA) was deliberate, difficult, and necessary.

World.title: Ruto leaves for New York ahead of UN General Assembly
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Ruto leaves for New York ahead of 81st UN General Assembly. [PCS]

President William Ruto has departed for New York, United States, to attend the 81st United Nations General Assembly.

Ruto is expected to push Kenya’s investment agenda and advocate for increased financing for Africa.

According to a statement from State House, Ruto will use the global gathering to seek partnerships in energy, infrastructure, manufacturing, health, agriculture and technology.

He will also advance Kenya’s agenda on artificial intelligence and Africa’s participation in the global digital economy.

Ruto is expected to co-chair roundtables hosted by the Africa Finance Corporation (AFC) and Global Africa Business Initiative (GABI), alongside industrialist Aliko Dangote.

A key focus will be the planned Sh2.2 trillion East Africa Refinery in Lamu, which the government says will have a capacity of 700,000 barrels per day and create more than 60,000 jobs. The project is scheduled to break ground on September 30, 2026.

On artificial intelligence, Ruto and Finland President Alexander Stubb will co-lead the AI Middle Powers Initiative, which seeks to enable countries to pool computing resources, data and talent to build AI capabilities.

Kenya will also advance the Africa Development Bank-backed AI 10 billion initiative, which aims to mobilise up to 10 billion dollars by 2035 for investment in Africa’s artificial intelligence sector.

The President is further expected to sign a global declaration and roadmap on child online AI safety alongside leaders from Spain, the United Kingdom, Canada and Australia.

He will also launch an Africa Resilience Compact that will use artificial intelligence, satellite earth observation and predictive technologies to strengthen preparedness for El Niño and other climate shocks.

During his address to the UN General Assembly, Ruto is expected to champion an Africa-financing-Africa approach, calling for reforms and international guarantees to unlock more African capital for infrastructure and enterprise.

Ruto will also highlight Kenya’s National Infrastructure Fund, which the government says is designed to mobilise up to 40 billion dollars without adding to public debt.

On the sidelines of the General Assembly, the President is expected to hold meetings with heads of state and government, multilateral institutions and global corporations to discuss trade, investment and diplomatic cooperation.

He will also engage Kenyans living in the United States as the government advances a Diaspora Investment Platform intended to channel diaspora capital into productive investment in Kenya.

World.title: Egypt’s Fuel Automatic Pricing Committee to hold meeting on fuel prices on October: Source
World.content:
An official source revealed that the Fuel Automatic Pricing Committee (FAPC) will meet during the first week of October to review developments in petroleum product prices and determine new prices.

The source said that – prior to making any decision – the committee will examine global oil price trends, international and regional variables affecting energy markets, and factors related to the cost of supplying petroleum products, in preparation for setting the pricing policy during the anticipated meeting.

The assessment preceding the meeting aims to evaluate the overall dynamics of energy markets —particularly given the instability currently affecting global markets— and the potential impact of geopolitical developments on crude oil prices, as well as supply and energy costs.

Former Minister of Petroleum and current Head of the Senate Energy Committee, Osama Kamal, said that contracts for petroleum products will remain in effect until September 30.

Consequently, there will be no change in prices prior to that date.

He added that the pricing of petroleum products will be determined following the pricing committee’s meeting.

The committee does not convene unless there are enough fluctuations in crude oil prices to warrant a review, he noted.

Kamal emphasized that setting prices for petroleum products in the local market is not a unilateral decision by the Petroleum Ministry, but is based on a recommendation issued by the pricing committee with the final decision issued by the government.

The outlook for gasoline and diesel price trends in the coming period remains unclear, he said, given the ongoing wars and tensions in various parts of the world.

Kamal noted that any external developments regarding these issues could have a direct or indirect impact on energy markets.

He noted that the difficulty in predicting fuel prices for the near future stems primarily from the uncertainty surrounding the global geopolitical landscape.

Kamal explained that determining when lasting global stability might be achieved would better facilitate the forecasting of oil and petroleum product price trends, anticipating no significant changes in fuel prices in the immediate future.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Egypt reserves legitimate right to protect its water security
World.content:
Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly stressed that Egypt’s water security is an existential issue that allows for no compromise.

Speaking on behalf of President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi during the high-level general debate of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly, Madbouly added that the Nile is not merely an economic resource but a lifeline intertwined with the existence and historical development of Egyptian society.

Madbouly affirmed that Egypt reserves its legitimate right, guaranteed by the UN Charter and international law, to protect its water security and safeguard the existential assets of its people.

He stressed that while Egypt does not oppose any nation’s right to development, it firmly defends the principle that development must not come at the expense of harming others.

Shared resources cannot be managed through unilateral measures or a fait accompli policy but rather through cooperation, good neighborliness, and binding agreements in accordance with international law that preserve the legitimate rights and interests of all, the prime minister said.

Madbouly emphasized that cross-border water resources must serve as a domain for cooperation rather than conflict, noting that development in one nation must not come at the expense of harming others, advocating for binding agreements anchored in international law.

Madbouly also stressed that regional crises cannot be managed as isolated cases, warning against foreign interventions and the erosion of national state institutions.

Regarding the Palestinian issue, the Prime Minister called for a permanent ceasefire in Gaza, rejecting any displacement of Palestinians and reaffirming the goal of an independent Palestinian state based on the 1967 borders with East Jerusalem as its capital. On the Sudanese crisis, Madbouly reaffirmed Egypt’s unwavering support for Sudan’s unity, sovereignty, and state institutions.

Concluding Egypt’s remarks, Madbouly called for a genuine and comprehensive reform of the UN Security Council, particularly to address the historical injustice faced by Africa through the Ezulwini Consensus and Sirte Declaration.

He further underscored the urgent need to reform the global financial architecture, govern emerging technologies like artificial intelligence responsibly, and ensure a just green transition that supports developing nations.

Madbouly said the international system is facing challenges that require restoring trust, stressing the need for effective multilateralism in which every country has a voice and for an international system that fulfills its commitments and guarantees equality in sovereignty among states.

He stressed that the Palestinian issue is a prominent example of the flaws in the current international system.

“Our goal is clear—to establish an independent, sovereign Palestinian state,” he said.

The Prime Minister stressed the need to consolidate the ceasefire in Gaza in accordance with the Sharm El-Sheikh plan and US President Donald Trump’s plan.

World.title: FM urges return to dialogue, resumption of diplomatic track through US-Iran negotiations
World.content:
Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation and Egyptian Expatriates Badr Abdelatty stressed the need for the United States and Iran to resume dialogue and the diplomatic track through negotiations aimed at reaching an understanding, saying this is the only way to end the current crisis and halt the escalation that is causing serious harm to the interests of all countries in the region.

Abdelatty made the remarks during a meeting with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on the sidelines of the high-level segment of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly in New York.

Foreign Ministry Spokesman Nader Zaki said Friday that the meeting addressed the latest developments in the region, adding that the two ministers reviewed ongoing efforts and proposals aimed at reaching an agreement to contain tensions and de-escalate the situation.

Abdelatty underscored the vital importance of all countries assuming their responsibilities to ensure the safety and freedom of international navigation, in order to contain the crisis’s adverse impact on the global economy.

He noted that the crisis has significantly disrupted energy and fertilizer supply chains, as well as international trade.

The minister also stressed the importance of respecting the security and stability of the Gulf states and all countries across the region.

World.title: MSMEDA discusses participation in Arab-African Investment Summit
World.content:
The CEO of Egypt’s Micro, Small and Medium Enterprise Development Agency (MSMEDA) Mostafa Hassan held talks on Thursday, September 24, 2026, with a delegation from the Arab Women Investors Union headed by its President, Hoda Galal Yassa.

The meeting aims to discuss future cooperation in supporting small businesses, entrepreneurs, young people, and women.

Hassan also discussed the agency’s participation in the 2026 Arab-African Investment and International Cooperation Summit in Luxor.

MSMEDA CEO also outlined the agency’s plans to work more closely with civil society organizations and institutions involved in developing the business environment.

He stated that MSMEDA plans to help more small businesses reach export markets by opening new domestic and international marketing channels for Egyptian products and improving their competitiveness.

The agency will also work with development partners to address challenges facing small businesses and help them become more capable of attracting private investment.

Its plans include wider use of modern technology to increase productivity, support knowledge-based businesses and help entrepreneurs turn new ideas into commercially viable projects.

During the meeting, Yassa invited Hassan to participate in the Arab-African Investment and International Cooperation Summit, scheduled to take place in Luxor from October 18 to 22.

The summit, organized by the Arab Women Investors Union, is expected to bring together delegations representing 43 countries.

Yassa affirmed that cooperation with MSMEDA could include vocational training linked to employment opportunities, particularly in the industrial and tourism sectors.

The two sides also discussed entrepreneurship programs and training to improve the skills of workers in small and medium-sized businesses and help Egyptian products compete in foreign markets.

World.title: Egyptian, Omani FMs discuss Iran crisis, Red Sea, Bab al-Mandeb developments
World.content:
Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation and Egyptian Expatriates Badr Abdelatty met, Friday, September 25, 2026, with Omani Foreign Minister Badr bin Hamad Al Busaidi to discuss bilateral relations, Iran Crisis, the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandeb developments.

The meeting took place on the sidelines of the high-level segment of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly in New York.

Foreign Ministry spokesperson Nader Zaki said Friday that the meeting addressed bilateral relations between Egypt and Oman and ways to further develop and strengthen them across various fields, reflecting the deep-rooted historical ties between the two countries and their brotherly peoples.

The discussions focused in particular on trade and economic cooperation, as well as continued communication and consultations at various levels to exchange views and assessments on key regional and international issues of mutual concern.

The two ministers also discussed regional developments, including the situation in the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandeb.

Abdelatty stressed the need to prioritize de-escalation and avoid any steps that could further fuel tensions or threaten regional security and stability.

He underscored the importance of ensuring freedom of navigation in accordance with international law in a manner that contributes to safeguarding regional and international security and stability.

Abdelatty reiterated Egypt’s categorical rejection of any threat to the security of Saudi Arabia and reaffirmed Egypt’s full solidarity with the Kingdom in safeguarding its sovereignty and stability.

He stressed the importance of allowing diplomatic efforts to proceed, stressing that diplomacy remains the appropriate means of addressing challenges.

The ministers also discussed the Iranian crisis and developments in the Strait of Hormuz, exchanging views on Oman’s efforts, in coordination with Egypt and other mediators, to de-escalate tensions.

They stressed the need to safeguard the safety and security of maritime navigation and ensure the uninterrupted flow of trade and energy supplies, which would help mitigate the repercussions of current tensions and promote regional stability.

World.title: Here’s everything you need to know about when Egypt will shift to winter time
World.content:
Winter closing times for public shops, restaurants, and cafes came into effect on Friday, September 25—a change that impacts working hours, school schedules, public transport, and various other daily activities linked to the country’s official time.

Citizens are anticipating the return to winter time in 2026—and the end of daylight saving time—in the coming weeks.

When will winter time begin?

Daylight saving time ends at the close of Thursday, October 29 and winter time begins on Friday, October 30.

The transition to winter time is achieved by setting the clock back 60 minutes at the scheduled time of the change.

Date of the clock change

At midnight marking the end of Thursday, October 29 the clock is set back by one full hour—shifting from 12:00 AM (midnight) to 11:00 pm—thereby initiating winter time.

As of September 25, approximately 35 days remain until the end of Daylight Saving Time and the return to winter time in Egypt.

Each year, Daylight Saving Time remains in effect from the last Friday of April until the end of the last Thursday of October.

Why does Egypt implement Daylight Saving Time?

The implementation of Daylight Saving Time is linked to making greater use of daylight hours during the summer months by advancing the clock by 60 minutes.

This time-adjustment system is also part of measures aimed at rationalizing energy consumption and reducing the use of electricity and fuel during specific times of the day.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Mall of Egypt to close at three pm on Saturday
World.content:
The management of the Mall of Egypt in 6th of October City has announced a change in visitor hours for Saturday, September 26, setting three pm as when the mall will close to the public.

Management clarified that the scheduled closure on Saturday afternoon is temporary; the mall will stop admitting visitors at three pm and remain closed for the rest of the day.

Consequently, the public will not be able to enter after this time, coinciding with a private event taking place at the venue.

The management apologized to visitors for any inconvenience caused by the temporary adjustment to the mall’s operating hours this Saturday, explaining that the temporary closure is intended to facilitate preparations for a special event.

The management urged visitors to take note of this exceptional schedule change and plan their visits accordingly—keeping the specific closing time in mind—to avoid any inconvenience resulting from the altered operating hours.

Mall of Egypt’s management confirmed that regular operating hours will resume on Sunday, September 27, allowing visitors to access the mall and enjoy its various services as usual.

World.title: We aren’t trying to kill Trump, Iran’s president insists to reporters at New York hotel
World.content:
New York — Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian’s media appearances in Iran are tightly controlled affairs.

But on Thursday he sat down to face questions from a group of journalists in New York, where despite being the leader of a country at war with the United States, he is visiting with the protection of the US Secret Service.

In the wide-ranging session, a day after addressing the UN General Assembly, Pezeshkian repeated familiar Iranian positions on the war, its nuclear program and dissent in Iran. He also talked about the effect of sanctions on the Iranian people, and claimed Iran would never try to kill Donald Trump – despite the president and US authorities accusing the regime of plotting his assassination.

The comments were made at the Millennium Hilton hotel, a stone’s throw from the UN headquarters where the Iranian president declared Wednesday that his country “will not bow down” as the war with the US drags on.

In the briefing, Pezeshkian also described recent meetings he had held with Iran’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, who has not been seen in public since the outset of the war, saying that the leader was “quite healthy.”

There has been mounting speculation in recent months over Khamenei’s health, after he was understood to have sustained serious injuries in the US-Israeli attack that killed his father and predecessor Ali Khamenei at the beginning of the conflict in February.

Speaking about Khamenei’s condition, Pezeshkian said, “I did not see any major challenges with his health or physical appearance,” adding that their most recent in-person meeting had taken place around one month ago and lasted around seven hours.

Pezeshkian said the pair had sat on pillows on the ground and stood up to walk around during the meeting. US intelligence assesses that despite his injuries Khamenei is still playing a critical role in shaping war strategy alongside senior Iranian officials, multiple sources familiar with the intelligence said in May.

A meeting in Manhattan

The presence of Iran’s delegation in a country with which it remains at war is already virtually unprecedented.

But this spectacle became increasingly unconventional on Thursday when the Iranian president and Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi briefed reporters including from CNN in a hotel function room in Midtown Manhattan.

Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi arrives during the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly on September 22, 2026 in New York City. Alexi J. Rosenfeld/Getty Images

A State Department official said earlier this week that the visiting Iranian delegates were “being admitted to the United States strictly for the purpose of representing the Islamic Republic of Iran before the United Nations” and that they must “restrict their activities to United Nations-related business only.”

The Iranians “must seek and receive approval in advance” from the State Department if they want to travel outside the vicinity of the UN headquarters, John F. Kennedy International Airport or Iran’s UN mission facilities, the official said.

In the briefing, Pezeshkian denied accusations that Iran was trying to kill the president, saying it has “never been the position [of the Iranian government], overtly or covertly, to seek to assassinate Trump or his family members.”

Last month, the US Secret Service said it was aware of a video aired by Iran’s state broadcaster appearing to threaten the life of Barron Trump, the president’s youngest son. This came after Israel shared intelligence with the US that Iran had devised a plan to assassinate Donald Trump. In late 2024, the US Justice Department announced federal charges over what it described as a thwarted Iranian plot to kill Trump before the presidential election.

Hard-line Iranian media have repeatedly featured content threatening the life of Trump and his family. During funeral events for the late Khamenei in July, regime loyalists were seen holding posters with the words “Kill Trump.” Trump has publicly discussed the Iranian threats on his life too, saying in July: “I’m on whatever list … so far, I guess I’ve been a bit lucky, but maybe that doesn’t last very long. These are evil, sick people.”

In response to Pezeshkian’s comments, White House spokesperson Anna Kelly said, “The Iranian regime has murdered thousands of its own people, killed Americans overseas, executed acts of terrorism in the Strait of Hormuz, and launched indiscriminate attacks against its neighbors in the region.”

“The president is courageously ensuring that such an evil country never possesses a nuclear weapon, which will make the entire world safer and more stable,” Kelly said.

‘We have problems’

Pezeshkian also discussed the domestic challenges facing Iran. US sanctions and the ongoing war have suffocated the country’s economy, sparking prices increases and shortages of basic necessities.

The Iranian president also said in the session that Iran wants a deal, but that any agreement was not related to the timing of the US midterms.

Separately, also on Thursday, Araghchi said Iran had presented a proposal to the US that — according to Iran — would re-open the Strait of Hormuz and restart negotiations toward a “final deal.”

The proposal, presented to the US through mediators this week, calls for the US to meet certain conditions within seven days to restart the talks and re-open the strait, Araghchi said. The foreign minister declined to elaborate on the conditions but said that they were “nothing more” than what was included in the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding.

That agreement, which was reached by the two countries in June, included provisions on sanctions relief; the release of frozen assets; and a cessation of military operations, including in Lebanon.

In response to Araghchi’s comments, a White House official told CNN they were having “positive and constructive discussions through the mediators.”

People walk on a street in Tehran, Iran, September 23, 2026. Majid Asgaripour/Wana News Agency/Reuters

Iran’s economy was in a dire state even before the war began, with the poor conditions a key driving factor behind the anti-regime demonstrations which kicked off in the Iranian capital city Tehran in 2025.

“We have problems. Unprecedentedly difficult problems,” Pezeshkian told reporters Thursday, while referring to US sanctions as a “silent murderous campaign.”

Much like in his Wednesday address to world leaders, Pezeshkian appeared confident in the briefing that Iran would prevail despite the challenges facing his country. He also insisted that US bases in the region were legitimate targets as they had been used to attack Iran.

“Most of the American bases in the region are no longer useable,” he claimed.

Iranian strikes damaged and destroyed hundreds of buildings and structures at US bases across the Middle East region during the war’s first months, according to an official Pentagon watchdog report released earlier this month.

“Of course, the US has the power to destroy anything anywhere, but it is impossible to bring about Iranian surrender,” Pezeshkian said.

World.title: Chipolopolo will bounce back against Togo – Lwandamina
World.content:
Coach George Lwandamina is banking on home advantage to revive Zambia’s AFCON 2027 qualification hopes after injuries and mistakes condemned Chipolopolo to a 3-1 defeat in Algeria.

Zambia’s campaign got off to a false start on Friday night at the packed Hocine Aït Ahmed Stadium, where Algeria punished a brave but inexperienced Chipolopolo side.

Despite the loss, Lwandamina insisted his young team fought to the end in a hostile atmosphere.

“It was a tough match and the boys played well. Away from home, it wasn’t easy for them, but they fought to the bitter end,” he said.

The Chipolopolo mentor was candid about what went wrong. Algeria took an early lead through Jaouen Hadjam after just two minutes, and after Fashion Sakala equalised in the 57th minute, Ibrahim Maza and Anis Hadj Moussa struck in the 67th and 72nd minutes.

“Few mistakes, of course, and we were punished. Injuries also affected us. We had to make changes which we wouldn’t have made, and that cost us the game,” Lwandamina admitted.

With Togo beating Burundi 1-0 in Lomé to join Algeria on three points, Zambia are now bottom of Group I. But Lwandamina issued a stern warning ahead of Monday’s home clash.

“Definitely, we need to win our home games if we are to qualify. Togo won’t have it easy,” he said.

The former ZESCO United and Yanga tactician believes his youthful squad will only get better.

“This is a young team and they are coping very well. We can actually change the tables. The boys are fighting very hard and, with a little bit of experience in the team, I’m sure we’ll be able to bring them together.”

He also paid tribute to Algeria’s depth, describing them as a football powerhouse.

“Algeria enjoyed their game. They played well. Algeria has a new team, mind you, Algeria is one of the big countries in the world, so the population is very big and you have more options of players out there. You can even make 10 teams here in Algeria.”

Zambia host Togo on September 29 at Levy Mwanawasa Stadium in Ndola, where only victory will keep their qualification bid alive.

World.title: Njobvu Says Judiciary Dented Its Reputation by Closing Courts After the Election
World.content:
Democratic Union leader Ackim Njobvu has said the Judiciary dented its own reputation when it closed courts after the disputed general election, and that it will be difficult for the institution to erase the effect on citizens’ access to justice.

Mr Njobvu said the damage was greatest at a time when people needed the courts most, particularly during the election. In an interview, he said the Judiciary must now work harder to restore public confidence and ensure citizens can exercise their constitutional rights.

He questioned whether denying citizens access to the courts was consistent with the responsibility to uphold justice.

“When you are closing courts, when you are denying people justice, when people needed to petition you close the courts. People lost trust and confidence in such institutions,” Mr Njobvu said.

The Judiciary, he said, should take steps to restore its reputation and prevent citizens from losing confidence in the country’s justice system. He addressed it directly.

“You have to respond to this. You have to redeem yourselves. You have dented your reputation as a Judiciary. Zambians have no respect and trust in this dented Judiciary,” he said.

Mr Njobvu also pointed to major judicial decisions on the eligibility of the late former president Edgar Lungu and on constitutional amendments. The Judiciary’s handling of such matters, he said, should be examined against its previous decisions.

He said citizens should be allowed to exercise their constitutional rights, including access to the courts, and closed with an appeal.

“What I would love to appeal is that where we are right now, let’s accord citizens the opportunity to access the courts. Let’s accord citizens the opportunity to exercise their rights,” Mr Njobvu said.

He then turned to the losing candidates of the United Party for National Development (UPND). Mr Njobvu questioned their decision to challenge the results of the polls after the ruling party had described the elections as free and fair.

World.title: Hichilema Dismisses Talk of Crisis, Warns Social Media Users Against Scaring Off Investors
World.content:
Hichilema Dismisses Talk of Crisis, Warns Social Media Users Against Scaring Off Investors

President Hakainde Hichilema has rejected claims that Zambia is in crisis after the polls, saying disgruntled and selfish individuals are creating a false impression of tension and scaring off the investors the Government has worked to attract.

The President spoke at State House in Lusaka yesterday during the swearing-in of Patricia Malaila as Deputy Auditor-General for the Audit Division at the Office of the Auditor-General. He used the occasion to question the motives of people, at home and abroad, who use social media to portray the country in a bad light, and he opened with an appeal.

“Let’s love our country; let’s not do things that damage our country consciously,” Mr Hichilema said.

He follows what is posted online, he said, and some of it is doing harm without those posting it realising. The Head of State then put the question to them directly.

“I scan social media, the kind of stuff that is thrown in there, you don’t realise what you are doing; you are scaring off an investor we have worked so hard to attract. What is your intention?” he asked.

The effect of such posts, the President said, is to make investors, whether domestic, regional or international, believe that something is wrong in Zambia. Nothing is, he insisted, and the country had already settled the matter at the ballot box.

“There is no issue in this country. We have had an election, Zambians voted, decisions are made by Zambians. We move on. What is this hullabaloo, creating a crisis where there is none?” he said.

Some of the people painting the country in a negative light had selfish interests, he said, because they were unhappy that they did not occupy certain public offices. Citizens who claim to love Zambia, he added, should stop peddling falsehoods, and he then turned to what follows when the law is crossed.

“Let us not have that mentality; let’s love this country, focus on the work ahead of us, let’s stay within the law. If you veer off the law, then you will pay. It doesn’t matter how old you are; the law does not recognise age, it recognises wrongdoing,” he said.

The appeal was not limited to those at home. Zambians living abroad were urged to remain law-abiding and to avoid conduct that could harm the country’s reputation.

The office he holds also featured in the address. State House, the President said, must stay focused on government business and national development, and he asked that it not be turned into something else.

“Let’s not dilute this office and make it something else, this office is sacred; it’s for serious work,” he said.

At the same ceremony, the Head of State called on public officers to treat public money with care, saying every kwacha saved is critical to the success of the Grow Zambia Agenda.

On the economy, Mr Hichilema said falling inflation and rising growth were evidence that the country was moving in the right direction. He asked citizens to support efforts to sustain the momentum.

Figures from the Zambia Statistics Agency (ZamStats) show inflation at 6.2 per cent in August, down from 6.5 per cent in July. The President said the country had come a long way from the high inflation levels recorded when he assumed office in 2021.

Growth was the second marker he pointed to. ZamStats data show the economy expanded by 7.7 per cent in the first quarter of 2026, compared with 4.5 per cent in the same period last year, and he urged Zambians to read the signs.

“You must read the writing on the wall, there’s something good happening in this country and be part of that good,” the President said.

Citizens were asked to recognise the progress made so far and to contribute to the implementation of the Grow Zambia Agenda. Careless actions, he warned, could undermine the gains being recorded, and he closed with a final appeal.

“Let us accelerate this growth, let us not damage the growth by our carelessness as citizens. Then we will show love to this nation called Zambia,” he said.

The latest ZamStats monthly bulletin, released on Thursday, puts second-quarter growth at 7.2 per cent, slightly below the 7.9 per cent recorded in the same quarter of 2025. It also shows annual inflation easing to 6.1 per cent in September from 6.2 per cent in August.

World.title: Police Say Kalumba Was Lawfully Arrested as Opposition Alleges Abduction and UPND Condemns His Remarks
World.content:
Police have rejected claims that former minister Dr Katele Kalumba was abducted, saying he was lawfully apprehended in Chienge and charged with harassment under the Cyber Crimes Act for allegedly publishing content meant to humiliate President Hakainde Hichilema.

Police spokesperson Godfrey Chilabi said in a statement that Dr Kalumba was apprehended on 23 September in Chienge, in Luapula Province. He was formally charged the following day at Kabwe Central Police Station.

The charge is harassment under Section 22 of the Cyber Crimes Act No. 4 of 2025. Police say it relates to content Dr Kalumba allegedly published on 11 August to humiliate the President.

The statement followed claims from the opposition that the arrest was an abduction. We Are One Zambia (WOZA) and Tonse-Pamodzi Alliance secretary general Muhabi Lungu said Dr Kalumba’s wife described the arrest as an abduction by heavily armed soldiers and police, who did not explain why they were taking him or where.

When the arrest was announced, Mr Lungu said, ruling party supporters dismissed it as fake. That forced the wife to make a recording.

Mr Lungu said it was laughable that Dr Kalumba was bundled into a military vehicle in Chienge and driven all the way to Kabwe, in Central Province, only to face charges. He said the journey fitted a pattern he described as a new punishment tactic, using jurisdiction as a weapon.

“Dr Kalumba was transferred all the way from Chiengi to Kabwe because a Kabwe resident allegedly complained. So, we can speculate that we will all be arrested and transported to a distant district for prosecution as punishment. Same with Mundubile and Makebi. From Kabwe, now Solwezi,” he said.

The two men he named, treason-accused opposition leaders Brian Mundubile and Makebi Zulu, were moved from Kabwe to Solwezi, where they appeared in the Magistrates Court on Friday on sedition charges. Mr Lungu said the transfers showed the same law being abused.

He went further, saying the continued arrests and clampdown on opponents and critics were meant to stoke fear and silence dissent. The aim, he said, was to lay the ground for a third term for the President and make him untouchable.

Mr Lungu also accused the United Party for National Development (UPND) Government of repealing the offence of defaming the President from the Penal Code, only to smuggle it back in a stronger and more punitive form through the sedition and cyber laws.

“Essentially, if you offer constructive criticism to the President, you are abducted and booked for sedition or cyber harassment,” he said.

He warned that the conduct of the Government amounted to the militarisation of politics, with Zambia projected as a constitutional democracy but policed like a military state.

“There is no remorse from the perpetrators of this crackdown. One has to ask: Are these arrests meant to create fear so that the President becomes unaccountable to anyone?” Mr Lungu said.

The ruling party took a different view of the matter. UPND deputy spokesperson Elvis Nkandu strongly condemned remarks attributed to Dr Kalumba against the President, describing them as regrettable and entirely out of step with constructive national discourse.

Mr Nkandu was referring to a video now circulating on social media in which the former minister makes disparaging remarks and issues threats against the President. The video is believed to have been made before the general election.

Citizens are free to express personal views, Mr Nkandu said, but such freedoms must be exercised with responsibility and deep respect for vital State institutions, particularly the presidency.

He expressed disappointment that a veteran figure of Dr Kalumba’s stature, a former senior public servant and prominent politician, would resort to disrespectful rhetoric. That was especially so, he said, given the history of his relationship with the current administration.

Dr Kalumba was imprisoned for corruption in 2022. President Hichilema pardoned him on medical grounds, and he was released from prison on 1 August 2023.

Mr Nkandu said that act of mercy should never be misconstrued as weakness.

“President Hichilema had every opportunity to approach the matter purely from a political perspective, but he instead demonstrated humanity and compassion,” he said.

He also issued a stern warning against attempts to promote regionalism and tribal divisions. The presidency belongs to all citizens, he said, and political disagreements should never be allowed to erode national unity.

Healthy criticism of Government policy is welcome, Mr Nkandu said, but it should not compromise the dignity of the Head of State. He urged Dr Kalumba to use his extensive political experience to contribute constructively to national development rather than divisive commentary.

Police maintain that Dr Kalumba was lawfully apprehended on 23 September and formally charged the next day at Kabwe Central Police Station.

World.title: Chipolopolo fall in Algeria
World.content:
Captain Fashion Sakala was on target but Zambia launched the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign with a 3-1 loss to Algeria in Group I.

Algeria posted a well deserved win after dominating both halves at the Hocine Aït Ahmed Stadium.

The home side started on a promising note when Jaouen Hadjam opened the scoring just after two minutes.

Algeria went into the half time break leading 1-0 after wasting some decent chances.

Saudi Arabia based Sakala equalised 12 minutes after the break to make it 1-1.

But Algeria bounced back in front after 67 minutes when Ibrahim Maza beat Zambia keeper Willard Mwanza from inside the box.

Winger Anis Hadj Moussa sealed the win in the 72nd minute with Algeria’s third.

The result puts Algeria top of Group I on three points on goal difference after Match Day One, while Zambia are bottom.

In the other Group I match played today, Togo made a winning start with a 1-0 victory over Burundi at the Kégué Stadium in Lomé.

Karim Dermane scored the only goal in the 17th minute to give the Sparrow Hawks all three points.

Togo controlled the first half and held on in the second, with Burundi unable to find an equalizer.

Group I Table After Match Day 1:

1. Algeria – 3 pts (+2)

2. Togo – 3 pts (+1)

3. Burundi – 0 pts (-1)

4. Zambia – 0 pts (-2)

Togo now travel to face Zambia on 29th September, while Burundi host Algeria on the same day.

World.title: President Hichilema urges prudent use of public resources
World.content:
President Hakainde Hichilema has sworn-in Patricia Malaila as Deputy Auditor General Audits, in the office of the Auditor General.

Speaking during the swearing-in-ceremony at State House, President Hichilema highlighted the significance of the utilisation of public resources and the timely delivery of audits.

“Accountability is crucial, all of us in public office must understand that we are accountable to the people of Zambia in what we do and superintending on resources that are available to us,” Mr Hichilema said.

President Hichilema further said the Office of Deputy Auditor General Audits, plays an important role to the citizens of Zambia.

The Head of State said accountability is crucial and everyone has a duty to comply with utilising resources in the most efficient and effective way.

“As Deputy Auditor General Audits, we expect you and your team to deliver audits on a timely basis,” Mr Hichilema said.

The President said audits should be delivered and concluded on time.

Mr Hichilema has since urged Ms Malaila to identify institutional weaknesses that require remedy, stating that this will help in the improvement of the use of public resources.

And newly sworn in Deputy Auditor General Audits, Patricia Malaila, said her office is committed to ensuring that real time audits are done.

“We will ensure that audits are done as an event is happening to prevent mistakes other than correcting after a mistake has been made,” Ms Malaila said.

Ms Malaila added that resources will be utilized accordingly, adding that every cent will be accounted for.

She said audits that will have an impact on the lives of people will be conducted so that the citizens can benefit.

World.title: Zambia records 16,500 new cancer cases annually
World.content:
University Teaching Hospital (UTH) Cancer Diseases Hospital (CDH) has disclosed that Zambia records approximately 16,500 new cancer cases and 9,700 cancer-related deaths annually, with cervical cancer accounting for the highest number of cases.

UTH-CDH Acting Senior Medical Superintendent, Paul Kamfwa, says the country records about 4,700 new cervical cancer cases every year, with more than half of the affected patients dying from the disease.

Dr Kamfwa made the remarks during a community cleaning exercise conducted by Zambia Correctional Service Officers to commemorate Africa Corrections Day at the Cancer Diseases Hospital in Lusaka.

He disclosed that about 3,000 of the 16,500 cancer patients recorded countrywide are currently receiving treatment at the hospital.

Meanwhile, Zambia Correctional Service Commissioner-General, Fredrick Chilukutu said the Service is committed to community engagement as part of efforts to promote safer and more resilient communities.

Mr Chilukutu, represented by ZCS Deputy Commissioner-General, Crispin Kaonga said correctional facilities should not only focus on custody but also equip inmates with skills, healthcare, education and opportunities for successful reintegration into society.

He also highlighted the need to strengthen healthcare services in correctional facilities through medical screening, disease prevention, health education and access to treatment.

Mr Chilukutu said the Service is placing greater emphasis on the mental health and overall well-being of inmates and correctional officers.

He has called for continued collaboration among government institutions, development partners, civil society organisations and regional correctional services to improve correctional management.
