World.title: Remote Osa Eco-Lodge Playa Cativo Joins Small Luxury Hotels of the World
World.content:
Playa Cativo Lodge, a secluded beachfront retreat on the Golfo Dulce in Costa Rica’s Southern Zone, has been admitted into Small Luxury Hotels of the World, the international collection of independently owned boutique properties. The addition gives the Southern Zone yet another foothold in one of the best-known names in independent luxury hospitality.

Founded in 2012, the lodge sits within a private rainforest reserve of roughly 400 hectares (1,000 acres) surrounded by Piedras Blancas National Park, a protected area that once formed part of Corcovado National Park. There is no road to the property. Guests fly into Golfito or Puerto Jiménez and finish the trip with a boat ride of about 30 minutes or arrive by helicopter. The crossing often brings sightings of dolphins and, in season, whales. On land, visitors share the grounds with toucans, scarlet macaws, monkeys and sloths.

The lodge has 18 rooms, ranging from ocean-view guest rooms to casitas with private plunge pools and a family villa. The rooms are designed to stay open to the surrounding forest, and most rely on breezes off the gulf rather than air conditioning, though some room types now offer it.

The property also offers wellness activities and a kitchen built around local ingredients, part of which come from the lodge’s own organic farm. Management says more than 95% of the land is devoted to conservation and that the reserve strengthens the protection of neighboring Piedras Blancas. The operation also relies on renewable energy, organic agriculture, recycling and the elimination of single-use plastics.

The Golfo Dulce itself became Latin America’s first Whale Heritage Site in 2023, a World Cetacean Alliance designation for places where communities protect whales and dolphins. Humpback whales from both hemispheres use the gulf to give birth and nurse their calves.

General manager Kenneth Hidalgo said joining the collection recognizes a style of hospitality rooted in independence, privacy, authenticity and a deep sense of place. He added that conservation stands as one of the lodge’s central pillars, treated as part of the luxury itself and as something guests are invited to take part in.

Hidalgo also said the membership is a chance for international travelers to discover Osa and the Golfo Dulce as one of the world’s great nature and luxury destinations. The lodge describes the surrounding wilderness not as a backdrop but as the reason the property exists. Small Luxury Hotels of the World, known as SLH, has spent more than 35 years building a portfolio of independent boutique hotels and now counts more than 700 properties in over 100 countries.

Its members average around 50 rooms, and the company says it personally visits and vets every hotel before admission and inspects members annually. The company is owned and led by siblings Daniel Shamoon and Jennica Shamoon Arazi. It has been expanding quickly, adding 29 hotels in the first three months of 2026 alone.

Membership carries real commercial weight. Through a partnership with Hilton, more than 550 participating SLH hotels can be booked through Hilton’s own channels, putting small independent properties in front of the chain’s loyalty members. SLH also runs its own complimentary guest loyalty program, The Club by SLH.

Playa Cativo joins a Costa Rican roster that includes Tabacón Thermal Resort and Spa in La Fortuna, Rio Perdido in Bagaces, Hotel Nantipa in Santa Teresa, Los Altos Resort in Manuel Antonio, Alta Las Palomas in San José and Hotel Three Sixty in Ojochal de Osa. It is the only member of the collection on the shores of the Golfo Dulce.

The news caps a strong run for the lodge. It earned a place in Tripadvisor’s 2025 Travelers’ Choice Best of the Best awards, ranking fourth among luxury hotels in both Costa Rica and Central America, and says it was honored again in the 2026 edition. For the Southern Zone, which remains far less developed than Guanacaste or the Central Pacific, the recognition adds to a growing reputation among travelers willing to go the extra distance for remote, nature-based luxury.

World.title: Costa Rica Changes Route 1 Traffic Pattern Near San Ramón
World.content:
Drivers using Route 1 between the Central Valley and Puntarenas is facing a new traffic pattern today as construction continues around San Ramón. The biggest change effects motorists going from San José toward Puntarenas. Instead of continuing straight through the construction area, drivers must go through the San Ramón access road, follow Route 135 and then reconnect with Route 1 after passing the work zone.

Those coming from Puntarenas toward San Ramón will continue using the temporary side road that was put into service several weeks ago. People leaving San Ramón for San José can continue along the San Ramón access road, take Route 156 and use the roundabout to return toward the capital.

The changes are expected to stay in place through December while crews work on the La Unión tunnel and a new two-level interchange at the entrance to San Ramón. For anyone heading from San José toward Puntarenas or the northern Pacific, you should pay particularly close attention once approaching San Ramón since the route is still open but don’t expect the normal path through the area.

This latest change is part of a larger traffic plan that has been in place around San Ramón since earlier this month. Construction has required vehicles to move onto temporary roads while crews carry out excavation, build support structures and expand the tunnel beneath Route 1. The Ministry of Public Works and Transport has previously asked drivers to keep their speed at no more than 30 kilometers per hour, about 19 mph, through the construction zone. Officials have also warned motorists to expect delays while the work continues.

When finished it should improve one of the main ways of getting to San Ramón and remove the current road-level crossing between Route 1 and local traffic. Construction on the interchange was about 25% complete in August, with the overall project valued at roughly $10.8 million and financed through a loan from the Inter-American Development Bank.

The San Ramón area is already a regular trouble spot for drivers heading west from the Central Valley, particularly on weekends and holidays when traffic builds toward Puntarenas and Guanacaste. The construction means travelers should leave extra time and rely on posted signs rather than assuming their usual Route 1 path will be available.

The temporary traffic setup is scheduled to remain through December, although separate work on the La Unión tunnel has previously been expected to continue into January 2027.

World.title: Atlantic Reaches Late September Without a Hurricane for the First Time Since 1914
World.content:
The Atlantic Ocean has reached late September without producing a single hurricane, something that has not happened in 112 years. As of this morning, the U.S. National Hurricane Center was tracking Tropical Storm Fay southwest of the Azores and a disturbance south of the Cabo Verde Islands. Neither had reached hurricane strength, and no hurricane has formed in the Atlantic this season.

The last season to go this deep into September without a hurricane was 1914, and that season never produced one at all. In records dating to 1851, only 1907 and 1914 finished without a hurricane. Both predate satellite tracking, so some storms from that era may have gone undetected.

The 2026 season has produced six named storms, Arthur, Bertha, Cristobal, Dolly, Edouard and Fay. None reached hurricane strength, which requires sustained winds of 119 km/h (74 mph). That is far below a typical year as the first Atlantic hurricane usually forms by Aug. 11, and by this point the basin would normally have produced about 10 named storms, four hurricanes and two major hurricanes, based on 1991–2020 averages.

The storms that did form were weak and short-lived. Accumulated cyclone energy, a measure that combines the strength and duration of every storm in a season, stood at 6.2 on Sept. 22, about 93% below normal for the date, according to the hurricane center. The main reason is El Niño. The warming of the equatorial Pacific strengthens upper-level winds over the Atlantic and Caribbean, and that wind shear tears developing storms apart before they can organize and intensify.

Forecasters expected a quiet year. In its August update, the U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration gave a 75% chance of a below-normal season, with seven to 13 named storms and two to six hurricanes. The season is not over. It officially runs until Nov. 30, and late September and October have historically produced dangerous storms, especially in the Gulf and along the U.S. East Coast.

Here in Costa Rica, the same El Niño is having a very different effect. The National Meteorological Institute has declared a meteorological drought across the Pacific slope and Central Valley, where rainfall is running up to 37% below normal and community water systems in 74 communities are rationing water.

Costa Rica rarely takes a direct hit from Atlantic hurricanes. Storms passing through the Caribbean have more often affected the country indirectly by pulling heavy rain across it, as Tropical Storm Nate did in 2017. The eastern Pacific has been far more active. Hurricane Polo regained Category 5 strength off Mexico’s Pacific coast with sustained winds of 260 km/h (162 mph), and the hurricane center was also issuing advisories today on Hurricane Odaly but neither storm is expected to affect Costa Rica.

If the Atlantic stays quiet through the end of November, 2026 would become only the third season on record without a hurricane.

World.title: Ashema Chang charged after allegedly burning down Eugene Thompson’s house and leaving him homeless; Court orders psychiatric evaluation
World.content:
Ashema Chang charged after allegedly burning down Eugene Thompson’s house and leaving him homeless; Court orders psychiatric evaluation

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Eugene Thompson says he lost his home, belongings and virtually everything he owned when fire destroyed his Belama Phase 5 residence just one day after he was ordered to leave the property amid a domestic dispute with Ashema Chang. Now, Chang has appeared before the Belize City Magistrate’s Court in connection with the dispute, but her arraignment was halted after the Chief Magistrate determined that she was not in a condition to enter a plea and ordered that she undergo a psychiatric evaluation.

Chang, 25, was brought before Court #1 on Tuesday, September 22, on a charge stemming from the case. During the hearing, however, she reportedly identified herself as “Erica,” appeared uncertain about where she was living and gave responses that caused the Chief Magistrate to question whether she understood the proceedings.

The court therefore did not take a plea and ordered that Chang be evaluated before the matter proceeds.

The case is linked to the September 15 fire that completely destroyed Thompson’s home at #5217 Belama Phase 5. Thompson, 43, told police he had lived at the property for about five years and estimated the house alone at approximately $45,000, excluding appliances, tools and other belongings lost in the blaze. The house was not insured.

Thompson had been served with a protection order the previous day and said he complied with the court’s direction to leave the residence while Chang remained there. He later told police that, days before the fire, Chang had allegedly sent him a threatening voice message referring to the house being burned.

Police subsequently sought Chang for questioning and later detained her. According to the information provided in the court matter, she was charged with threat to damage property.

At Tuesday’s hearing, the Chief Magistrate questioned Chang about whether she had previously visited a clinic or taken medication. A sister who was present told the court that Chang had recently seen a doctor and had previously been prescribed medication, although she could not provide details.

The Chief Magistrate ordered Chang’s family to have her undergo a psychiatric evaluation and obtain information on her medical history before the case continues.

Rather than remanding her to prison, the court granted Chang bail of $300 plus one surety of the same amount. She met bail and is scheduled to return to court on November 13, 2026.

The cause of the September 15 fire has not been publicly established, and the allegations against Chang remain before the court.

World.title: ‘The Devil This Time Used Meh’: Security guard fined $800 after caught on camera stealing $2,000 motorcycle
World.content:
‘The Devil This Time Used Meh’: Security guard fined $800 after caught on camera stealing $2,000 motorcycle

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A Belize City security guard who admitted stealing a $2,000 motorcycle told a Magistrate that “the devil this time used me” as he pleaded for leniency in court on Friday.

Twenty-six-year-old Jaimie Adrian Fuller, a security guard employed with Fort Point Security Company, appeared unrepresented in the Belize City Magistrate’s Court, where he pleaded guilty to a single charge of theft.

Fuller was accused of stealing a green Lifan motorcycle valued at $2,000 from Patrick Martinez on September 16, 2026.

According to the prosecution’s case, Martinez had left the damaged motorcycle near a laundromat on Freetown Road. When he later checked for it, the motorcycle was gone.

Police investigating the theft reviewed surveillance footage which reportedly showed a shirtless man pushing the motorcycle away from Freetown Road and through nearby streets, including Douglas Jones Street and Yorke Street.

An officer who reviewed the footage reportedly recognized the man as Fuller. Police said the individual captured on camera also appeared to walk with a limp.

Fuller pleaded guilty but offered an explanation to the court, saying he had done wrong and was willing to pay for any damage caused to the motorcycle.

“I did the wrong thing, but at the moment I never realized what I was doing. I returned the cycle and I am willing to pay for damages caused to it if I must,” Fuller told the court.

He also explained that he helps care for his mother and sister and expressed remorse for his actions.

“The devil this time used me,” Fuller told the Magistrate.

Taking his guilty plea and mitigation into consideration, the Magistrate imposed a non-custodial sentence, fining Fuller $800 plus $5 cost of court.

He has until November 30, 2026, to pay the fine or face three months imprisonment.

World.title: UDP demands full investigation into reported Guatemalan military aircraft incursion
World.content:
UDP demands full investigation into reported Guatemalan military aircraft incursion

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): The United Democratic Party is demanding a full investigation into reports that a Guatemalan military aircraft may have entered Belizean airspace near Lighthouse Reef Atoll and Caye Caulker.

In a statement issued Thursday, September 25, the UDP said Belizeans deserve clear answers about the aircraft’s route, purpose and exact position during the reported September 24 flight.

The Opposition referred to comments attributed to Ministry of National Defence and Border Security CEO Francis Usher indicating that Belize had not authorized the flight.

The UDP also pointed to Guatemala’s subsequent response, saying the Guatemalan Ministry of National Defence stated that its military operations comply with national and international law, but did not directly answer whether the aircraft entered Belizean airspace.

The party is now calling on the Government to establish the aircraft’s route using available radar, air traffic and flight records and to make its findings public.

It also wants the Government to seek a direct explanation from Guatemala regarding the purpose of the flight and the aircraft’s location near Lighthouse Reef and Caye Caulker.

The UDP said that if evidence confirms the aircraft entered Belizean airspace without authorization, Belize should lodge a formal diplomatic protest and raise the incident with appropriate regional and international partners.

The reported incident comes amid the longstanding Belize Guatemala territorial dispute. Belize has described the peaceful resolution of that dispute as a major foreign policy priority, with the matter currently before the International Court of Justice. Ministry of Foreign Affairs

The UDP said it would support lawful and peaceful measures to protect Belize’s sovereignty.

World.title: UDP says “Guatemala must provide a direct answer”
World.content:
UDP says “Guatemala must provide a direct answer”

By Zoila Palma: The United Democratic Party (UDP) is calling on the Government of Belize to provide answers following reports that a Guatemalan military aircraft flew near Lighthouse Reef Atoll and Caye Caulker on September 24.

In a statement, the UDP said Chief Executive Officer in the Ministry of National Defence and Border Security Francis Usher confirmed that Belize did not authorize the flight.

Guatemala’s Ministry of National Defense has maintained that its military operations comply with national and international law, without directly addressing the aircraft’s location, the UDP said.

The UDP is urging the Government to establish the aircraft’s route using radar, air traffic and flight records and to make the findings public.

“Belize needs a specific account of the flight, not a general assurance,” the party said.

It is also calling for a direct explanation from Guatemala regarding the purpose of the flight and the aircraft’s position near Lighthouse Reef and Caye Caulker.

The UDP further stated that if evidence confirms the aircraft entered Belizean airspace without authorization, “the absence of authorization makes a formal diplomatic protest necessary.”

The call comes as the Ministry of Foreign Affairs says it is working with the Ministry of National Defence and Border Security to officially confirm the details of the reported incident, while stating that any incursion by a foreign military aircraft would constitute a violation of Belize’s sovereignty.

The UDP also linked the incident to Belize’s recent protest over the reported obstruction of Belizean nationals near Sarstoon Island.

“Belizeans deserve the facts, and Guatemala must provide a direct answer,” the UDP said.

World.title: Man says he paid car dealer more than $13,000 for Pathfinder but never got it then found same vehicle being advertised on Facebook Marketplace
World.content:
Man says he paid car dealer more than $13,000 for Pathfinder but never got it then found same vehicle being advertised on Facebook Marketplace

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police are investigating a complaint of obtaining property by deception after a Belize City man reported paying more than BZ$13,000 for an imported SUV that was never delivered — only to later allegedly find the same vehicle being advertised for sale on Facebook Marketplace.

A 31-year-old man told police that in March he contacted a car dealer to purchase a 2014 Nissan Pathfinder through an online bidding site.

The complainant said they agreed on a price of BZ$13,000, with BZ$10,000 to be paid as a deposit and the remaining BZ$3,000 when the vehicle arrived in Belize.

According to the report, the man met the dealer at the Novelo’s Bus Terminal on March 20 and handed him BZ$10,000 cash. He said he later received an electronic receipt.

On June 24, the car dealer allegedly informed the complainant that the Pathfinder had reached Belize’s northern border and requested the outstanding balance plus a BZ$150 broker’s fee.

Smith told police that he subsequently transferred BZ$3,150 to an account provided.

The vehicle was reportedly supposed to be delivered on June 29, but the complainant alleged that the car dealer later told him he was unable to retrieve it from the border.

Nearly three months later, on September 17, Smith said he was scrolling through Facebook Marketplace when he saw a 2014 Nissan Pathfinder advertised by an account bearing the same dealer’s name.

Smith told police he recognized the SUV because the  allegedly used the same photographs as the original online listing for the vehicle he had paid to purchase.

Police are investigating the complaint as obtaining property by deception. No criminal charge is indicated in the situation report.

World.title: Belize to protest after Guatemalan Military plane spends 70 minutes in Airspace, turns off transponder
World.content:
Belize to protest after Guatemalan Military plane spends 70 minutes in Airspace, turns off transponder

By Zoila Palma: Belize is preparing to issue a formal protest note to Guatemala after a Guatemalan Army aircraft entered Belizean airspace, circled near Lighthouse Reef and remained inside the country’s airspace for approximately one hour and 10 minutes before exiting through the Sarstoon River. The incident occurred on September 24, 2026.

Francis Usher, Chief Executive Officer in the Ministry of National Defence said the aircraft, identified as FAG706, entered Belizean airspace from the east at approximately 7:29 p.m. and began circling in the vicinity of Lighthouse Reef.

“FAG706 did enter our airspace at 7:29 pm local time on 24 September and it entered from the East and began circling in the vicinity of Lighthouse Reef,” Usher stated. He added that “they began circling as if though they were looking for something.”

According to Usher, the aircraft disappeared from Belize’s secondary radar at approximately 8:07 p.m., indicating that its transponder had been turned off.

However, he said Belizean authorities continued tracking the aircraft through primary radar. “But even if you fall off the secondary radar, we can still track you using the primary radar. So, we were able to pick them up. They were still in Belizean airspace,” he explained.

Usher said FAG706 eventually left Belizean airspace at approximately 8:40 p.m., departing through the south pass of the Sarstoon River. The aircraft therefore remained in Belizean airspace for approximately one hour and 10 minutes after entering from the east.

Meanwhile, CEO in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Oscar Arnold said Belize will deliver a protest note to Guatemala’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, including information on the aircraft’s location and movements. “And we will demand from them an explanation as to why this is taking place. We find it very troubling that the leadership would not have this information available to them at the time when they made the social media post stating that they operate within the scope of professionalism and respect of sovereignty,” Arnold said.

World.title: Guatemalan military plane enters Belize airspace, circles Lighthouse Reef and exits through Sarstoon
World.content:
Guatemalan military plane enters Belize airspace, circles Lighthouse Reef and exits through Sarstoon

By Zoila Palma: A Guatemalan Army aircraft, FAG706, spent approximately one hour and 10 minutes inside Belize’s airspace on September 24, 2026, before exiting through the southern part of the country, according to Francis Usher, Chief Executive Officer in the Ministry of National Defence.

Usher provided details of the incident today.

Usher said the aircraft entered Belizean airspace from the east at 7:29 p.m. and began circling near Lighthouse Reef. “FAG706 did enter our airspace at 7:29 pm local time on 24 September and it entered from the East and began circling in the vicinity of Lighthouse Reef,” Usher stated.

He explained that the aircraft appeared to be circling between Lighthouse Reef and other aviation reference points, adding that “they began circling as if though they were looking for something.”

According to Usher, the aircraft disappeared from the secondary radar at approximately 8:07 p.m., indicating that its transponder had been turned off.

However, he said Belizean authorities continued tracking the aircraft using primary radar. “But even if you fall off the secondary radar, we can still track you using the primary radar. So, we were able to pick them up. They were still in Belizean airspace,” he explained.

Usher said the aircraft eventually departed Belizean airspace at approximately 8:40 p.m., around one hour and 10 minutes after entering the country. “At approximately 8:40pm, 1 hour and 10 minutes after, they initially entered Belize, they departed Belize through the south pass, the Sarstoon River,” he stated.

CEO in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Oscar Arnold has indicated that Belize will deliver a protest note to Guatemala’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs along with coordination and location.

“And we will demand from them an explanation as to why this is taking place. We find it very troubling that the leadership would not have this information available to them at the time when they made the social media post stating that they operate within the scope of professionalism and respect of sovereignty,” Arnold said.

World.title: Burglars steal cash, cigarettes, lottery tickets and 50 live 9mm rounds from Racecourse Street shop
World.content:
Burglars steal cash, cigarettes, lottery tickets and 50 live 9mm rounds from Racecourse Street shop

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police are investigating a burglary at J&C Shop on Racecourse Street in Belize City where thieves reportedly stole more than BZ$7,600 worth of property — including 50 live rounds of 9mm ammunition.

Police responded to the business early Monday morning, September 21, after the businessman was alerted that locks securing the shop had been damaged.

Investigators say entry was gained by cutting a padlock on the burglar-bar door and opening a shutter.

The shop owner later provided police with a detailed list of stolen property including cigarettes, cigars, scratch lottery tickets, beer, noodles, a network video recording device and UPS, and BZ$3,104 in cash.

Also reported stolen were 50 live 9mm rounds valued at BZ$75.

Police estimated the total loss at BZ$7,622.

Investigators processed the scene and reportedly lifted fingerprints. Police also recovered a pair of bolt cutters and took a DNA swab from a beer can which surveillance footage allegedly showed the perpetrators drinking from during the burglary.

Police have also reviewed surveillance footage from the shop as the investigation continues.

World.title: ‘You must die!’
World.content:
Late pastor of Pathways International Restoration Ministries Kevin Smith

A police sergeant testified on Friday that he opened gunfire on a knife-wielding male attacker at Pathways International Restoration Ministries in Albion, St James, after the man, who hurled death threats, refused to comply with law enforcers’ orders to drop his weapon.

The cop, who was the fourth witness in the murder trial of Andre Ruddock at the Home Circuit Court in downtown Kingston, said that the knife-wielding man was rushing from the church towards the police and using threatening language.

Ruddock is being tried in relation to the October 17, 2021 killing of 39-year-old Taneka Gardner, whose throat was cut, allegedly by the accused, at the church in what has been described as a human sacrifice ritual. Ruddock was said to have been acting on the instructions of the pastor of the church, Kevin Smith.

Smith died a few days later in a motor vehicle crash in St Catherine while being transported to Kingston to be charged in relation to the incident.

On Thursday, another member of the constabulary testified that Smith had instructed members of the church to kill the police if they gained access to the compound.

On Friday, the second police witness told the court that he and members of his team were attacked by the male member of the church and because he feared for his life, he was forced to discharge multiple rounds into the upper body of the attacker. His colleague also fired at the man.

The witness said that the members of the police team did not enter the church compound via the gate at the front, but had to skilfully scale a wall, topped with barbed wire, at the back of the premises to gain access. The policeman said that it was while the members of the team were going over the wall, one after the other, that the man with the knife rushed to them.

“I was in the process of assisting members of the team to get past the barbed wires. He spoke to me, and I turned around and looked in the direction of the church.

“I looked to the left of a boardwalk where I saw a man of dark complexion, slim build, about 5 feet 7 inches in height. He was dressed in a red shirt and a pair of white and grey trousers. I saw this man with what appeared to be a silver-looking knife in his right hand and this man seemed to be disturbed by the presence of the police on the church compound,” the cop shared.

He said that the man was looking in the direction of the police who were coming over the wall and was pointing the knife furiously at them.

“It was as if he was trying to say something. He was agitated, moving from one side to the other. At the time when I saw this man, I did not see anyone else. I shouted out to the man, saying, ‘Police! Put down the knife!’ He did not put the knife down. The man then started to run towards me and shouted, ‘You must die!’ repeatedly,” the cop said.

He told the court that when he first shouted to the man, he was about 33 metres away from the him. The policeman said he made numerous attempts to get the man to stop advancing towards him.

“He did not obey the command. He continued to advance towards me with the knife and on reaching about three meters away, he put his right hand in the air with the knife in a stabbing position. I moved two steps backwards and then to the right. I then pointed my M16 rifle to the chest area of the man and I discharged three rounds because I was fearful for my life and the life of my colleagues who were beside me. I also heard loud explosions to my right. A constable was positioned to my right and the loud explosions sounded like gunshots. It came from the constable’s rifle. The man [the attacker] fell to the ground,” the witness testified.

He further said that following the shooting, all seven members of his team had got over the wall, through the barbed wire, after which the knife was removed from the man’s palm.

“We tried to assist him to the hospital but the front gate was locked and the service vehicle could not enter the premises. I saw a few people on the verandah section of the church and they went inside of the church. I then contacted the police emergency communications centre and I informed the monitor at the Area One control centre about the incident. I also requested from the monitor additional personnel to come to the scene,” he said.

The cop told the court that he then instructed two of his team members to cover the rear of the building and another set was sent to monitor the front.

“I, along with one member, went to the top of the church building to also give coverage. I walked towards the front of the building where I could see the gate and the roadway. I could see persons on the inside of the church premises. I saw someone close to the front gate, kneeling behind a column, covered with a white sheet and it seemed as if this person was hiding,” he said.

“Whilst on the top of the building I went to the right and I saw someone motionless lying face down and covered with white cloth. I also saw what appeared to be blood leaking from the neck area to the head. I saw more police arriving on the scene, as well as members of the Jamaica Defence Force. I shouted out to them and told them not to climb over the gate because I did not know if that person who was kneeling was armed,” he said, explaining that instructions were given to them on how to safely enter the compound.

World.title: Cephas’ injury-time strike gives Boyz dramatic 3-2 win over Guatemala in Nations League
World.content:
Jamaica's Kasey Palmer battles Guatemalan Óscar Santis for the ball. (Photo: Garfield Robinson)

KINGSTON, Jamaica — A stoppage-time goal from substitute Renaldo Cephas gave Jamaica’s Reggae Boyz a dramatic come-from-behind 3-2 win over Guatemala in their Concacaf Nations League Group B League A opener at the National Stadium on Friday.

Jamaica avenged last year’s loss to the Central Americans at the Gold Cup despite a double from Oscar Santis, the first coming in the second minute.

The Reggae Boyz, rallied from a goal down to lead 2-1, Guatemala levelled before Cephas’ late strike settled the points.

Santis, who scored in Guatemala’s 1-0 win at the Gold Cup, gave them an early lead when he fired low under goalkeeper Andre Blake to finish off a counter-attack.

They could have been 2-0 up in the 18th minute, but Darwin Lom guided a cross from Santis just wide of the far left post with the Jamaican goal at his mercy.

Kasey Palmer, who had a good outing, pulled Jamaica level in the 39th minute when he capitalised on an error by Jorge Aparicio and fired low under goalkeeper Kenderson Navarro for his third goal for Jamaica.

Palmer was also involved as Jamaica took the lead in the 53rd minute, making the pass to Ruman Burell, who scored, beating Navarro to his right into the far corner.

A mistake in the Jamaican defence left the door open for Santis in the 67th minute, and he made no mistake, dribbling around Blake, who came off his line, and scored in an open goal.

Both teams came close to scoring. Cephas shot just wide in the 79th minute, and Olger Escobar hit the inside of the Jamaican left upright in the 90th minute.

Four minutes into added time, Cephas made up for his earlier miss when he beat Navarro with his fourth goal in national colours.

Meanwhile, head coach Rudolph Speid had named seven members of the team that had lost in the final game of the failed World Cup 2026 attempt in the starting X1—goalkeeper and team captain Blake, Joel Latibeaudiere, Richard King, Isaac Hayden, Palmer, Ronaldo Webster and Tyreece Campbell.

Jamaica’s bid for a spot in the expanded FIFA World Cup to be hosted by Concacaf failed after a 1-0 loss to the Democratic Republic of Congo in their FIFA intercontinental play-offs in Mexico in March.

Starting team: Andre Blake, Joel Latibeaudiere, Damion Lowe, Richard King, Isaac Hayden, Karoy Anderson, Kasey Palmer, Ronaldo Webster, Tyreece Campbell, Rumarn Burrell, Javon East.

— Paul A Reid

World.title: Bartlett welcomes Sandals, Royal Caribbean partnership
World.content:
Minister of Tourism Edmund Bartlett

Tourism Minister Edmund Bartlett has welcomed the signing of a partnership agreement between Sandals Resorts and Royal Caribbean Group, highlighting its potential to expand Jamaica’s international reach, support tourism investment and create opportunities for workers and local businesses.

“Sandals is a Jamaican success story, built on the vision of Gordon ‘Butch’ Stewart and the contribution of generations of Caribbean hospitality professionals. His son, Adam Stewart, has carried that legacy forward as executive chairman, guiding the brand into a new chapter of growth and global partnership. This announcement represents a significant moment in that journey. We recognise the importance of that legacy and the possibilities that greater global reach could bring to its next chapter,” a release from the tourism ministry quotes Bartlett.

He noted that combining Sandals’ resort expertise with Royal Caribbean Group’s international customer base and distribution networks could introduce Jamaica to wider audiences.

Over time, this could support demand for resort stays, encourage further investment and create additional opportunities across the tourism economy, including procurement from Jamaican farmers and manufacturers, opportunities for attractions and creative enterprises, and training and career development for tourism workers.

These possibilities, he said, align with Jamaica’s Tourism 3.0 growth agenda, which places greater emphasis on retaining tourism value locally, developing human capital and ensuring that communities share in the sector’s progress.

World.title: FIFA president Infantino at National Stadium for Reggae Boyz clash
World.content:
KINGSTON, Jamaica — FIFA president Gianni Infantino is at the National Stadium in Kingston for Jamaica’s Concacaf Nations League game against Guatemala.

Infantino arrived around 7:00 pm amid an ongoing re-election campaign for the top job in football.

The FIFA president’s campaign has been marred by controversy surrounding a proposal to take aspects of the World Cup to private investors, which prompted swift and widespread backlash from football associations worldwide.

Attendance at the match just an hour before kickoff was scant, with barely any seats filled at the sporting ground.

This is the first official match at the stadium since a record number of Jamaicans packed the venue to witness the possibility of the country booking a ticket for the 2026 World Cup in their Concacaf final round finale against Curacao.

That match ended nil-nil, and the resulting draw left the Reggae Boyz in second place in their group, sending Curacao through to the World Cup. They were forced into the inter-confederation play-offs and eliminated after falling to DR Congo.

Five members of the Reggae Boyz team who lost in the final game of the failed World Cup 2026 attempt were named in the starting team to face Guatemala in their Concacaf Nations League Group B game.

Five members of the Reggae Boyz team who lost in the final game of the failed World Cup 2026 attempt were named in the starting team to face Guatemala in their Concacaf Nations League Group B game.

Boyz coach Rudolph Speid named goalkeeper and team captain Andre Blake, Joel Latibeaudiere, Richard King, Isaac Hayden, Kasey Palmer, Ronaldo Webster and Tyreece Campbell in the starting team.

Starting team-

Andre Blake, Joel Latibeaudiere, Damion Lowe, Richard King, Isaac Hayden, Karoy Anderson, Kasey Palmer, Ronaldo Webster, Tyreece Campbell, Rumarn Burrell, Javon East.

World.title: 3-y-o with Erb’s palsy needs $3m for life-changing surgery in US
World.content:
The Wilson Family needs $3 million to fund Ayana's treatment overseas

KINGSTON, Jamaica — “Every child deserves the chance to run, play, laugh, and grow without being limited by an injury they never chose.”

Three-year-old Ayana Wilson from Riverton City in Kingston, is hoping for that chance, according to her family.

The toddler was injured during delivery following shoulder dystocia, resulting in a diagnosis of Erb’s palsy, a condition involving nerve damage affecting the shoulder and arm.

Ayana’s caregivers say despite the challenges she faces, she remains a happy, loving and vibrant child who wants what every three-year-old wants: to play with other children, explore the world, and enjoy her childhood.

However, the damage to her shoulder and arm has made many ordinary childhood activities difficult.

Ayana’s family reached out to Jamaican charity Crisis Support Charity Limited seeking assistance and her case was subsequently brought to Shriners Children’s in Philadelphia, where she has been accepted for further evaluation and treatment.

Ayana is scheduled to travel to the United States in October 2026 for medical evaluation and surgery, which the family describes as a chance for a new beginning— to use her arm more freely, play and participate more fully in childhood activities.

The three-year-old and her mother, Rosalee Eccles, have already obtained their United States visas, but the cost of traveling and remaining there for approximately six weeks following surgery and recovery is an obstacle to her treatment.

Anya’s father works for a local waste management company and the family says his modest income is used to meet their daily needs.

Eccles operates a small tuck shop in their community while caring for her family and helping to provide for their everyday expenses.

Noting that the cost associated with Anya’s medical journey is far beyond what the family can manage on their own, Crisis Support Charity Limited has shared a fundraising goal of $3 million to help.

The funds will assist with:

Airfare for Ayana and her mother

Accommodation for approximately six weeks

Specialised seating and support equipment required following surgery

Meals and basic living expenses

Transportation to and from medical appointments

Other essential expenses associated with Ayana’s medical care and recovery

“Every contribution, regardless of size, can help bring Ayana closer to the treatment she needs. Imagine being three years old and wanting to run, play, climb and participate with other children, while an injury makes many of those activities difficult,” the charity said.

“You may not know Ayana personally, but your kindness could become a meaningful part of her life story,” it said, noting that donations, no matter how small, matter.

Interested individuals, groups and companies can donate to Crisis Support Charity Limited at www.crisissupportycharity.org, specifying their beneficiary as Ayana Wilson.

The charity is urging people who cannot donate to share Ayana’s story.

“One child. One opportunity. One community coming together. Let us help Ayana get the chance she deserves,” the charity said.

World.title: KC principal responds to viral video of student being held over railing
World.content:
Kingston College Principal Dave Myrie speaking at morning devotion on Monday, March 31, 2025 as the school celebrated its 36th Boys’ Champs title. (Photo: Joseph Wellington)

KINGSTON, Jamaica — Kingston College (KC) has launched an investigation after a video surfaced online showing a student being held by colleagues over a railing before falling.

In an official statement dated September 23, Principal Dave Myrie said the school’s administration and Board of Management are aware of the matter and are conducting a “thorough investigation” into the circumstances surrounding the incident.

Myrie said, however, that no student was injured.

“The School Administration and the Board of Management are aware of the matter and are currently conducting a thorough investigation into the circumstances surrounding the incident,” Myrie said in the statement.

He assured parents, guardians, students and members of the wider KC community that the matter was being taken seriously and would be addressed in accordance with the school’s established policies and procedures.

The principal also reiterated the school’s commitment to maintaining what he described as a safe, disciplined and supportive environment for its students.

KC has also appealed to members of the school community to refrain from sharing or reposting the video.

According to Myrie, further circulation could unnecessarily compromise the privacy, dignity and welfare of the young students involved.

“Any further information considered appropriate will be communicated through the School’s official channels,” the statement said.

Myrie has served as principal of Kingston College since 2012.

– Howard Walker

World.title: Court walkout looms
World.content:
Defence attorneys staging a ‘silent protest’ outside the Supreme Court on King Street in downtown Kingston on Wednesday demanding that their concerns about the Firearms (Prohibition, Restriction and Regulation) Act, 2022 and its impact on “justice, due process and the rule of law” be taken on board for reform. (Photo: Karl Mclarty)

Defence attorneys have been placed on alert to pull their services from the island’s courts for an entire week, starting next Monday, a move that will deal a significant blow to the Michaelmas term which began just over a week ago.

The lawyers arrived at the decision after a meeting on Thursday with Justice Minister Delroy Chuck which they say failed to produce any meaningful plans to reform the 2022 Firearms Act.

The emergency meeting was called following Wednesday’s ‘silent protest’ outside the Supreme Court on King Street in downtown Kingston, where members of the Jamaican Bar Association, the Advocates Association in collaboration with Bar associations across the island, armed with placards, demanded that their concerns about the Firearms (Prohibition, Restriction and Regulation) Act, 2022 and its impact on “justice, due process and the rule of law” be taken on board for reform.

Some hours later, Chuck indicated that he would be meeting with representatives of the bodies to hear their concerns.

However, following those discussions, defence attorney Tamika Harris, a member of the Bar Council of the Jamaican Bar Association and chair of its Criminal Practice and Procedure Subcommittee, who was a key figure behind the protest, told the Jamaica Observer that the meeting amounted to little less than an exercise in futility.

“The minister could not give a timeline as to when anything would be taken to the legislature, and he has asked for the discussion to be placed in writing but before [the Act was passed] the Bar Association… made a submission to Parliament. We are not asking for anything different, so it’s not like our argument is new,” Harris stated.

“The meeting, in my mind, was an opportunity for us to say the same things we have already said, but we have not gotten any response from the minister to, for example, say when he will go to Parliament [with proposed amendments]. I know everything takes time, but I did not get any idea of a plan to put in action. So the minister didn’t confirm that he was going to put a plan in action, so there is no resolution,” Harris declared.

As such, she said attorneys will be moving to action the next stage of their protest.

“He was very courteous and he listened. He expressed that he understood our concerns, but he did not go any further to say exactly if they were going to be dealt with and when, so there is nothing. I am aware he has already been presented with similar arguments by the director of public prosecutions and even the chief justice. I am going to ask my members to withdraw our services,” Harris told the Observer.

“We are going to use the opportunity, perhaps, to do quick education. The public needs to be aware that we are not saying legislation must be weak on persons who use firearms to terrorise our Jamaican citizens, we are not saying the legislation needs to be weak; we are saying that the legislation is to be fair and cognisant that not every case is the same,” Harris said.

The protests come just over a week after the justice minister’s comments at the Annual Assize Service of the judiciary. Chuck said, while the mandatory minimum sentences contained in the provision were being reviewed because of widespread concerns, “The security forces and a number of my colleagues feel that the Act is working and it is bringing down murders and shootings.

“It is under consideration, but firearms are a major problem in our country, and that is why we don’t want to send a signal that we are going to relent on the enforcement to condemn the possession and the use of firearms. But it is under consideration,” Chuck said.

The comments triggered furious commentary from several quarters.

A week later members of Jamaica’s legal profession met on Saturday, September 19 to consider what they described as “the operation and impact of the Act, particularly its mandatory sentencing provisions and the restrictions placed on judicial discretion”.

In a statement issued following that meeting, the attorneys said, “The legal profession supports strong and effective laws to combat gun violence and punish those who use illegal firearms to murder, rob, terrorise and intimidate our citizens. Our concern is not with strong penalties. Our concern is with a sentencing regime that does not adequately allow judges to distinguish between offenders, offences, and individual circumstances.”

The Act, which prescribes a mandatory 15-year sentence for specified violations, took effect in November 2022 and, among other things, provides penalties ranging from 15 years to life imprisonment for possession of illegal weapons. It establishes a dual regime — distinguishing between prohibited weapons or unregulated firearms and connected activities, and firearms that are duly authorised or registered.

According to the advocates, their September 19 meeting “identified several areas of serious concern, including the restriction of judicial discretion; the proportionality of mandatory minimum sentences in individual cases; the diminished incentive for early guilty pleas; the resulting increase in matters proceeding to trial and pressure on an already burdened criminal justice system; the treatment of imitation firearms; and the consequences of certain provisions for licensed firearm holders”.

“The legal profession is calling for urgent amendments to the Act, including consideration of an ‘exceptional circumstances’ provision allowing judges appropriate discretion in deserving cases, meaningful sentencing incentives for early guilty pleas, reform of the certificate regime, and a review of the provisions governing imitation firearms and licensed firearm holders. The profession also calls for urgent, structured consultation with the Government, Opposition, Parliament, the judiciary and other relevant stakeholders on the proposed amendments”, the attorneys said in that statement.

World.title: Christiana clampdown
World.content:
Vendors on Wildman Street in Christiana on Thursday (Photos: Kasey Williams)

CHRISTIANA, Manchester — Mandeville Mayor Donovan Mitchell says, effective today, there will be a clampdown on unapproved buildings and illegal vending, as part of enforcement activities in the south-central town of Christiana.

“Yesterday (Wednesday) I came into Christiana and as the chairman of the local Board of Health I spent about five hours walking the streets of Christiana. I visited the abattoir. I visited the market. I visited the transportation centre. I looked at some businesses [and] buildings going up. I know at the council meeting early this month I made a statement and some people are up in arms and all of that… What is happening in the parish will not continue,” he said on Thursday while addressing the launch of Sam Fo Meats mobile application on Wildman Street in Christiana.

“I said it yesterday (Wednesday) to my team that Wildman Street, please be prepared, because I am going to be changing the entire look of Wildman Street. There will absolutely be no selling on the street. I am warning the businesses that are putting their sewage and grey water into our water channels to stop and stop before tomorrow [Friday] morning, because a team from the public health service will be coming out and we are going to make sure it cannot continue,” added Mitchell.

He pointed to the public safety concerns and hazards of waste water flowing on the busy commercial street.

“You cannot be walking on the street and all you are seeing is grey water. Businesses can’t build their buildings and put their grey water on the street. What about our children, the elderly? You are walking and miss your step in soap water and you break your leg and the first thing is they call the parish council,” said Mitchell, who chairs the Manchester Municipal Corporation.

“I am warning people who are building houses without plans from the Manchester Municipal Corporation. I am not holding bar; you have to do better. When a building collapses because you have not done the correct thing, who is the first person you blame? Government. Where was the Government when you were building? Not around, because you put zinc all around your place and you do what you have to do and when you are finished you open up the zinc and you see a building there that has not gone through the proper channel,” added Mitchell.

Pertaining to the Christiana abattoir, Mitchell said he is contemplating closing it for renovations.

“We are having some problems and I will tell you that maybe, based on the letters I am getting from the health services, I may have to close it even temporarily to make sure that things go right. I am warning, since I am in Christiana, that things are not going to be the same in Christiana. There has to be some changes,” declared Mitchell.

World.title: Iran says Strait of Hormuz could reopen within seven days if US accepts deal
World.content:
Vessels transit the Strait of Hormuz off the coast of Bandar Abbas, Iran on Sept. 5, 2026. | Atta Kenare/AFP via Getty Images

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi Friday said his country is offering to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days and resume talks on its nuclear program in exchange for concessions from Washington.

Those would include lifting its naval blockade of Iranian ports, waiving sanctions on Iranian oil sales and a ceasefire that would include Lebanon, Araghchi told reporters on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York, according to an AP report.

“The seven-day timeline will start as soon as the United States accepts this plan,” he said on Friday, adding that Iran had conveyed its offer to the U.S. through Qatar.



Although U.S. President Donald Trump has not formally responded to the proposal, he privately rejected the plan, according to a Wall Street Journal report citing U.S. officials. He is instead betting on renewed escalation including by raising the possibility of another bombing campaign on the country after the midterm elections in November, according to the same report.

Trump on Friday night shared a map of the region on Truth Social, renaming the Strait of Hormuz as the “Trump Strait.”

The Strait of Hormuz is a critical route for global oil and natural gas supplies and has been a major flashpoint since the U.S. and Israel launched their war against Iran in February.

World.title: Trump’s G20 invite to Putin is an ‘opportunity,’ German foreign minister says
World.content:
But Germany’s Wadephul struck a more optimistic tone during a press conference with his Canadian counterpart in Ottawa.

The invitation “will be a litmus test really, also for Vladimir Putin to negotiate. So these kind of opportunities, one would have to take advantage of,” he said. “Repeatedly we have asked the Russian government and Vladimir Putin to come to the negotiation table. And if it is a possibility, then perhaps it would be at least a start to serious negotiations.”

He then added that the prerequisite for a meaningful conversation would be for a ceasefire to be in place during the talks.

Canadian Foreign Minister Anita Anand said she was surprised by Trump’s invitation to Putin, but added that Canada would show up regardless because that would be “what diplomacy truly is.”

Wadephul’s remarks diverged from his government’s official position. Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s spokesperson, Stefan Kornelius, had said earlier this week that “the German government does not view relations with Russia as business as usual” and that it was coordinating a joint response with its partners.

The German foreign ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The White House’s invitation is the latest U.S. effort to reintegrate Moscow into the international diplomatic fold and could lead to `Putin’s first in-person G20 appearance since 2019.

World.title: Ein Spaziergang mit Karl Lauterbach
World.content:
Ein politisches Beben rüttelt die Republik durch: Während die Linkspartei in Berlin an die Spitze stürmt, fliegt die CDU in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern komplett aus dem Landtag. Nach diesem historischen Wahlsonntag stellt sich die drängende Frage, wie handlungsfähig die Koalition bei künftigen Reformen überhaupt noch ist. Steht das deutsche Parteiensystem vor dem Kollaps oder gibt es noch einen Ausweg aus der Krise?

Gordon Repinski spricht mit dem früheren SPD-Gesundheitsminister Karl Lauterbach über die Verschiebungen und darüber, ob die Politik nun völlig neue, grundsätzliche Ideen braucht. Lauterbach warnt davor, alles schlecht zu reden und verteidigt die Koalition von Union und SPD, die stabiler sei als oft behauptet. Außerdem warnt er davor, zu glauben, dass Kürzungen bei den Sozialausgaben zu mehr Wirtschaftswachstum führen würden.

Dazu diskutiert Repinski mit Lauterbach über neue KI-Modelle, ihre Gefährlichkeit und das weltweite KI-Wettrennen, bei dem Deutschland droht, den Anschluss zu verlieren.

Das Berlin Playbook als Podcast gibt es jeden Morgen ab 5 Uhr. Rixa Fürsen, Maximilian Stascheit und das POLITICO-Team liefern Politik zum Hören – kompakt, international, hintergründig.

World.title: Burnham’s AI agenda is already in disarray thanks to Trump
World.content:
Within the space of a week, however, Trump trashed any hopes that America will participate in global agreements on AI and POLITICO revealed that AISI’s usually privileged access to new AI models is now being delayed by the White House – which told leading AI firms OpenAI and Anthropic not to share their models with the U.K. until U.S. testers have finished ascertaining that they don’t pose a threat to American systems.

So if Burnham wants to stick to his plan of making U.K. the center for brokering international AI harmony he has to figure out how to bring the U.S. onside, or else press on without the U.K.’s closest ally.

When approached by POLITICO, a U.K. government spokesperson said: “The U.K. is a world leader in AI security, and the AI Security Institute continues to work closely with the U.S. government, international partners and leading AI companies, including OpenAI and Anthropic.”

Special relationship problems

The U.K. already has a track record for convening global meetings on AI safety, but it has also tended to stick by the U.S. when deciding whether to sit out specific international agreements.

In 2023 the U.K. hosted the Bletchley Park Summit on AI safety, which produced an agreement on the opportunities and risks of AI signed by 28 countries, crucially including the U.S. and China.

However, at the Paris iteration of the summit in 2025 the U.K. declined to sign a new declaration on the ethical development of AI alongside the U.S.

World.title: Dutch opposition party votes to join European Socialist family
World.content:
“There are only three European political families represented at all three levels [of the

EU],” the advisory committee wrote in a report, adding that the PES has “prime ministers, the President of the European Council, European Commissioners, and leaders of national parties.”

“The Greens … have fewer ministers, no members of the European Commission, and no

heads of government; consequently, their preliminary consultations carry less weight,” the

report went on.

PRO leader Jesse Klaver joined a PES meeting ahead of the European Council summit in June, alongside Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez and Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen.

What about the MEPs?

European political parties and political groups in the European Parliament are closely

linked, but they are not the same thing.

A PRO spokesperson told POLITICO that the party’s eight MEPs are likely to remain in

their current parliamentary groups: four in the Socialists and Democrats and four

in the Greens/European Free Alliance.

The spokesperson said PRO would likely review the arrangement ahead of the next

European Parliament election in 2029.

World.title: Pope Leo calls for dialogue as France’s populist forces eye power
World.content:
The pope named no politician or party. But his defense of diversity and religious freedom lands as Le Pen’s National Rally campaigns against immigration ahead of a presidential election she hopes to win for the first time.

“This dialogue is all the more urgent in the context of present-day France, where the people of differing cultural and religious backgrounds are called to live together,” the pontiff continued.

Standing in front of French government members and church dignitaries, the pope also argued against pushing religion out of public life, weeks after the National Rally said it was in favor of banning the Muslim headscarf. “Righteous secularism doesn’t mean excluding religion from public spaces,” he said.

Macron said the pope brought “hope” to France and praised his work on artificial intelligence and human dignity.

The papal visit will take Leo from the Élysée to UNESCO, Notre-Dame Cathedral and a youth vigil at the Stade de France. He will celebrate Mass on Saturday, expected to gather 600,000 people on the Champs-Elysées in Paris.

French politics have become deeply polarized in recent years, with the far-right National Rally and the far-left France Unbowed gaining popularity, just as traditional parties struggle to attract voters after a decade of Macron’s presidency.

World.title: Zelenskyy warns $27B funding gap could leave Ukraine short of weapons
World.content:
Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky (R) and High Representative of the European Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy Kaja Kallas (L) attend a joint press-conference following talks in Kyiv on October 13, 2025. | Sergei Supinsky/AFP via Getty Images

The president said he received a positive and constructive response from the EU during his diplomatic talks this week.

KYIV — Ukraine needs to secure $27 billion to plug a hole in its defense budget in the next two months or risk being unable to buy weapons early next year, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told reporters in a WhatsApp chat Friday.

“Most of this money is for our drones, missiles, and supplies for our warriors. About a third of this money, perhaps even a little more, is for drones for January, February, and March. And if we do not order and pay for them in October and November, we will face serious challenges in January and February,” Zelenskyy said.

The president added that covering the deficit was a top topic of his negotiations with European partners: “I am urging the European Commission to provide the second tranche of the €90 billion [loan] sooner. Because, once again, we must have the necessary drones and missiles for January and February.”

World.title: Burnham plans first Berlin visit for talks with Merz
World.content:
Burnham took office on July 20 after replacing Keir Starmer, whose government had come under growing pressure following electoral losses, internal Labour Party disputes and weak public support. Starmer’s departure capped a turbulent final period in office in which domestic political problems increasingly dominated his government’s attention.

The change in leadership came less than a year after Starmer and Merz had made a major push to bring Britain and Germany closer.

The two governments signed the Kensington Treaty in July 2025. It laid out plans for closer work across defense and security, economic ties, transport and migration.

Defense has become one of the strongest parts of the relationship. Britain and Germany signed the Trinity House Agreement in October 2024, creating a framework for much closer military and defense-industrial cooperation. Since then, they have expanded work on joint weapons projects and military coordination while remaining major European supporters of Ukraine.

Burnham now has the chance to give those efforts new political momentum while setting his own approach to Europe. He entered Downing Street promising an intense domestic focus, but has since embarked on a diplomatic blitz, including meetings with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy along with France's President Emmanuel Macron and U.S. President Donald Trump.

While Burnham is enjoying an early bout of optimism about his leadership, he will meet a German government facing significant domestic pressure.

Merz’s Christian Democrats suffered sharp losses in two state elections this month, while the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) has gained support nationally. POLITICO’s Poll of Polls puts the AfD at 28 percent, ahead of the Christian Democrats at 20 percent.

For both governments, the October meeting offers an early opportunity to show that the closer relationship built over the past two years can continue under new political leadership in London.

World.title: Thousands of protesters take to the streets in Madrid over Ceuta migrant crisis
World.content:
Thousands of people are taking part in Madrid's second "March for Dignity" on Saturday, with protesters calling for a general election and voicing their support for Ceuta amid the autonomous city's ongoing migrant crisis.

 

The demonstration, organised by the Sociedad Civil Española with the support of the People's Party (PP) and Vox, set off shortly after 10 am from the Plaza de Cibeles and headed towards the Arco del Triunfo in Moncloa, where it is expected to end at around 13:30 pm local time.

Among those taking part was Vox leader Santiago Abascal, who insisted that migrants who arrived in Ceuta must be returned to their country of origin and launched a scathing attack on the government's handling of the crisis - which began in late July when tens of thousands of people crossed into the Spanish North African territory from Morocco.

"Ceuta remains invaded because Sánchez continues to be Morocco's servant; the migrant invasion is being encouraged," he said, referring to Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez.

A separate "March for Dignity," held before the mass entry of migrants at the end of July, saw tens of thousands of people come together to demand Sánchez resign and for snap elections to be held.

According to the Government Delegation, that demonstration drew around 40,000 people, while organisers put the figure as high as 120,000.

On 2 September, Ceuta's official day, thousands of people also took to the streets in cities across Spain in a demonstration organised by the Spanish Federation of Municipalities and Provinces.

The crisis continues

Almost two months after the mass influx of migrants, the situation in Ceuta remains unresolved.

Around 8,300 migrants are being housed in facilities set up in the city, with more than 4,000 people estimated to still be living on the streets.

Morocco has accused Spain of obstructing the return of migrants who remain in Ceuta.

Spanish Foreign Minister José Manuel Albares recently met with his Moroccan counterpart Nasser Bourita in New York to address the issue.

During their talks, Bourita referred to "obstacles" and "controversies" that he believes are being fuelled in part by the Spanish political class and are preventing the situation from being resolved.

In the meantime, authorities are continuing to carry out surveillance and provide assistance across the city.

On Friday, the National Police arrested three Moroccan nationals who were living in a makeshift camp on Trampolín beach for their alleged involvement in the detention of two migrant minors. The two minors were taken to Ceuta University Hospital for treatment.

That same day, 63 women who were either alone or with young children were moved to a facility set up at the Hípica, as part of an ongoing effort to relocate people still living on the streets.

Firefighters have also discovered a makeshift settlement in underground tunnels in recent days, where around 30 to 50 migrants are thought to have been staying.

On Friday, a young Moroccan man died in a camp situated on the site of a former factory near Trampolín beach. The cause of death has not yet been established.

World.title: Forget Asia and Africa: bats originated in Europe 65 million years ago
World.content:
For decades, it was assumed that bats had originated in Asia, Africa or somewhere in the Americas. A new study now calls that idea into question. According to its authors, the lineage arose around 65 million years ago in Europe, from where it spread to colonise the rest of the planet. In other words, the first bat species dates back to the age of the dinosaurs.

 

The research, the most comprehensive carried out to date on this group of mammals, combines the genome sequencing of 103 species with the study of 44 fossils. The work forms part of Bat1K, an international consortium devoted to gathering genomic information on bats, and has been published in the journal "Nature" (source in Spanish). On the Spanish side, researchers from the National Museum of Natural Sciences (MNCN-CSIC) and the University of Granada have taken part.

Ismael Galván, a researcher at the MNCN, sums up the scope of the study: it is the first time that the genome of a flying mammal has been reconstructed, and this resource offers the scientific community a solid framework for investigating the genes responsible for their most distinctive traits. He explains that this line of research could eventually provide useful information for studies on ageing, immunity and resistance to disease in humans.

Professor Liliana M. Dávalos, of the University of Stony Brook, notes that the method used (jointly modelling the evolution of fossil and living species) makes it possible to do something other techniques could not: to place the oldest group of fossil bats while taking genomic data into account and thus determine when and where the group appeared. The data suggest that the first descendants of that European population dispersed into Africa, forming a Euro-African core from which bats later reached Asia, the Americas and Australia.

Bat1K project showing 21 known bat species Nature

Flight and echolocation, present from the very beginning

One of the findings highlighted by the team is that powered flight and echolocation, two features that define the biology of these animals, did not emerge at later stages of their evolution but near the very origin of the group.

The position of the fossil of the genus Vielasia, regarded as an ancestor of modern bats, on the oldest branch of the family tree reinforces that conclusion, which would help explain the evolutionary success of the lineage over 65 million years.

Michael Hiller, of the Senckenberg Institute in Frankfurt, describes the procedure followed: state-of-the-art DNA sequencing techniques combined with computational methods to generate and compare genomes, identify the genes they contain and cross-reference that information with the 44 fossils collected in different parts of the world.

Phylogenetic comparison of bat chromosomes Nature

The result, according to Professor Emma Teeling, of University College Dublin, is a robust phylogenetic tree after decades of findings that often contradicted one another.

To assemble the set of samples, the team turned to little-known species found in remote locations: the bumblebee bat from Thailand and Myanmar, one of the smallest mammals on Earth; the Madagascar sucker-footed bat, able to cling to smooth leaves thanks to small suction cups; and the lesser short-tailed bat, native to New Zealand, which uses its folded wings as if they were forelegs to move along the forest floor.

A resource with implications beyond animal biology

With more than 1,500 species distributed around the world, bats represent one fifth of all living mammals. Their role in ecosystems is significant: they pollinate plants, disperse seeds and control insect populations.

On top of that comes a feature of particular interest to biomedical research: their resistance to disease and a longevity that is striking in relation to their size.

Origins of the different bat species Nature

Professor David Ray, of Texas Tech University, stresses that the volume of data generated will allow the scientific community to track genomic variation, from changes in a single base to the absence of entire segments in one lineage that are present in another.

These differences, he notes, help to explain in part the enormous diversity of bats that exists today and the origins of their unique traits, a body of work whose relevance, he adds, goes well beyond this group of mammals.
