World.title: Zagreb City Break, Remote-Worker Style – Why 90 Days Could Be All You Need
World.content:
September the 25th, 2026 – Zagreb is an up and coming city break, but it could be more than that thanks to the remote worker boom. Many talk about Croatia’s famed “digital nomad visa”, but 90 days and zero admin could be all you need.

Not every remote worker wants (or needs) a full digital nomad visa. For many professionals, the classic Croatian “temporary stay of digital nomads” route – with its income thresholds, documentation piles and multi-month planning – is overkill. If your passport already allows visa-free entry to the Schengen area, you can simply turn up and stay for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. That window is long enough to settle into a real routine, yet short enough to feel like an extended city break rather than a bureaucratic relocation. Zagreb is perfectly suited to this lighter approach.

the 90 day limit could be all you need

Unlike the coastline and the islands, which swing between peak-season summer intensity and winter quiet, Zagreb functions as a proper European capital all year. Trams run, cafes stay open, co-working spaces keep their regular hours, and the cultural calendar never really stops. You get the infrastructure of a serious city without the summer price spikes that hit Split or Dubrovnik.

Reliable high-speed internet is the baseline, not a luxury. The co-working scene is mature and varied – from community-focused hubs to quieter central spots – so you can choose between focused workdays and networking as the mood takes you. Plenty of remote workers simply rotate between a well-chosen apartment and a handful of cafes with strong Wi-Fi and power sockets; the cafe culture here is built for lingering.

a big-little city with plenty to offer

Outside working hours, the city rewards curiosity. Upper Town’s cobbled streets and the instantly recognisable St Mark’s Church, the Museum of Broken Relationships, Maksimir Park, Lake Jarun (Zagreb’s unofficial “sea”), and the open-air Dolac Market are all within very easy reach. In the evenings, the bar and restaurant scene is lively without being overwhelming. Weekends open the door to day trips – Plitvice Lakes, the hills around Samobor, or a quick train to Ljubljana – without the stress of long-haul logistics.

Cost of living remains noticeably lower than in most Western European capitals, so a three-month stay feels financially sustainable rather than extravagant.

you don’t need to be a digital nomad to… be a digital nomad

Croatia’s official digital nomad temporary stay is designed for longer periods (up to 18 months) and requires proof of remote work for a non-Croatian entity, health insurance, a clean criminal record, and a minimum income currently set at 2.5 times the average net salary – currently over €3,600 per month, or the equivalent in savings. Processing takes time and the paperwork is real.

The 90-day Schengen short stay, by contrast, asks far less of you if your nationality qualifies for visa-free entry. You arrive, register your accommodation as required, work remotely for your existing foreign employer or clients, and leave before the 90 days are up (or before you hit the 183-day tax-residency threshold if that matters to you). No special permit, no income threshold tied to Croatian averages, no multi-week application process. It is simply a long, productive city break with a laptop. Of course the usual rules apply: you cannot take local employment, and the days count toward your overall Schengen allowance. But for many remote professionals testing life in Croatia, or simply wanting a change of scenery without administrative drama and a baptism of fire from the Croatian bureaucratic machine, that is precisely the point.

who could this work best for?

This approach suits a whole cohort of people; those who already work remotely for a company or clients outside Croatia and hold a passport that allows 90 days visa-free in the Schengen zone, those who want a proper base rather than a series of hotel stays and those prefer a walkable, cafe-packed European city with four seasons and good transport links, and those who are curious about Croatia but not yet ready to commit to the full digital nomad process. It also works well as a trial run. Spend 60–90 days in Zagreb, get a feel for the rhythm, the food, the community and the climate, then decide whether a longer digital nomad stay or a return trip next year makes sense for you.

no visas, no paperwork, and full freedom

Book a furnished apartment or serviced flat with reliable internet rather than a short-term tourist rental if you can. Join a coworking space for at least a few days a week to meet people. Use the city’s excellent public transport and the green spaces to keep the work–life balance healthy. And treat the weekends as genuine exploration time – Zagreb rewards slow discovery more than checklist tourism.

In short, you do not need a special visa to work remotely from Croatia for three months. You just need a laptop, a passport that opens the Schengen door, and a city that actually works for everyday life. Zagreb quietly delivers on all three. For practical information on accommodation, events and getting around, the Zagreb Tourist Board is a good starting point. The rest is simply showing up and getting to work – and leisure.

World.title: Končar Showcases Croatian Manufacturing to the World in Berlin
World.content:
September the 25th, 2026 – Končar has showcased Croatian manufacturing to the world in Berlin, taking the most prominent positions at this year’s InnoTrans.

Končar’s striking visuals were visible in the most prominent positions right at the entrance to the space of the prestigious fair, and the scene at the very entrance to the exhibition area was spectacular, where Končar’s train, a top product of Croatian industry, was positioned in a more prominent place than giants such as Alstom and Stadler. Sinisa Malus reports for Poslovni that after it was put into regular service on the Zagreb – Split route a week earlier in cooperation with the customer HŽ Passenger Transport, the second train from this series has now also been presented to the international public. With the global premiere of its latest solution for more modern, more comfortable and more sustainable passenger transport, Končar has once again confirmed that the knowledge, competences and technological solutions developed in Croatia compete on equal terms with the biggest names in the European railway industry.

croatia impresses visitors from around the world

The InnoTrans fair in Berlin once again brought together the world’s leading manufacturers, carriers, operators and experts from the fields of transport technology, railways, public transport and sustainable mobility. Among the most visited parts of the fair was the outdoor exhibition area with 3,500 metres of track, on which 130 exhibitors from 17 countries of the world exhibited a total of 113 vehicles, including the latest generations of trains, locomotives and vehicles with alternative propulsion systems. Precisely in such an international environment Končar is presenting technological solutions developed and produced in Croatia for the jubilee 10th time, confirming its position among the relevant European manufacturers of modern rail vehicles and advanced solutions for sustainable urban mobility.

berlin breaks records

All 42 exhibition halls in the Berlin Messe complex, with a total exhibition area of around 200 thousand square metres, are completely full. After two years ago it was the only one at InnoTrans to present a battery train, which then also became the first such product in commercial use in Europe and one of the first such products in the whole world, Končar has also displayed its new bimodal electro-diesel train at one of the most attractive positions on the outdoor exhibition area of the fair – on 75-metre-long tracks.

At the same time, the latest solutions for railway infrastructure, electrification, urban mobility and traffic digitalisation were presented on the spacious indoor area, further emphasising the ability of the domestic company to independently develop and deliver integrated technological solutions for the transport systems of the future.

“The presentation of our latest bimodal train at InnoTrans is confirmation that Končar today stands side by side with the leading European manufacturers of railway vehicles. It is a product of a new generation that confirms the strength of domestic knowledge, innovation and industrial competences and Končar’s ability to respond to the requirements of modern and sustainable railway transport. We believe that precisely with such projects we contribute to strengthening the competitiveness of the Croatian economy and positioning Croatia among the countries that actively participate in shaping the future of sustainable mobility in Europe,” emphasised Končar Management Board President Gordan Kolak.

One train, two sources of propulsion and no compromises – precisely this idea guided the development of the new Končar bimodal electro-diesel train that combines the advantages of electric and diesel traction and enables uninterrupted traffic on electrified and non-electrified sections of the railway network. Additional operational adaptability is provided by the possibility of controlling up to three coupled units from one driver’s cab, whereby the capacity of the train can be adapted to the actual transport needs. Accordingly, it is an innovation that represents a direct response to the need for more sustainable and more efficient railway transport on long routes that encompass both types of infrastructure, and is the result of many years of experience and independent development at Končar – Electric Vehicles.

With its presentation Končar rounds off a unique development portfolio of trains and, after electric, diesel-electric and battery trains, is introducing the fourth propulsion platform developed and produced in Croatia to the market. The new train is also one of the best references of the long and successful application of Croatian products in domestic railway transport. Namely, the model from the new generation that was put into service last week represents a total of the 70th train that Končar has delivered to HŽ Passenger Transport, which further confirms the joint orientation towards the modernisation of the domestic railway system.

a new era

“The new train for long-distance transport combines the development, design and production competences of the Končar Group. Thanks to the bimodal propulsion system it ensures a high level of reliability and quality of service on the entire network, while bringing passengers a higher standard of comfort through first class, a catering zone and full accessibility for persons with reduced mobility. It is a technologically advanced and operationally flexible solution that meets the requirements of modern railway transport and the long-term needs of sustainable mobility,” emphasised Josip Ninić, President of the Management Board of Končar – Electric Vehicles.

By developing advanced rail vehicles, digital platforms and integrated solutions for critical infrastructure, including railway and transport systems, Končar is increasingly entering a new era of electroenergetics and urban mobility and occupying the position of a serious European partner for the implementation of complex projects. In this way it not only confirms the technological strength of Croatian industry, but also actively contributes to positioning Croatia as a relevant participant in the European green and digital transition and one of the centres of development of the technologically most complex solutions in this part of Europe.

This year InnoTrans is celebrating its 30th anniversary – and, quite fittingly, the fair is recording new record figures. For the first time more than 3,170 exhibitors will participate, which is around 200 more than in 2024, which was also a record year. All 42 exhibition halls in the Berlin Messe complex, with a total exhibition area of around 200 thousand square metres, are completely full. The same applies to the outdoor exhibition area of InnoTrans of 20 thousand square metres, where this year 113 vehicles from 17 countries will be exhibited.

Of the approximately 130 exhibitors presenting themselves on the outdoor area, around 30 of them are participating in that segment for the first time. Therefore the event has great prospects of surpassing the record attendance of around 170 thousand visitors from 2024. That is a huge advance compared to the modest beginnings of what is today the world’s leading railway transport fair.

World.title: Exotic Indian Bananas Successfully Being Grown in Međimurje
World.content:
September the 25th, 2026 – Exotic Indian bananas are successfully being grown in Međimurje, seeing seeds turn into three thousand seedlings.

In the municipality of Štrigova, an area in the north of Međimurje known primarily for its vineyards, one of the largest plantations of Indian bananas in this part of Europe was planted a few years ago. Index reports that behind the project is the family of Ivan Žižek, who decided to grow this unusual fruit after learning that it tolerates low temperatures well and is not attacked by diseases, HRT reports.

3,000 seedlings

The Žižek family planted a plantation of Indian banana, also known as pawpaw (asimina), in the village of Banfi three years ago. Since the seedlings are expensive and they needed more than three thousand of them, they opted for a cheaper but slower route. “We obtained a larger quantity of fruit from Italy, manually extracted the seeds, processed them and put them to germinate. Luckily, everything germinated excellently so we grew the first rootstocks of asimina that way. After that I personally started grafting them,” Ivan explains.

The trees are not yet in full yield so for now the family is selling only fresh fruit. In a year or two they plan to start production of food and cosmetic products from that fruit. “A tree in full yield can give around 20 kilograms. We plan to place 20 to 30 percent on the market through retail chains, and the rest would go into the food industry – for craft breweries, jams, liqueurs and aromatic wines,” says Roman Mraz.

hail reduced the yield

This year’s plantation was also quite damaged by strong hail that hit the area in June. “Still, with some earlier varieties we noticed that the first fruit we tasted was of good quality and tasty inside,” Ivan emphasises.

The Indian banana plantation is not the only example of growing exotic crops in that area. Namely, next to the edge of the plantation of fruit that originates from North America, the Žižek family is also growing 16 pistachio trees, whose original homeland is the Middle East, and 65 feijoa bushes, a fruit species from South America.

World.title: Tartu researchers develop blood test to identify genetic causes of pregnancy loss
World.content:
Researchers at the University of Tartu's Institute of Molecular and Cell Biology are testing a solution that makes it possible to determine the cause of pregnancy loss based on a blood test.

Those involved are hopeful that the method will reach practice already in the coming years.

Approximately two‑thirds of pregnancies that end in the first trimester are caused by chromosomal errors. To determine the exact genetic cause of the loss, medical researchers have until now analyzed removed abortive tissue, that is, the product of conception.

However, this is emotionally and physically exhausting for both the patient and the analyst, expensive, and often technically difficult, because the laboratory sample may contain the woman's own cells, leaving the exact answer unattainable.

According to the study's lead, Professor Ants Kurg, the new method is based on cell‑free fetal DNA that enters the mother's bloodstream during pregnancy. "It is an interesting phenomenon that when a woman is expecting a child, fetal DNA also reaches her bloodstream. There is very little of it, but it can still be analyzed. This has laid the foundation for an entirely new application called non‑invasive prenatal testing," Kurg explained.

The blood test is made difficult by the fact that cell‑free fetal DNA is extremely scarce in the mother's blood, and researchers must find it against the background of the mother's own DNA. The pilot project, which ended in August, demonstrated that the blood‑based method is sufficiently accurate and that the results largely match tissue analyses.

A clear answer brings peace of mind

A precise genetic cause is important for families who have experienced pregnancy loss, primarily to restore peace of mind. "This is always the main question when a pregnancy loss occurs: what did I do wrong and why did this happen to me?" Kurg said.

If the blood test identifies a cytogenetic cause — a random chromosomal error — it relieves parents of unjustified guilt. "For doctors, it is also important that if a cytogenetic cause can be shown, there is a fairly high likelihood that when planning a new child, the next pregnancy will go well. But if no cytogenetic cause is found, additional investigations are needed, and these are much more complex," the professor added.

A three-year research project

To bring the blood‑based analysis into everyday medical practice, researchers together with the University of Tartu Women's Clinic and the health‑technology company Celvia CC are launching a large applied research project supported by Estonian Business and Innovation Agency (EIS).

The three‑year project begins this autumn. "There is a whole series of questions we want to continue working on. For example, how early in pregnancy the analysis can be performed, and how maternal comorbidities and medications affect it. Another separate question is missed miscarriage — within what time frame after a missed miscarriage it is still possible to determine the cause based on cell‑free DNA," Kurg explained.

World.title: Gallery: Lennart Meri's epic 'Silverwhite' journey brought to life
World.content:
50 years after its publication, the Estonian Maritime Museum has brought Lennart Meri's epic "Silverwhite" journey to life with a new exhibition at Tallinn Seaplane Harbor.

First published in occupied Estonia in 1976, "Silverwhite" ("Hõbevalge" in Estonian) weaves together history, research, myths and imagination, becoming a landmark work of Estonian cultural history.

The anniversary exhibition, "Silverwhite 50," takes Meri's journey from the pages of the book into the hangars of Tallinn Seaplane Harbor, tracing the route of ancient Greek explorer Pytheas from the Mediterranean to Saaremaa through sound, space and light.

"We wanted to invite people to read the book again and discover its many layers," said curator Martti Helde.

"Silverwhite 50" unfolds as a journey through a series of spaces, culminating in the story of the Kaali meteorite, which has left a lasting mark on Estonia's cultural history. Like Meri's book, it also explores the mystery surrounding the island of Ultima Thule.

Bespoke experience

At the heart of the exhibition's sound design is NOUS Sonic, an Austrian-developed system being used for the first time in the Baltic and Nordic regions.

Finnish sound artist Janne Laine's soundscapes, heard through headphones, change according to each visitor's movements, pauses and choices.

Lennart Meri and ETV editor Martin Viirand at Meri's Nõmme home in 1976. Source: Jaan Rõõmus/ERR

"Each visitor gets a personal 'Silverwhite' experience," said EMM director Urmas Dresen. "No two sound experiences are exactly the same."

The exhibition also features rare artifacts, items from Meri's family collection and even meteorite fragments.

Helde said it is designed for both readers familiar with the book and those encountering it for the first time, inviting visitors to explore its many layers rather than providing any definitive answers.

"'Silverwhite' is at once an exhibition, an expedition and a state of being," the exhibition team said. "It is an opportunity to step into a world where time moves at a different pace and where each visitor creates their own journey."

Pre-presidential legacy

Lennart Meri was a traveler, published writer, documentary filmmaker and statesman before being elected in 1992 as Estonia's first president following the restoration of its independence the previous year. He was reelected as head of state in 1996, serving two terms over ten years.

Originally published in 1976, "Silverwhite," Meri's best-known work, was published in Finnish in 1983, Italian in 2016, Russian in 2020 and English in 2025.

A new, 50th anniversary edition of the Estonian-language book is set for release, while filming also continues for a feature film adaptation of the same name.

"Silverwhite 50" will remain open to visitors at Tallinn Seaplane Harbor through October 31, 2027.

World.title: Estonian choreographer's ballets to premiere as two-part evening in Tartu
World.content:
Two of Estonian choreographer Jevgeni Grib's ballets will share the stage for the first time Saturday as Vanemuine Theater pairs "Keep a Light in the Window" with "Tango."

Premiering September 26, the new two-part program at Vanemuine's Small House opens with "Keep a Light in the Window," which follows the lives of people in a single tall apartment building through stories of love, loneliness, waiting and farewells.

Originally created as a short-form work, the ballet earned Grib the Estonian Theater Union's 2019 Ballet Award.

"Tango" explores the meeting of a man and woman, their attraction and opposition, using the language and imagery of tango to examine tension and intimacy between two people.

Grib serves as choreographer, set designer and costume designer for both works.

He said "Keep a Light in the Window" draws on childhood memories of walking through the city with his grandmother.

"All four parts of this ballet actually contain a little of my own story and experiences," he noted.

He describes "Tango" as one of his more emotional works, built around passion, mystery, intimacy and visual imagery.

Better together

The two works, which first premiered at the Estonian National Opera in 2018 and 2020, respectively, have never before been performed together in a single evening.

"One is more grounded in life and contemplative, while the other fuels passion and imagination while offering visual pleasure," Grib said.

World.title: Higher‑ranking civil servants set for another pay rise
World.content:
Although Finance Minister Jürgen Ligi criticized the tone with which rescue workers and teachers demand higher pay, the salaries of higher‑ranking state employees rise every year without anyone needing to protest, because their pay increases are indexed.

Ligi said on Thursday in an ERR broadcast regarding teachers' and rescue workers' pay demands that rescue workers' salaries rise more than inflation or roughly at the same rate, and that those who are accommodated should not complain the most. He also noted in the program that the tone in which money is demanded is unpleasant to him.

At the same time, those who decide, among other things, on teachers' and rescue workers' pay have a guaranteed annual pay rise, because the salaries of higher‑ranking civil servants — such as members of parliament, ministers, chancellors and judges — are indexed.

Elo Ellermaa Autor/allikas: Kalle Veesaar

"The exact size of the pay increase for higher civil servants will be determined in March 2027, when it is known what the annual growth of the 2026 consumer price index was and what the annual growth of the social tax pension insurance portion was," explained Elo Ellermaa, head of the Ministry of Finance's communications department.

The value of the salary index consists of 20 percent annual growth in the consumer price index and 80 percent annual growth in the social tax pension insurance portion.

In next year's state budget, which the Ministry of Finance will publish on Monday, the index value is forecast at 1.051.

"This means that salaries indexed with the full index for higher civil servants will rise by 5.1 percent according to the forecast, and salaries indexed with the temporarily reduced index will rise by 2.6 percent," Ellermaa explained.

She noted that because these decisions are tied to the state budget strategy, which has not been finalized, these numbers are not set in stone and may change.

Jürgen Ligi. Source: Priit Mürk/ERR

The full index applies to the salaries of the president, the speaker and deputy speakers of parliament, the chief justice of the Supreme Court, committee chairs and faction chairs in parliament, committee vice‑chairs and faction vice‑chairs, members of parliament, the auditor general, the chancellor of justice, and the chair and members of the Bank of Estonia's supervisory board.

The temporarily reduced index applies until 31 March 2028 to the salaries of the prime minister, ministers, Supreme Court justices, the secretary of state, the prosecutor general, circuit court judges, county and administrative court judges, the national conciliator, and the gender equality and equal treatment commissioner.

This means that when full indexing is restored for all higher civil servants on 1 April 2028, the previous situation will return, bringing them an unusually large pay rise.

"This means that those affected by the reduced indexing will receive a larger one‑time pay increase, and salaries will reach the level they would have been at without the temporary reduction. For example, the prime minister's salary will become equal to that of the president, the speaker of parliament and the chief justice of the Supreme Court," Ellermaa pointed out.

In 2023, ERR reported that due to the temporarily reduced indexing, higher‑ranking state employees would have to settle for pay increases of one to a few hundred euros in the interim years, but in 2028 they can expect a pay rise of €1,000–€2,000.

World.title: NATO deputy supreme commander: If we must attack to defend, that's what we'll do
World.content:
NATO would strike targets on another country's territory if needed to defend its members, NATO's top commander in Europe, Air Chief Marshal Sir Johnny Stringer told Postimees .

In an interview with the paper during the ongoing Estonian Defense Week, Stringer, Deputy Supreme Allied Command Europe (DSACEUR), said although NATO is a defensive alliance, "sometimes to defend, you have to attack."

The commander declined to put any timeline on a possible Russian attack, saying he would not "get drawn into discussions about whether we are talking about months or years."

He did say large-scale attacks would give NATO "indicators and warnings," though smaller operations can be organized more quickly and require constant readiness.

Stringer said NATO has spent several years developing deterrence and defense plans for the Euro-Atlantic area, with close attention paid to defending the three Baltic states.

Asked whether deep strikes against Russia would be needed, he said that if NATO found itself in a military conflict, attacking targets to ensure the security of European countries "is what we would do."

He said the course of what Russia called a three-day special operation, now in its fourth and a half year, "has not gone very well for Mr Putin."

On hybrid threats below the Article 5 collective defense threshold, the commander said NATO's military response is only one part of a wider collective response, with member states able to impose sanctions and expel diplomats.

Stringer said he was NATO's air and missile defense commander when the alliance shot down its first drones over Poland last September, and that rules of engagement and authorization are clearly defined.

Stringer noted NATO has since developed its approach further in response to a changed threat, adding: "You will see a new approach, although I cannot go into the details of it."

World.title: Government sets 2032 target for Rail Baltica's Tallinn–Pärnu section
World.content:
Although the completion of Rail Baltica is being postponed, work continues on the sections already started. The Tallinn–Pärnu section should be completed in 2032.

Martin‑Erich Torjus, adviser at the Ministry of Climate's communications department, confirmed that construction work already begun in Estonia will continue as planned.

"Construction is underway at the Ülemiste passenger terminal and on the Tallinn–Pärnu route over more than 100 kilometres. Planning of construction activity also continues along the rest of the route," he said.

Torjus noted that when starting new construction phases, the construction pace will be set in such a way that it allows avoiding overheating of the construction market, taking into account the progress of construction in neighbouring countries and, among other things, considering funding opportunities in the next European Union budget period.

According to Estonia's domestic plan, the Tallinn–Pärnu section will be completed no later than 2032, the Soodevahe–Muuga section in the north no later than 2033, and the Pärnu–Ikla section in the south no later than 2034.

Prime Minister Kristen Michal said that the works fall within the European Union's next budget period, 2028–2034. At the same time, he stressed that it is important that the Latvians also take on the obligation to finish their part by 2034.

Prime Minister Kristen Michal. Source: Priit Mürk/ERR

Lower costs

According to Michal, postponing the works will result in lower costs.

"Put very simply: if we had done it faster, we would have had to borrow more money, the market would have been hotter and prices higher. By proceeding gradually, we can likely build more cheaply and, thanks to this budget period, use approximately €660 million more EU funding than we would have received if we had rushed," Michal said.

On Tuesday, the prime ministers of Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania confirmed in a joint statement that instead of the previously agreed 2030, the route crossing the three Baltic states will be completed in 2034.

Secretary of State Keit Kasemets wrote on social media on Thursday that the government did not cut Rail Baltica funding in the 2027 budget and in the 2027–2030 budget strategy.

"All funds previously foreseen in the budget are also in the budget now. Next year's funding is the largest ever — €541 million (1.15 percent of GDP). This is €32 million more than this year. In the following years, approximately 1 percent of GDP will be invested annually in Rail Baltica construction until 2030," he added.

The 2030 pace would have meant additional investments of 1 percent of GDP in both 2027 and 2028, Kasemets said. For the construction sector this would have meant very large volumes in a short time and then a rapid decline.

Kasemets added that he believes that in 2032 the train will depart from Ülemiste terminal to Pärnu, and in 2034 to Kaunas and from there onward to Warsaw.

According to initial plans, Rail Baltica was supposed to be completed in full by 2026.

Minister of Infrastructure Kuldar Leis said that the total funding requested from Europe by the Baltic states is €10 billion. Funding applications to the European Commission will only be made for the next budget period.

The first train at Tallinn's new Ülemiste Linda Terminal. June 12, 2025. Source: Siim Lõvi/ERR

Construction timeline changes

Clarifying the completion stages now also changes the construction timelines somewhat.

Anvar Salomets, CEO of Rail Baltic Estonia, said that the intensity of ongoing work will not change, and regarding upcoming procurements they will be wiser once the precise construction schedule based on the submitted funding proposal has been completed. "It can be assumed that certain works on the priority section Tallinn–Pärnu will receive longer deadlines in upcoming procurements," he noted.

Salomets added that between Tallinn and Pärnu there is more than one hundred kilometres of active construction area and resources are loaded to the maximum. The new schedule therefore also slows down the current hyper-fast construction pace, he noted.

Additional EU financing for Rail Baltica not clear

The Estonian government's claims that postponing Rail Baltica's completion deadline will bring hundreds of millions of euros in additional funding from the European Union budget are not certain, because the new seven‑year budget (MFF) itself and the rules for using it have not yet been agreed upon.

"Funding for Rail Baltica's construction has mainly come from the Connecting Europe Facility (CEF), and it is a fund — unlike structural funds and other funds that Estonia has used, for example, to finance regional development — from which you are not given money for a project in advance. In other words, it is actually impossible to say beforehand how much money one project or another will receive from this specific fund," said Ave Schank‑Lukas, head of the European Commission Representation in Estonia.

Schank‑Lukas said that in the European Commission's proposed budget for the new period, CEF is indeed allocated twice as much money as in the current MFF — €51.5 billion — but its distribution will still take place on a project basis according to specific criteria and in competition with other applicants.

"It must be said that Rail Baltica has been one of the biggest beneficiaries from there (from CEF — ed.) and the project has actually progressed a great deal in recent years, which is why it has received money from the Connecting Europe Facility," she noted.

Rail Baltica is also included in the next budget framework, Schank‑Lukas added.

"But the conditions have not been agreed upon yet. It is not possible to state with full certainty how much money Rail Baltica will receive from there in the next budget period," she said.

This article was updated on 26 September with Ave Schank‑Lukas's comments regarding Rail Baltica funding.

World.title: Varja wind farm scaled back by one‑third in revised plan
World.content:
In Ida‑Virumaa's Lüganuse municipality, the planning of the first part of the Varja wind farm is nearing completion, and construction of 12 turbines should begin next year. Compared with the original plan, the park has become one‑third smaller.

The Varja wind farm consists of four parts. The eastern and western sections have progressed the furthest, and a total of 12 turbines should rise there next year.

When the current state of the wind‑farm development was introduced to local residents, the main concern of those who attended was the impact of the turbines on the living environment. There is fear that if all wind farms planned in the municipality are built, those who can will move elsewhere. This despite the planned compensation measures.

"Young people who have built a home here and had children will move away, they will simply leave, there is nothing to be done," said local resident Jane Varimaa.

At present, Lüganuse municipality has 27 turbines. Various developments foresee the construction of another 150 turbines, but municipal leaders are certain that so many will not be built. The Varja wind farm has also become one‑third smaller during the five‑year administrative process. The turbines will be lower than planned.

Gregor Raudvere, member of the management board of Varja Windfarm, said that initially the plan was to build 32 to 34 turbines. By now, the number has reached 23. "The fact is that across the country all developers start planning with maximum possibility, and afterwards it becomes clear which positions are specifically feasible," he said.

According to Raudvere, this may indeed cause confusion among people. "Certainly, in such volumes, not all of the turbines planned will be built in local municipalities," he added.

Lüganuse municipality has given wind‑project initiators the directive that they must reach agreement with residents who fall within the disturbance area.

Chairman of Lüganuse municipal council Mart Kivistik noted that the municipality has clearly sent a message to all developers that the municipality will not act against people's property. "We will not establish any planning before all people's consents have been obtained, regardless of what the matter concerns — whether line corridors or turbine‑blade height," he said.

According to the Varja wind‑farm developer, at least 90 million euros will be invested in the completion of the first dozen turbines. They will produce about 250 gigawatt‑hours of electricity per year.

World.title: Farmers use 'empty planting' schemes to obtain subsidies
World.content:
In Estonia, vegetable cultivation has multiplied several times in just a couple of years, but some farmers sow crops only to receive subsidies and have no intention of harvesting them. Such scheming, however, leaves real farmers in trouble.

Store shelves should be full of turnips — agricultural stats show Estonia is growing nearly seven times more than a few years ago, yet in reality not a single turnip reaches the market.

In addition to turnips, pumpkin cultivation has also multiplied. In 2024, pumpkins were grown on 50 hectares, but this year subsidies were requested for 224 hectares. Red beet was grown on 65 hectares a couple of years ago, but this year nearly 594.

These numbers are driven by clever scheming, said Estonian Gardening Association's CEO Raimond Strastin.

"Cheap seed is bought with the aim of defrauding the state for subsidies, sown with a grain drill without any plan to obtain or harvest a crop," Strastin said.

During summer, these fields are not maintained, and in autumn the crop is simply plowed back into the soil — but vegetable‑growing subsidies are still requested. Since vegetable cultivation had been declining for years, additional subsidies have recently been paid for root‑crop growing. Such subsidy fraud angers the few farmers whose actual root crops do reach stores.

"This is direct theft from real producers, because vegetable‑production subsidies are meant to compensate for this hard work and to provide valuable goods for people's tables — goods that in Estonia are produced at roughly half of what is needed," said Mart Timmi, a farmer at Jaagomäe farm.

In earlier years, Jaagomäe farm received nearly 400 euros per hectare in subsidies, but this year the amount is 160 euros due to schemers, since the total subsidy pool has not increased. The Ministry of Agriculture became aware of the manipulation late last year, and therefore this year ten times more vegetable‑subsidy applicants have been inspected than before.

"There are two types of violations. In one case, the declared crop is simply not found in the field — and applications are submitted in spring. In the other case, the crop does not grow according to local agrotechnical norms. This means it is too weedy or is grown in a way that is not typical for that specific crop," said Katrin Rannik, head of the agricultural environment department at the Ministry of Agriculture.

Rannik admits that tighter inspections likely are not enough, and they are also quite costly. Therefore, other solutions are being considered.

"A more radical example is that turnip as a crop likely will no longer be eligible for vegetable subsidies. Carrot and pumpkin will certainly remain, because at least we have seen those on store shelves," Rannik said.

World.title: Basra tribesmen liberate hijacked oil tanker in Gulf of Aden
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – A tribal dignitary from Basra Governorate revealed on Friday, September 25, 2026, that approximately 40 members of the Al-Shaghanba tribe from the Abu Al-Khaseeb district successfully liberated a hijacked crude oil tanker in the Gulf of Aden, freeing the crew and capturing seven armed pirates.

Sheikh Ali Al-Shaghanbi stated that the commercial vessel, owned by an Iraqi businessman belonging to the Al-Shaghanba tribe, was intercepted and boarded by maritime pirates while transiting strategic maritime lanes off the southern Arabian Peninsula.

According to the tribal leader, the pirates seized control of the tanker, took the crew hostage, and issued ransom demands as a condition for their release.

In response, an expeditionary group of roughly 40 armed tribesmen from Abu Al-Khaseeb and the village of Jaykoor mobilized to mount a direct recovery operation, coordinating logistics and tracking through international contacts positioned outside Iraq.

The intervention concluded with the tribal forces successfully storming the vessel, regaining full command of the tanker, and securing the safe release of all detained crew members unharmed.

Sheikh Al-Shaghanbi confirmed that the clash resulted in the capture and detention of seven armed pirates found aboard the vessel, while remaining members of the pirate group managed to flee the maritime perimeter.

World.title: Al Zaidi courts US banks in New York targeting 10M bpd oil capacity
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Under the auspices and in the presence of Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi, the Permanent Mission of the Republic of Iraq to the United Nations in New York hosted a high-level roundtable meeting bringing together representatives from premier American commercial banks and financial institutions, Iraqi banking delegates, senior government officials, and economic analysts.

Held late Thursday evening Baghdad time on September 24, 2026, the diplomatic engagement was convened to re-establish institutional communication between Iraq’s financial sector and the international banking architecture, with a particular focus on direct correspondent relationships with major U.S. lenders.

In his address to the executive gathering, Prime Minister Al-Zaidi stressed that Iraq has embarked on an irreversible trajectory of structural economic transformation and banking sector modernization. He acknowledged that past vulnerabilities within Iraq’s domestic banking ecosystem were partly rooted in institutional isolation and restricted interaction with global financial hubs, particularly American banking conglomerates.

Al-Zaidi extended an open invitation to U.S. financial institutions to establish direct operational footprints in the Iraqi market, emphasizing that their market entry would represent a qualitative leap toward elevating local banking practices, adopting international compliance standards, and deepening Iraq’s integration into global capital networks.

Highlighting Iraq’s macroeconomic foundations, the Prime Minister noted that the country currently produces approximately 4.5 million barrels of crude oil per day, with federal energy policies actively targeting an expansion toward 10 million barrels per day over the long term.

This hydrocarbon expansion strategy is designed to maximize sovereign revenues and channel critical liquidity into national development, industrial manufacturing, and cross-sector economic diversification. Al-Zaidi assured participants that the government is actively engineering an investor-friendly environment with streamlined regulatory, customs, and fiscal frameworks, underscoring that American banks hold vast opportunities to structure project financing, issue commercial credit, and underwrite major capital ventures across energy, logistics, and real estate.

Detailing administrative reforms underway, Al-Zaidi outlined the government’s clear operational blueprint for comprehensive institutional restructuring across state-owned commercial banks. The initiative aims to enforce corporate governance benchmarks, upgrade anti-money laundering and know-your-customer compliance mechanisms, and build an agile banking framework capable of supporting modern commercial activities.

The Prime Minister affirmed that statutory anti-corruption proceedings, asset recovery drives, and fiscal protection measures are advancing effectively, reiterating Baghdad’s commitment to institutional transparency and the safeguarding of public and private investment funds.

World.title: Iraq and US sign accord handing over diplomatic center at Baghdad Airport
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Government and the United States signed a formal agreement on Thursday, September 24, 2026, transferring full control of the Baghdad Diplomatic Support Center (BDSC) at Baghdad International Airport to the Iraqi side, marking a significant step in the systematic restructuring of bilateral ties between both nations.

The signing ceremony, hosted at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs headquarters in Baghdad, brought together Iraq’s Undersecretary for Bilateral Relations, Muhammad Hussein Bahr Al-Uloom, and the Chargé d’Affaires ad interim at the U.S. Embassy in Baghdad, Steven Fagin.

The foreign ministry stated that the handover forms an integral milestone in federal efforts to fulfill the technical and sovereign prerequisites for concluding the mission of the U.S.-led International Coalition and drawing down foreign military presence across Iraq, aligned with the established September 30, 2026, deadline.

By transferring authority over the high-profile logistical installation at the capital’s international gateway, the sovereign transition moves forward on schedule toward the formal cessation of coalition combat missions.

Undersecretary Bahr Al-Uloom emphasized the strategic weight of the agreement, framing the handover as an operational pivot toward an expanded bilateral era centered on mutual economic partnerships, energy infrastructure modernization, and broad-based development projects.

In response, Fagin reaffirmed Washington’s support for advancing bilateral collaboration within agreed strategic frameworks that uphold mutual sovereignty, with both diplomatic delegations concluding the ceremony by noting that the handover establishes practical foundations for deeper institutional cooperation and coordinated regional security frameworks.

World.title: Iraq targets first Gulf Cup win against Kuwait
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq will take on Kuwait on Saturday, looking for their first victory in the 27th Arabian Gulf Cup, after drawing 1-1 with Oman in Jeddah.

The Group A match will take place at Prince Abdullah Al Faisal Stadium in Baghdad at 6:55 p.m. local time, with Iraq starting the second round with one point and Kuwait aiming to rebound from a 1-0 loss to Saudi Arabia.

Iraq started quickly against Oman on Wednesday, with Mohammed Qasim scoring in the sixth minute with a strong left-footed finish.

Oman answered in the second half with Nasser Al-Rawahi, who equalized in the 67th minute to give both sides a draw.

News from Iraq’s Coach Graham Arnold said that preparations for the first match had been restricted, with his group having little time together before playing an Oman team that had been in camp for many days.

Arnold mentioned that Iraq’s players are physically, tactically, and emotionally ready for Kuwait. Arnold may make changes to his team for the match against Kuwait due to exhaustion and the hot weather in Saudi Arabia.

Half of Iraq’s Gulf Cup roster had competed in the 2026 World Cup, with the remaining being younger players given a chance with the national team.

Arnold said that Mustafa Saadoun and Mohammed Qasim are available for the match, while defender Akam Hashim’s fitness is being examined.

Saturday’s encounter is crucial after Iraq’s two-point loss to Oman. Saudi Arabia leads Group A with three points, Iraq and Oman have one apiece, while Kuwait has no points after the first round.

The top two teams advanced to the semifinals.

Iraq’s last group encounter is against Saudi Arabia on September 29, making it crucial to win against Kuwait before facing the current group leaders.

World.title: Iraqi PM calls on US firms to seize investment opportunities
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi called on US companies on Wednesday to seize investment opportunities available in Iraq, particularly in the petrochemicals, glass, and phosphate industries, as well as the gas and clean energy sectors.

Al-Zaidi’s remarks took place during his meeting in New York with a delegation from the US Chamber of Commerce, according to the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The prime minister stated that Iraq has considerable natural resources, human resources, and a key geographical position, all of which serve as necessary foundations for successful partnerships. He explained that the government is seeking to use these resources to promote economic development and increase investment possibilities.

Al-Zaidi emphasized the government’s commitment to providing support for businesses and investors, such as granting ownership of land for investment projects in accordance with Iraqi laws, as well as access to tax and customs exemptions for up to ten years.

Iraq is working on infrastructure and transportation projects, notably the strategic project of the Development Road, which will improve Iraq’s position as a corridor connecting the East and West, according to al-Zaidi.

The prime minister affirmed that the government looks forward to establishing factories and setting up projects to diversify the economy and create job opportunities.

Al-Zaidi also asked members of the US Chamber of Commerce and specialized firms to attend the Baghdad Energy Conference and capitalize on the prospects offered in the country. He added that Iraq aspires to establish economic partnerships based on collaboration, mutual interest, and long-term investment.

World.title: Iraqi PM, US president discuss partnerships, regional stability
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi met with US President Donald Trump in New York on Tuesday on the sideline of his participation in the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly.

The two leaders discussed bilateral relations and approaches to strengthen cooperation and partnership between the two countries across political, economic, and investment sectors, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The two sides also reviewed the latest developments in the region, as well as the joint efforts undertaken by Iraq and the United States to enhance regional and international security and stability.

The discussion takes place ahead of a crucial September 30 milestone, which marks a shift in Washington-Baghdad ties toward long-term economic collaboration as the US prepares to end its coalition military mission in Iraq.

Amid continuing negotiations between Iraq and US officials, including a recent meeting between al-Zaidi and US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Washington pressured Baghdad on its obligations to place weapons possessed by armed factions under state supervision.

In addition to their exclusive bilateral discussion, al-Zaidi attended President Trump’s larger gathering that included leaders from important regional powers, including Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Jordan, Egypt, and the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) nations.

The larger gathering addressed strategies to coordinate post-war arrangements, protect global commerce supply lines, and develop diplomatic frameworks for Middle Eastern stability.

World.title: Iraqi PM meets Iranian president in New York
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi met on Wednesday with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian in New York on the sidelines of their participation in the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly.

According to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), the meeting addressed developments in the region and the necessity of working together to handle difficulties in ways that promote security and stability.

The two leaders also addressed approaches to keep the region from spiraling into a cycle of escalation, tensions, and crises.

During a meeting on Wednesday with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein emphasized the importance of defusing regional tensions through dialogue.

The meeting addressed bilateral relations and regional developments, as well as the importance of continued coordination between the two countries to respond to current challenges and support diplomatic efforts aimed at enhancing regional stability.

Hussein also stressed the significance of continued diplomatic efforts among the parties involved to defuse tension and prevent escalation.

Araghchi outlined the discussions that began between Iran and the United States, sponsored by an intermediary, on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly meetings in New York. These discussions attempt to de-escalate the situation and find approaches to reopen the Strait of Hormuz for navigation.

The two ministers also discussed the outcomes of the meeting involving the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states, Iraq, Jordan, Syria, Lebanon, Egypt, and Turkey—attended by US President Donald Trump—as well as how regional and international relationships might help efforts for de-escalation.

World.title: Iraq’s Gulf Cup 27 match against Oman ends in 1-1 draw
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi and Omani national teams drew 1-1 on Wednesday in the opening match of the 27th Gulf Cup held at Prince Abdullah Al-Faisal Sports City Stadium in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

Iraq launched a strong attack, causing Oman to make a defensive mistake. Zaid Ismail took advantage of the rebound and set it up for Mohammed Qasim, who fired a rocket shot with his left foot into the near corner, giving the “Lions of Mesopotamia” an early lead in the sixth minute.

The Omani team’s performance improved, and their level rose during the second half. After a decisive and skillful pass from Ahmed al-Kaabi, Nasser al-Rawahi scored the equalizer brilliantly from a close range, winning the “Man of the Match” award in recognition of his outstanding performance.

In a candid evaluation, Australian coach Graham Arnold, who manages the Iraqi national team, acknowledged that the team’s performance fell short of expectations. He pointed out that the rushed preparations had hindered the implementation of their tactical plan.

The Iraqi team only had one training session before the tournament compared to six for the Omani team.

“We were not the better side, and we must work harder in the coming matches to secure the win,” Arnold said.

The manager of the Oman team, Tarik Sektioui, expressed his great pride in his team, describing the squad as “fighters” for their ability to recover from an early setback and snatch a vital opening point against the defending champions.

World.title: 19 dead after consuming suspected spurious alcohol in Nagaland; SIT formed
World.content:
Samples have been sent to Guwahati for forensic examination

NEW DELHI: At least 19 people have died in Nagaland after allegedly consuming spurious liquor, prompting police to launch an investigation into the suspected supply of adulterated alcohol in the state, where prohibition has been in force since 1990.Police said eight deaths were reported in Mokokchung district and 11 in Tuensang over the past two days. An SIT headed by Additional Superintendent of Police I Bunglang Chang has been formed to investigate the deaths and trace the source and supply chain of the suspected illicit liquor, Senior Superintendent of Police Vesupra Kezo said on Saturday.Samples have been sent to Guwahati for forensic examination to determine the cause of the deaths. Police have also conducted several raids, arrested 19 people and seized nearly 3,000 bottles of liquor.Authorities urged people to avoid unidentified or unlabelled alcohol and seek immediate medical attention if they experience dizziness, blurred vision, breathing difficulties or loss of consciousness after drinking.

World.title: Watch: Indian diplomat's reaction to Pak PM Shehbaz Sharif's UN speech goes viral
World.content:
Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's address at the United Nations General Assembly, in which he sought to reiterate Islamabad's false narrative on the 2025 conflict with India, drew a viral reaction from an Indian diplomat.

The cameras captured Indian diplomat R Srinivas appearing to smirk and laugh as Sharif spoke about Pakistanâs claimed âvictoryâ in the May 2025 conflict with India.

The moment came as Sharif presented Islamabadâs version of the conflict and raised several issues concerning India, including the

and Kashmir.

Addressing the UN, Sharif praised US President Donald Trump for his role in preventing further escalation between the two nuclear-armed neighbours during

.

âHis timely intervention came at a decisive juncture when two nuclear-armed neighbours stood at the brink of an all-out war. And, who knows, Mr President, the extent of devastation that could have taken place had President Trump not stepped in at this critical moment with clarity of thought and action,â Sharif said.

âMr President, we must therefore ensure that South Asia never reaches that precipice ever again,â he added.





India, however, has consistently maintained that the cessation of military action on May 10, 2025, was reached through direct communication between India and Pakistan and did not involve third-party mediation.

Pakistanâs Director General of Military Operations (DGMO) had approached his Indian counterpart on May 10, seeking a cessation of military action.

India had launched Operation Sindoor on May 7, 2025, following the April 22 Pahalgam terror attack that killed 26 people.

India said the operation targeted terrorist infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir.

India also exercised its right of reply to Sharifâs remarks. Petal Gahlot, First Secretary in Indiaâs Permanent Mission to the UN, criticised Pakistanâs political system and its references to democratic rights and human values. She also referred to Osama bin Ladenâs presence near Pakistanâs military academy.

âThis afternoon, the General Assembly heard some bizarre remarks from the representative of Pakistan. This happens just a fortnight after New York City and the world marked the 25th anniversary of the horrendous 9-11 terrorist attack. This context is important to keep in mind because its mastermind, Osama bin Laden, was living right on the doorstep of the Pakistani Army's premier academy. This was the very entity which was the subject of such deep genuflection before us today by the representative of Pakistan.

But all this is only to be expected from what Pakistanis themselves call a Form 47 government.â

Gahlot also responded to Pakistanâs references to democratic rights and the role of the military in the country. âWe heard some hypocritical homilies about democratic rights and human values from a regime whose capital at this very moment is being fortified against its own people. And that, Mr. President, is happening because this is a regime of the army, by the army, and for the army.

Their puppets may come and go, but let us have no illusion about who calls the shots.

The reality of Pakistan is expressed in its 27th Amendment and the lifelong immunity granted to its real ruler," she added.

Sharif also criticised Indiaâs decision to place the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance, arguing that the âmove was not legalâ and highlighting the importance of the Indus river system to Pakistan.

India placed the treaty in abeyance following the Pahalgam terror attack and has said the decision will remain in effect until Pakistan takes credible and irreversible action against cross-border terrorism.

The 1960 Indus Waters Treaty governs the sharing of the waters of the Indus river system between India and Pakistan.

World.title: CCPA penalises Amazon, Flipkart, JioMart for selling unregistered herbicide
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has imposed penalties of Rs 10 lakh each on Amazon and Flipkart, and Rs 5 lakh on JioMart, for selling and advertising an unregistered agrochemical product, Cyclosinone Herbicide.

Cyclosinone Herbicide is marketed as a granular weed-control product used to prevent and eliminate broadleaf and grassy weeds in lawns, gardens and agricultural fields.

In separate orders issued recently, the consumer watchdog directed the e-commerce marketplaces to immediately discontinue the false and misleading s and conduct a self-audit of their platforms to identify and remove products that violate the law or pose a risk to consumersâ life and safety.

The CCPA initiated proceedings after the department of agriculture and farmersâ welfare forwarded a complaint it had received from the Crop Care Federation of India (CCFI) regarding the sale and  of the unregistered herbicide through e-commerce and digital media platforms.

During the investigation, the agriculture department informed CCPA that the import, manufacture, sale, transport, distribution and use of insecticides and pesticides are regulated under the Insecticides Act, 1968, and the Insecticides Rules to safeguard human beings and animals from potential risks.





The department told the authority that no chemical named Cyclosinone is included in the Schedule to the Insecticides Act. However, a product marketed as âCyclosinone Herbicideâ was being sold through online platforms without disclosing the chemical name of its active ingredient or its composition.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

âIt is currently being marketed illegally because it bypasses the mandatory safety, bio-efficacy, quality and legal checks required under the Insecticides Act,â the department said in its submission to CCPA.

The authority rejected the e-commerce companiesâ argument that they could not be held responsible for products listed by third-party sellers. The CCPA said online marketplaces cannot disown their statutory obligation to protect consumers and are required to exercise due diligence to prevent the sale of products that are illegal or hazardous.

World.title: 'No hard feelings': US on India's stern warning over Russia Sanctions Act
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The United States on Saturday said that it was looking to meet India's massive energy needs, days after US President Donald Trump signed the 'Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026', which authorises him to impose tariffs of up to 100 per cent on countries buying Russian oil and gas.

"We are looking to also become a huge source of India's energy needs. We're increasing our hydrocarbon exports,â a senior US state department official told news agency PTI.

âThe demands are great, and the needs for oil are there. We are looking for alternatives. But I would say before even the war, India had been looking to diversify when it came to energy for a long time. It's not a new concept. We just need to expedite it faster,â he added.

The US official also played down New Delhi's warning over the contentious law and said that India's response was expected after the US Congress took a pretty hard approach, especially publicly.

âIndia has been looking for a long time to diversify its energy sources. They're a country that has massive energy needs,â the official told PTI.

âYou had members of Congress calling out India in particular, so of course India has to respond.





We understand that. They have a domestic constituency, as do we. Like, there are no sort of hard feelings on any of that kind of activity," he added.

Last week, the ministry of external affairs warned the US of the legislationâs potential impact on the US-India relationship.

The official said that the new act gave President Trump a new tool in his toolbox.

âThat doesn't necessarily mean he deploys it tomorrow, but he has the opportunity to. His focus is on ending this war. It's been something he campaigned on and something he's been dedicated to from the beginning,â he said.

âWe're looking for our friends, especially like India, to help support that effort. But I think you'll have to stay tuned on how the bill gets implemented. But there is a broad national security waiver, so you can imagine also the president, there's a scenario, the president uses that as well,â he added.

"Now, with President Trump's incredibly successful operation in Venezuela, we are moving into a better position that countries like India are going to be able to get access to that market,â he added.

World.title: 'Time for bhajan clubbing but not for serious questions': Congress takes swipe at PM Modi
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Karnataka home minister Congress leader Priyank Kharge on Saturday took a swipe at

after he shared a video of himself attending a âBhajan Clubbingâ event in Delhi, questioning his response to issues concerning the Election Commission.

âPM @narendramodi has time for âBhajan Clubbingâ, but no time to answer serious questions about the clubbing of democracy through the Election Commission. For 13 years, there has been a familiar pattern: when difficult questions confront the government, the Prime Minister is conspicuously absent from answering them. Celebrations get his presence. Accountability gets his silence,â Kharge said in a post on X, quoting the video shared by PM Modi.

PM Modi on Friday evening attended a âbhajan clubbingâ event at a park named after BJP ideologue Deen Dayal Upadhyay, as part of tributes marking his 116th birth anniversary.

The remarks came as the Congress intensified protests against the Election Commission across the country, with party workers demanding Chief Election Commissioner Kumarâs resignation over the poll bodyâs functioning and the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.





In Delhi, the Indian Youth Congress marched from Raisina Road to Jantar Mantar, raising slogans against the CEC and calling for his resignation.

The protests were also held in several states. In Patna, police used water cannons to disperse Congress workers demonstrating against Kumar. Similar scenes were reported in Chandigarh, where police used water cannons against protesting Congress workers, some of whom climbed onto police vans.

Congress workers also held demonstrations in Jammu and Kashmir, Assam, Uttarakhand, West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh and Manipur.

The political confrontation has intensified following an Indian Express report that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections at least 14 times over 10 months to decisions and procedures concerning electoral rolls and access to election databases.

World.title: Bangladesh, U.S. sign MoU on strategic civil nuclear cooperation
World.content:
Bangladesh and the United States have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) on strategic civil nuclear cooperation, to deepen cooperation on the peaceful use of nuclear energy. MoU was signed in New York on Friday (September 25, 2026) by Rehan Asad, Adviser for Science and Technology to the Bangladesh Prime Minister, and Jacob Helberg, U.S. Under Secretary of State for Economic Growth, Energy and the Environment, according to the media cell of Bangladesh’s ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP).

The agreement comes as Bangladesh seeks to expand and diversify its long-term energy sources. The country is developing its first nuclear power plant, at Rooppur, and has been pursuing international cooperation in nuclear science and technology.

Under the MoU, the two sides recognised the strategic significance of their diplomatic relationship and its regional and international security implications, including energy security. They also noted the role nuclear energy can play in meeting the energy requirements of both countries, according to local media reports.

The MoU records the shared position that all civil nuclear cooperation should follow the highest standards of nuclear safety, security, safeguards and non-proliferation, according to the newspaper The Daily Star.

It also noted that both Bangladesh and the U.S. have International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) safeguards agreements and Additional Protocols in force. Both countries are parties to the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons.

Bangladesh and the U.S. had also signed an MoU on strategic cooperation in the broader energy sector in May 2026, aimed at strengthening Bangladesh’s long-term energy security through diversified energy sourcing. The latest MoU specifically focuses on civil nuclear cooperation and the peaceful use of nuclear energy.

World.title: Police gag media from asking questions to CM Satheesan in Kochi, ACP cites security aspect
World.content:
The Kochi city police on Saturday (September 26, 2026) allegedly prevented journalists from asking questions to Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan. The alleged incident happened when TV journalists were waiting for the Chief Minister’s arrival at an event at a convention centre in Kaloor.

Peter K.J., Assistant Commissioner, Ernakulam subdivision, prevented the journalists from getting near the Chief Minister, citing security reasons.

In a video aired on TV channels, the officer is heard saying that the Chief Minister is someone in the Z Plus security category. He did not give a clear answer to repeated queries from reporters on whether he had received any instruction to prevent journalists from asking questions to the Chief Minister.

“I spoke only from a security aspect. I didn’t get angry at you,” Mr. Peter is heard saying in the video.

The incident comes a day after Mr. Satheesan reportedly lost his cool at journalists who sought answers from him about allegations that he received money from former Cochin Minerals and Rutile Limited (CMRL) Managing Director S. Sasidharan Kartha and the controversy over his recent chartered flight to flood-hit Malappuram on a flight lent by a benefactor whose details the chief minister has preferred to withhold.

While coming out of an official meeting at Thodupuzha on Friday (September 24, 2026), the chief minister declined to respond to the media and told the reporters, “Move aside… I am not meeting you.” He also alleged that the reporters were causing inconvenience to the public who had come to hand over petitions to him.
